poem:
Echoes of the Unseen

The quiet ache of sunrise, 
The hollow whisper of night
The Mother
Who cradles shadows in her sigh, 

The Sculptor
Who chisels memories from mist, 

The Wanderer
Who walks the corridors of loss, 

Tears that linger on the tongue, 
Heartbeats that falter in the still, 

A candle flickers, then sighs, 
Its flame a fragile prayer to the void, 

The wind carries fragments of laughter, 
Scattered like leaves on an endless road, 

To honor the absent, we gather silence, 
To love the gone, we hold the echo, 

And in the space between breaths, 
Grief becomes the bridge to tomorrow.

The Willow’s Whisper

I stand like a willow in a cracked concrete yard, 
Roots tangled in old brick, stubborn against the grind. 
Rain drums on my bark, each drop a tiny drumbeat, 
Yet I bend, not break, when the wind tries to pry.

My leaves are thin pages of a story unfinished, 
Pages that have been torn, re‑stitched, and read again. 
When the storm strips them bare, I let the naked branches 
Reach for the sky, daring the clouds to paint me anew.

The city hums horns, sirens, hurried footsteps
A chorus that could drown a softer heart. 
But I listen to the quiet thrum beneath the noise, 
A pulse that says: keep growing, even in shadows.

Season after season, I shed what I cannot keep, 
Winter strips me to a skeletal grin, 
Spring returns with a shy green, a whispered promise, 
Summer crowns me with a canopy of sighs.

People pass, eyes flicker, some see only a weed, 
Others pause, feel the cool shade, and rest a breath. 
I am the patient survivor, the quiet stubbornness, 
A reminder that resilience is not loud it is simply being.

So when the world feels heavy, think of my thin limbs, 
How they sway, how they survive, how they keep reaching, 
And know that within every cracked pavement, a root can find 
The strength to rise, to whisper, to endure.

Whispers of the Wild

I walk where the pine needles carpet the earth, 
where the wind sketches stories on the bark of old oaks, 
and the sky hangs low enough to taste the amber light. 

There is a quiet pulse beneath the creek’s soft chatter, 
a rhythm that matches the steady beat of my own heart, 
as if the water knows the places I keep hidden. 

I do not ask the mountains to move, nor the clouds to stay, 
I only listen for the sighs that rise with each sunrise, 
for the gentle reminder that I am still a part of this place. 

The meadow hums with insects that have no names, 
yet their chorus fills the air like a secret hymn, 
and I find myself humming back, a fragile echo. 

When the rain taps against the windowpane, 
I feel the world exhale, letting go of dust and doubt, 
and in that moment, the scent of wet soil becomes prayer. 

I am not searching for answers in the rustle of leaves, 
just a simple gratitude for the way the light filters through, 
for the way a single feather drifts and lands without haste. 

So I stand here, barefoot on the damp grass, 
letting the earth’s coolness seep into my skin, 
and I understand that the wild does not need to be tamed
it only needs to be felt, one breath at a time.

Echoes from the Playground

I sit on the curb of my old street, 
the chalk dust still clinging to the cracks. 
A swing set rusts where we once beat 
the summer heat with laughter attacks. 

The orange bike I rode at ten 
now leans against a garden wall, 
its chain a silent, tired friend, 
still humming the song of a fall. 

I hear the distant squeak of sneakers, 
the thud of a ball against the fence, 
the way our secret code felt like seekers, 
spelling “forever” in present tense. 

A paper plane glides through the wind, 
its edge a memory, sharp and bright. 
We launched it high, believing we’d never end, 
until the sky turned pink at night. 

The ice‑cream truck’s jingle drifts, 
a low‑key hymn to sticky hands. 
I taste the vanilla that still lifts, 
the sugar that slipped through childhood’s sands. 

Now I pull the rope of yesterday, 
feel the tug of a time that won’t stay, 
and smile at the ghost of my younger self, 
who still rides the bike and keeps the shelf. 

The world moves on, the streets get new, 
but the echo of those playground shoes 
reminds me that nostalgia’s not a trap
it’s a warm pocket where the past still naps.

The Arithmetic of Absence 

A chair holds the shape of an absence. 
The wind forgets the name of your laughter, 
how it once curled around your ribs 
like a serpent of light. 

Days stack like unsent letters. 
I fold your socks, find a hole 
where your thumb used to rub the cotton thin. 
The clock’s hands are strangers now, 
tracing circles without you in the inkwell. 

The sea combs its fingers through the sand, 
but even the tide grows tired of returning. 
Time is not a balm but a trowel
it digs, and digs, and digs, 
and leaves the hollow open. 

Grief is the shadow that outlives the flame. 
I carry it like a stone 
in the throat of my throat, 
its weight a language I’ve yet to learn. 

Still, the world insists on blooming
a bird’s song stitches the air, 
and I, unthreaded, 
count the absence 
as the only constant.

Echoes in the Fade

In the silence of a forgotten place,
I hear the whispers of a fading face,
A reminder that our time is brief,
A moment's beauty, a lifetime's grief,
The hours tick by like falling leaves,
Each one a memory, a piece of what we leave,
The weight of years, the sting of pain,
A bittersweet reminder of life's refrain,

We chase the sun, we dance in rain,
We cling to love, we grasp in vain,
The threads of life, so fragile and thin,
A single cut, and all our moments spin,
Into the void, where shadows play,
And darkness claims the light of day,
Yet even in the darkness, there's a glow,
A light that flickers, as the heart says no,

To the inevitability of our demise,
A truth we cannot escape, a fate that lies,
In wait for us, with patient, silent sighs,
A whispered promise, a gentle, loving guise,
That all we are, all we've known, will cease,
And in the stillness, our memories will release,
Like autumn's leaves, they'll rustle, they'll fall,
And in the silence, our stories will stand tall,

But even as we fade, our echoes remain,
A whispered legacy, a love that still sustains,
A flame that flickers, a heart that still beats,
A memory that clings, a soul that still retreats,
To the moments we lived, the love we shared,
The laughter, the tears, the joy, the care,
For in the end, it's not the years we live,
But the life we live, the love we give,

That truly matters, that truly remains,
A legacy of heart, a love that still sustains,
So let us cherish every moment we share,
Every breath, every heartbeat, every care,
For in the end, it's not the time we have,
But the love we give, the life we live, the memories we crave,
That will echo on, long after we're gone,
A bittersweet reminder, a love that still lives on.

The Shattered Mirror's Lament 

Each shard a memory, sharp and bright, 
Once framed in gold, now fractured, split. 
In every piece, a ghostly smile
A laugh that echoes, incomplete. 

The mender’s hands, with trembling art, 
Attempt to glue what time undid. 
But fragments cut with every touch, 
And bleed the hues of what we knew. 

Now gazing deep, the glass reveals 
A stranger’s eyes, a hollowed stare. 
The face I knew has slipped away, 
Leaving a void that cold air shares. 

Some shards still sing in fractured tones, 
A lullaby of what could be
While others hold the frost of dusk, 
Where all our "forevers" ended, brief. 

So let the pieces pierce the floor, 
A mosaic of the love we lost. 
For even broken, they hold the light
But not for me. Not for me most.

Echoes of Tears

Silent nights weeping with me,
Shadows dancing upon the wall,
A lonely heart beating in sorrow,
Yearning for a love that would not fall.

The wind whispers secrets in my ear,
Of memories that bring only pain,
A bittersweet reminder of what's lost,
A grief that refuses to wane.

In the darkness, I search for a light,
A guiding star to lead me through,
The emptiness that echoes within,
A hollow voice that whispers "what to do".

The tears I've cried have formed a sea,
A deep ocean where my heart would sail,
In search of solace, a place to be,
Where sorrow's waves would gently fail.

But still I hold on to the thought of you,
A memory that my heart holds true,
A love that shone like a beacon bright,
A light that guided me through the dark of night.

Echoes of Elegance

In the hollow of a forgotten melody,
a whispered promise of beauty resides,
where gentle fingers once danced upon,
the skin of a well-loved instrument.
The harmony of hues, a symphony,
plays softly in the recesses of the mind,
as sunbeams filter, warm and slow,
through the prism of a summer's day.

In secret gardens, petals unfold,
like the pages of a lover's tender tale,
each bloom a brush stroke on the canvas,
of a masterpiece that never fades.
The language of the beauty is a murmur,
a soothing balm that calms the soul,
a reminder of the harmony that exists,
between the heartbeat and the universe's goal.

In the stillness of a winter's night,
the stars align, a twinkling show,
a celestial showcase of wonder,
a beauty that the heart can know.
The world, a tapestry so fine and rare,
interwoven with the threads of love and care,
each strand a testament to the divine,
a beauty that echoes, beyond compare.

The Sidewalk's Green Insurgent 

A crack splits the concrete
a blade of green fists its way through, 
clawing past frost, steam, and cement’s grudge, 
a rebel flag in a gray fortress. 

It wears no medals, this rootless soldier, 
just a crown of rain and a heart of thirst, 
its spines bent but unbroken by the weight 
of cities grinding their teeth above. 

No one sees its war: how it gnaws at shadows, 
how it drinks from the rot of forgotten cans, 
how it hums a hymn through fractured earth, 
a psalm of not-yet-defeated. 

You might trip on its tenacity, 
swear it’s just a weed
but that green insurgent laughs in the storm, 
its roots a map of survived.

When the Horizon Swallowed the Sun
Grief descended like a storm, uninvited, 
Suffocating the breath of every dawn. 
The soul, now orphaned, traced its name in dust, 
Where whispers of Your absence echo on. 

The heart, a hollow vessel, once filled with light, 
Now hoards the weight of unspoken goodbyes. 
Each tear etched deeper than the scars before
A language only deserts could apply. 

In the silence, I’ve learned to speak in shadows, 
To kneel where rivers drown the voice of time. 
You asked me to wear loss as a second skin, 
Yet how can a candle burn beneath such rain? 

But You, the Weaver, spin sorrow into thread, 
To stitch the frayed edges of this broken dawn. 
Until the day the void returns to me 
A fragment of the love it borrowed
I’ll wander, a ghost in the anatomy of night, 
Holding Your name like a liturgy of wounds. 
For even grief, in its endless pilgrimage, 
Must one day bow to the mercy of tombs.

The Space Between 
It wasn’t the wanting. 
It was the pause 
between the beat of a moth’s wing 
against the glass
that humming, 
the quiet song of almost. 

Not the fire, 
but the flicker before it licks the flame, 
not the hunger, 
but the shadow of what’s unheld. 

Let’s chase the echo, then
not the thing itself, 
but the breath that trembles 
when we almost say it. 

Let’s keep the fire lit 
not by what we have, 
but by what we might never touch: 
the ache of the close-door, 
the soft click of a name 
left trembling on the tongue. 

Desire is the ghost of the leap, 
the gravity that pulls 
but never drops. 
We stay suspended, 
sweet and endless, 
in the space between.

The sunrise spilling laughter onto the meadow 
The dawn drips golden giggles on the grass, 
A chorus of sparrows humming bright threads, 
The river chuckles as it skips over stones, 
Children’s shadows dance, unburdened by time. 

When the sky paints smiles on every leaf, 
The heart opens like a blossom at noon, 
Joy rides the wind, a featherless kite, 
And the world sighs, content in its glow.

Unfolding Petals of Delight

In the garden of life, a flower blooms, 
A gentle whisper of happiness that fills the room, 
The soft caress of sunshine on a summer day, 
Brings warmth to the heart and chases all the blues away.

A child's laughter echoes, contagious and free, 
A melody that resonates deep within you and me, 
The twinkle in their eyes, a spark that ignites, 
A sense of wonder that opens doors to new delights.

The rhythm of music, a symphony so fine, 
That stirs the soul and makes the heart entwine, 
With every beat, a memory is made, 
A moment frozen in time, a joy that's not faded.

In the silence of night, a star shines bright, 
A guiding light that navigates through life's plight, 
The world is full of beauty, a tapestry so grand, 
A masterpiece that's woven with the threads of joy and love's command.

So let us bask in the radiance of this feeling, 
And let our spirits soar on the wings of joy that's revealing, 
For in its presence, we find our true selves, 
And our hearts are filled with the sweetness that never fades or shelves.

In the unfolding petals of delight, 
We find the essence of life, a treasure to hold tight, 
A sense of joy that's pure and true, 
A gift that's given to me and you.

Echoes in Amber 

Time bottles certain days in amber
how we keep them, unspooling 
the light around their edges. 

Your grandmother’s kitchen hums 
still in the crack of an egg, 
the way cinnamon clung to her wrists 
like a secret she refused to spend. 

We were always collecting sounds: 
the rattle of a milk truck at dawn, 
your father’s voice, a radio tuned 
between stations, static holding 
the shape of a name. 

Now the porch swings without you, 
its chains remembering the weight 
of laughter. You trace the map 
of an old song on your tongue, 
but the melody slips
a fish vanishing into deep water. 

Even the photographs grow shy, 
their colors bleeding into ghosts. 
You stand in the yard where the lilac bush 
once clawed at the sky, and wonder 
if you’re mourning the thing itself 
or the ache that lingers 
when the thing you loved 
was just the world 
for a moment, unbroken.

The Quiet Awe 

When morning spills its gold across the field, 
I stand and watch the sky unfold, 
Like a great, unrolled map of light. 

A single leaf twirls in the breeze, 
Its curve a whispered secret, 
And I feel the world pulse soft and bright. 

Stars linger in the hush of dusk, 
Their silver threads stitch the night, 
Each one a tiny lantern of wonder. 

I hear the river hum a low refrain, 
Stone to stone, a steady chant, 
And the water carries my breath away. 

In the hush of a child’s laugh, 
In the sudden bloom of a wild rose, 
I find the endless, gentle miracle of being. 

So I tilt my head, I open my eyes, 
And let the marvel rise like sunrise
A quiet awe that never ends.

The Journal Beneath the Floorboard 

Beneath the floorboard where the floor creaks, 
I found your journal, yellowed, thin
each page a photograph I’ve never seen: 
your handwriting, a map of then. 

You wrote of the scent of rain on bus windows, 
how we swore to meet each spring 
with pockets full of dandelion clocks. 
Now the clock ticks without that name, 
and the dandelions have gone to dust. 

I trace your words like a bruise that won’t fade, 
a love letter to a city we never named, 
its streets paved with the sound of your voice 
mumbling into the static of an old radio. 

There’s a sketch of your hand in the margins, 
fingers curled around a childhood fear
I’ll forget you, the lines seem to whisper. 
But you’re still here, aren’t you? 
In the ache of the floorboard’s hollow, 
in the way the light bends where you bent it, 
a ghost rehearsing how to stay.

Echoes of Sorrow

I AM NOT A STRANGER TO PAIN
I AM NOT A FOREIGNER TO TEARS
I AM NOT A GUEST IN THE HOUSE OF SADNESS
I AM THE OWNER OF THIS BROKEN HEART
I AM THE GUARDIAN OF THESE SHATTERED DREAMS
I AM THE KEEPER OF THESE SILENT SCREAMS
SORROW IS MY COMPANION MY FRIEND MY GUIDE
IT WALKS WITH ME THROUGH THE DARKEST NIGHT
IT WHISPERS TO ME IN THE DEEPEST SILENCE
IT REMINDS ME OF ALL THAT I HAVE LOST
IT TAUNTS ME WITH ALL THAT COULD HAVE BEEN
BUT STILL I HOLD ON TO THE MEMORIES
STILL I CHERISH THE LOVE THAT WE ONCE SHARED
STILL I SMILE THROUGH THE TEARS AND THE PAIN
FOR IN THE ECHOES OF SORROW I FIND A STRANGE COMFORT
A COMFORT THAT REMINDS ME I AM STILL ALIVE
A COMFORT THAT TELLS ME I AM STILL CAPABLE OF FEELING
SO LET THE SORROW WASH OVER ME
LET IT FLOOD MY SOUL WITH ITS DARK WATERS
FOR IN ITS DEPTHS I WILL FIND A GLIMMER OF HOPE
A HOPE THAT ONE DAY I WILL BE FREE FROM THIS PAIN
A HOPE THAT ONE DAY I WILL FIND PEACE AGAIN.

Beyond the Fading Light

Rays of sunshine filtering through the blinds
Awakening the soul to a new-found mind,
A gentle breeze that whispers low and sweet
Of a tomorrow where heartaches retreat,

In the silence, a spark takes flight
A flame that flickers with warmth and light,
Guiding us through life's plodding pace
And filling our hearts with a steady grace,

Like a lotus blooming in the darkest night
Hope rises, a beacon shining bright,
Its petals unfolding, a beauty to see
A symbol of strength, for you and me,

In the stillness, a voice begins to speak
A gentle murmur that our spirits seek,
A soothing melody that calms the mind
And leads us to a place where love is aligned,

With every step, with every fall
Hope lifts us up, through it all,
A constant presence that never fades
A reassuring touch that soothes our shades,

In the depths of sorrow, it's a light that stays
A comforting ember that guides our way,
Through life's turbulent and troubled sea
Hope is the anchor that sets our souls free,

And when the darkness closes in around
Hope is the whisper that echoes a gentle sound,
A reminder of a brighter day to come
A promise of a new beginning, a new life to be won.

Whispered threads of love
The quiet pulse of sunrise,
Tracing the curve of a sigh,
When eyes meet the soft horizon,

A breath becomes a promise,
And the silence folds into a smile,
While shadows linger,
The heart learns to glow,

In the garden of lingering thoughts,
Petals unfold like whispered verses,
Each touch a lingering echo,
Each word a lingering kiss,

When the night drapes its velvet,
Love stitches constellations on the skin,
And the soul, unburdened,
Finds its rhythm in the gentle hum
of two beating as one.

MORTAL ECHOES

I hear the whispers of my final breath
A gentle breeze that stirs the trees
And in its sigh, a truth is revealed
That all our moments are but brief

In the mirror's gaze, a face so worn
A map of lines and wrinkles born
Of laughter, tears, and all the years
A topography of joy and fears

The hours tick on, a relentless pace
A countdown to a final, silent space
Where memories and love will be the guide
That leads us through the dark, unknown tide

And when the time comes, and I am gone
My legacy will be the love that's strong
The echoes of my heart, the beat that stays
A rhythm that remains, a mortal sway

In the stillness, I will find my peace
A sense of calm, my worries released
For though my body may return to earth
My spirit will soar, and give new birth

To all the dreams, the hopes, the fears
The moments lived, the laughter, tears
For though mortality may take its toll
It cannot claim the love that makes us whole.

When the Sky Murmurs Secrets
I trace the veins of galaxies painted on the night, 
Each star a breath held still in the throat of time, 

They whisper of oceans unborn and mountains of light, 
Of a dance older than the ache of forgetting, 

I have not seen the face of the moon’s hidden sea, 
But I’ve cupped its cold radiance in my trembling palms, 

The wind carries hymns from the cradle of the Milky Way, 
And I am a beggar, begging for the shape of wonder
Is it the birth cry of comets? 
The silence between heartbeats? 
The way shadows kneel to dawn? 

I was small, but the sky taught me to swallow the vast, 
To let the unknown carve its poetry into my bones, 

Now I wander a compass of stardust and fractured questions, 
Chasing the echo of what the universe hums 
when it thinks no one is listening.

The Clockless Realm
The hourglass drowned in its own silence, 
Eternity, a labyrinth without an exit. 
Shadows kneel where the sun forgets to rise, 
And our breath, the only hymn that outlives the stars, 

Vines carve hymns into forgotten ruins, 
Love, a pendulum trapped between two infinites. 
The desert cradles the seed of an unyielding rain, 
And eternity, a scar that blooms in the wound of the now. 

The sky stitches constellations from fallen hours, 
The heart, a thief, hoards moments it cannot spend. 
The soul, a river that thirsts for its own source, 
Drinks from the well of a nameless dawn. 

Only the unwritten verse knows the end of the story, 
Only the echo remembers what the cry has forgotten. 
Only the star that drowns in its own light becomes the compass, 
Only the hand that holds the void cradles infinity. 

We are the flicker never swallowed by the flame, 
The breath that outlives the throat, the shadow that outgrows the sun
Eternity, the wound that never forgets to heal: 
A paradox humming in the marrow of the unspoken.

Grey Dawn on the Balcony 
He presses his thumb against the cold glass, 
the world below a muted watercolor of traffic and rain. 
A coffee cup rests on the railing, steam curling like a sigh, 
its heat fading faster than the sunrise. 

The neighbor’s cat, a speck of soot, watches from a windowsill, 
eyes reflecting a streetlamp that has already forgotten its purpose. 
He pulls his coat tighter, not against the chill, 
but against the ache that settles behind his ribs. 

A newspaper lies open, headlines about triumphs he never felt, 
the ink smudged by a tear he didn’t notice until it dried. 
He remembers a song his mother hummed while folding laundry, 
the melody now a ghost drifting through the hallway. 

Below, a delivery bike rattles past, its rider humming a tune, 
unaware that each note lands on a heart already bruised. 
He thinks of the empty chair across the table, 
the silence there louder than any argument ever was. 

The city hums, indifferent, as he watches the clouds 
pull themselves apart, revealing slivers of pale light. 
He breathes in the damp air, lets it fill his lungs, 
and for a moment, the melancholy feels like a companion, 
not a weight, sharing the balcony’s quiet watch. 

When the bell above the door finally rings, he rises, 
leaves the cup behind, and steps back into the drizzle, 
carrying the soft gray of the dawn like a coat he cannot shed.

Unbroken Petals

The garden of the soul was shaken,
By the fierce storms that life has spoken,
Pain, like autumn, stripped the tree,
Leaving scars, a testament to destiny,

But even in the barren landscape cold,
A flame of hope, a light, did unfold,
A rose, with unbroken petals, stood,
Defying the tempests, as it withstood,

The weight of tears, the sting of rain,
Could not erase the beauty that remained,
For in the depths of sorrow, a spark,
Ignited a fire, that lit the dark,

The winds of adversity, they did blow,
But the roots of resilience, did grow,
Deeper, stronger, a foundation true,
A bond between the heart, and all it knew,

Like a river, that flows to the sea,
The spirit, with each challenge, is set free,
To navigate the rapids, to find its way,
Through the darkness, into a brighter day,

The unbroken petals, a symbol stand,
Of the courage, that lies, within the land,
A reminder that even in the night,
A light, a love, a hope, can still take flight,

And when the storms, have passed, and gone,
The garden of the soul, will bloom again, strong,
The unbroken petals, a testament will be,
To the resilience, of the human heart, wild, and free.

Eternal Embrace 

In the quiet moments when the stars align, 
Your laughter becomes the melody I chasin’. 
If love’s a language, then my heart’s been learnin’ 
Every verse you whisper, every note you yearn in. 

I’ll be the coffee warm on winter’s bitter morn, 
The softest shadow when the world feels stern. 
Through tangled days where patience starts to fray, 
I’ll mend the frayed edges, smooth the wounds you earn. 

No need for crowns or thrones of gold to boast
Your eyes hold galaxies I’d never lose. 
I’ll trade the sun for a single spark from you, 
For in your gaze, my forever finds its house. 

Through storms we’ll dance, through fire we’ll stand, 
Two roots entwined where the earth is cracked. 
If you should wander, I’ll be the bridge you cross, 
The steady hand when shadows fall too black. 

No script is needed, no grand, staged lines
Just truth between us, raw and unafraid. 
I’ll write your name in the clouds, let the sky be my rhyme, 
And when our time’s a song that’s played, 
I’ll still hum your tune in the dust of fading days. 

‘Cause love ain’t a spark it’s embers never dying, 
A pledge to stay when the world begins to flee. 
You’re my first breath, my last goodbye, 
The only map I’ll ever need to find eternity.

Whisper of the Wild

Nature breathes in quiet pulses, 
steady, unashamed. 
In the way a leaf unfurls after a storm, 
in the way the wind carries a song through pine, 
in the way a river refuses to remember the stones it has brushed. 

Nature is the ember that glows beneath frost, 
even when no eyes linger on its heat. 
It is the tide that rolls, indifferent to applause, 
whether or not a shore watches its rise. 
It is the sunrise that climbs without asking permission, 
never wondering if the world is ready to see. 

Some will call it background, 
some will hear only the rustle. 
Some will label it ordinary, 
because it does not shout for notice. 

But nature was never meant to bow before gazes. 
It was meant to exist wild, whole, uncontained. 
If only they understood, 
the forest does not live in the forest‑watcher’s mind, 
it lives in the soil that dares to hold roots. 

If only

Quiet Ledger of Belief 

A sunrise whispered through cracked curtains, 
soft enough to let the room breathe. 

You place a question on the sill, 
let it sit beside the mug that still holds warmth. 

Listen for the hum of the kettle, 
it’s the same tone the world uses when it promises 
more than the night has given. 

Tie a thin string of hope around a thumb, 
feel it tighten when doubts drift in, 
loosen when gratitude settles. 

Speak to the empty chair across the table, 
say the words you would say to a friend you trust, 
even if the chair does not answer. 

Turn the page of a notebook, 
write a line that does not need proof, 
just the certainty that it exists. 

Step outside, let the wind brush your cheek, 
notice how it carries the scent of rain 
and the faint echo of a promise kept long ago. 

When the day folds into dusk, 
light the candle and let its flame wobble
it does not demand perfection, only presence. 

Gather the fragments of today, 
place them in a quiet jar, 
label it “faith” in a hand that still trembles. 

Sleep with the jar close, 
knowing the world will spin again, 
and the jar will hold its quiet ledger, 
ready for the next sunrise to write upon it.

Echoes in the Silence

In the hollow of my chest, a cave resides
Where shadows dance and darkness abides
A place where solitude has made its nest
And I am the guardian of this quiet unrest

The city outside is a distant hum
A muffled melody that's never to become
A part of me, for in this space I've found
A world where I am the only sound

The walls that surround me, they whisper low
Of memories and dreams that only I may know
The creaking floor, a symphony of old
Echoes of footsteps that have long since grown cold

In this solitude, I find a strange reprieve
A sense of freedom from the world's loud leave
A chance to breathe, to think, to be
A moment's peace, where I am me

The silence is a canvas, vast and wide
Where I can paint my thoughts, and let them reside
The emptiness, a mirror to my soul
Where I can see the depths, and make myself whole

In this quiet, I find a gentle friend
A companion that will never come to an end
A place where I can hide, and be alone
And find the solace that I've been searching for, back home.

Echoes of Sorrow

In the silence of night
A lonely heart beats slow
 Memories of joy now lost
Fading like the morning light
My soul is a canvas gray
Painted with tears and pain
The colors of happiness
Have faded like the summer rain

In this emptiness I search
For a glimpse of what's been lost
A whisper of a love now gone
A shadow that forever costs

not with a slam of the door but with the rustle of a coat. 
Speak to it in low tones, not demanding answers, 
just offering the simple fact that you are present. 

Give it a cup of tea that has been left a moment too long, 
the steam curling like a sigh, the bitterness reminding you 
that sweetness can be a memory, not a promise. 
Let the steam rise, let the scent settle, let the silence fill the space. 

Allow sorrow to look at the faces you pass, 
to listen to the laughter that feels distant, 
to taste the taste of a song you once sang. 
Feed it with moments that are honest, not polished, 
for it grows on raw, unfiltered feeling. 

When it stumbles into the wrong thought, 
or rushes ahead before you can catch up, 
do not pull it back with force. 
Acknowledge its haste, give it a soft hand, 
a place to rest, a breath of cool water, a pause to name itself. 

If it cracks, gather the shards tears, sighs, half‑spoken words
mix them with the quiet of a night sky, 
let the constellations of old joy hold them together. 
The glue is not perfect; it is the patina of having survived. 

When the weight feels lighter, let it wander a little, 
into a conversation, into a small act of kindness, 
into the sticky sweetness of being seen. 
Do not tie it too tightly with expectations. 

A cared‑for sorrow, when honored, will give back pieces of itself
not as burdens, but as quiet strength that you can carry forward. 
Trust the process. 
It knows its own path back to you.

Fragmented Light

a hallway of ordinary rooms stretches ahead,

A Cartography of Light

Fragments of a Shattered Symphony

Beneath the sand’s deceitful grin, 

Though storms may blur the lighthouse’ glow, 
My compass spins your ancient name, 
And when the tide of doubt surges wild, 
I’ll kneel and let the waves carve hymns 
Into the bones I cannot see, 

For every scar that whispers why? 
I’ll answer with a deeper trust
The seed that splits the concrete wide 
Is not the rock, but what it feeds.

WHEN THE PAST DRAWS NEAR 

When the past draws near, I breathe it in
a scent of rain on cracked concrete, 
a song that stutters through a rusted radio, 
the way your grandmother’s hands folded dough 
into time’s warm oven. 

I’ve traced the cracks in a childhood window, 
watched shadows dance where our younger selves 
ran barefoot through the dusk of summer. 
I’ve held the weight of a closed piano, 
its silence humming with keys once played 
in a different key of light. 

Nostalgia is the ghost of a hand in mine 
on a path now overgrown with thorns, 
the echo of a name whispered in a hallway 
where walls have forgotten their colors. 
It’s the ache of a photograph’s edges, 
fading, curling like the corners of a goodbye. 

I’ve tasted it in the first bite of a lost recipe, 
in the way a certain star lingers too long 
after sunset, as if delaying the dark. 
I’ve worn it like a second skin soft, unraveling
threaded with the language of fireflies 
and the low hum of a mother’s lullaby. 

Do you feel it? That pull of the tide 
toward shores we no longer recognize? 
The past is a door left ajar, 
a letter addressed to a version of us 
who still believes in the magic of forever. 
We carry it like a lantern, 
illuminating the ghosts of what once glowed, 
even as the present folds its map 
and the future blinks uncertain.

Ash to Ankle 
Her spine is a compost heap
each vertebra a buried hymn, 
unfurling roots toward the light. 

She lets the old language rot
syntax of survival, nouns 
that outlived their meanings. 
Something new is wet in her throat, 
a bird’s first song after a fire. 

She peels back the husk of yesterday’s skin, 
and what was once a death grip 
becomes a vine, learning to climb 
the inside of her ribs. 

The mirror shows a stranger 
with her eyes: half-formed, 
already shedding. 

PROFILE TRAITS: 
Addicted to metamorphosis. 
Wears her shedding like a second skeleton. 
Mistakes echoes for beginnings. 

SUBTEXT: 
To be reborn is to drown 
in the weight of your own hollows.

Whispers of the Eternal Peaks 
The traveler’s breath became a mountain, 
His pulse a river carving the stone
Stars stitched their secrets into his eyes, 
And the night bloomed with unspoken vows. 

A fox trailed shadows through the pine grove, 
Its paws painting the frost with desire
While the moon, a silent court of lovers,

He met her where the cliffs dissolve into mist
Her hair, a constellation unraveled, 
Her voice, the hum of a thousand cascades

And when dawn cracked the sky like an eggshell,

It soars, a phoenix built from shattered embers,

The Weight of Unspoken Ashes 
A stone rests in my palm
smooth as a held breath, 
its heft a quiet argument 
against the river’s murmur. 

Here, the water forgets its name, 
wearing a thousand faces 
as it bends around the rocks 
that refuse to move. 

I count the shadows: 
one for each time the light 
slips off the current’s back, 
another for the birds 
who carve their messages 
into the sky’s blank page. 

My fingers trace the moss 
clinging to the bank
a green that does not ask 
why the world is wet. 

This stone will not speak. 
It only grows heavier, 
a cairn of small certainties 
stacked in the language 
of unbroken things. 

The wind carries the scent of pine, 
but I taste the salt 
of older storms, 
the kind that pools in the hollows 
where the roots forget to reach. 

I place it back in the earth
a monument to what remains 
when even the river 
learns to carry its sorrow 
without a sound. 

Lichen will bloom there someday, 
soft and persistent, 
turning loss into a color 
the world can wear.

The Clockmaker’s Star 

He winds the gears of midnight, 
each cog a constellation, precise as a wish. 
A pendulum of light swings between his palms
a star, built for a child’s palm, ticks into being. 

His daughter kneels, a pilgrim of the unknown, 
her fingertips brushing its brass heart. 
It hums a hymn of friction, of distant supernovae
and her breath becomes a hymn to the impossible. 

Her eyes, twin telescopes, unravel the script of his soul: 
how he stole time’s blueprints to forge this fragile flame. 
The room swells with the weight of unsaid equations, 
while the star spins, a galaxy trapped in a gear’s embrace. 

Time, unraveling, is a ribbon of stardust. 
She asks, Daddy, is the sky a clock too? 
And wonder, that sly alchemist, turns every end 
into an unsung beginning
a constellation of maybes flickering in her hair.

Auroral Hymn 

In the cathedral of the night, I stand, 
A pilgrim beneath endless blue, 
Where constellations trace their silent paths, 
And galaxies hum hymns ancient and true. 

The stars, like whispers, murmur secrets old, 
Of supernovas’ demise and births of light, 
While comets, with their tails of fire unroll, 
Weave tales of cosmic dance through velvet night. 

Oh! Witness the auroras’ ethereal waltz, 
Green ribbons, pink, in heavens’ embrace, 
A symphony of colors without halt
The sun’s own breath in magnetic grace. 

Each photon, a note in the universe’ song, 
Each atom, a verse of existence’ tale. 
The void, adorned with galaxies’ bright throng, 
Sings wonder in a voice that never fails. 

And here, in this hush where the cosmos breathes, 
My soul, a vessel, drinks in boundless awe. 
For wonder, unchained, in its boundless reach, 
Is the light that time and darkness never saw.

The Weight of Absence 
Grief arrives as a storm without thunder, 
a slow seep of shadow through every crack, 
its breath a tide that drowns the clock’s hands
time dissolves in its salted ache. 

You carry it like an attic of dust, 
where memories cling to the rafters, 
fragile and sharp as moth-wing shreds, 
whispering your lost ones’ names in braille. 

The ocean of loss has no shoreline; 
each wave is a mirror, each recede a theft
you learn to wade through the hollows, 
counting shells of unsaid words 
at the bottom of your pockets. 

Yet in the marrow of this ache, 
a single green shoot stirs
not a promise, but a defiance, 
unfurling where the cracks let light in. 

And when the weight feels less like a stone 
and more like the earth’s own gravity, 
you’ll find their voice in the wind’s turn, 
a star’s flicker, the way the dawn leans close 
to trace the shape of your unfinished song.

The Architecture of Wonder 

I trace constellations on the pavement, 
a child’s map of mysteries, 
before science taught me they were not there. 
Now I know the distances
how light bends through time to reach my eyes
yet still, some nights, I kneel 
and whisper to the dark: Tell me more. 

Science dismantles myths, gives names to stars, 
but wonder is not a thing to be dissected. 
It flickers like a candle in a storm, 
unstable, yet stubborn. 
Even as algorithms predict my gaze, 
as notifications drown the silent awe 
of a sky without words, 

I hunt for it in the cracks: 
a dewdrop’s geometry, 
the math of a leaf’s spiral, 
how a stranger’s laughter once echoed 
in a subway tunnel, turning steel into song. 
These are the blueprints I build with
loose, imperfect, refusing to be archived. 

Doubt is a door I’ve learned to leave ajar. 
If I close it too tight, 
wonder suffocates in the vacuum. 
I’ve memorized the data, 
but the data cannot tell me 
how it feels to stand small 
and let the universe breathe. 

So I choose to let wonder be my compass, 
not a destination, but the map’s blank spaces, 
where I etch my questions in pencil, 
soft enough to vanish, 
bold enough to remain.

The Mended Sock 
One hole in the heel, another by the toe
this sock has seen more mends than I remember to sew. 
I bought it in a pair, bright red, bold, 
now it’s a patchwork of duct tape and stories untold. 

It’s slipped off my foot in the iciest snow, 
rescued my toe from the freeze, though its threads barely hold. 
People smirk when they see it, "Replace it, for heaven's sake," 
but I keep it close, this frayed, stubborn flake. 

For resilience isn’t born in the new or the pristine, 
but in the fabric that clings when the world tries to split. 
Each tear is a map of the ground I’ve refused to lose, 
each mend a small victory, threaded with proof of "I choose." 

So let it unravel. Let the holes multiply. 
Resilience isn’t about never falling, you see
it’s the sock that stays on when the path gets too steep, 
and the foot that keeps walking, though it’s not quite complete.

The Echo of Your Name 
The teacup cools in your absence, 
steam curling into the silence 
like a question unanswered. 
Your chair holds the ghost of your shape, 
and the clock’s hands 
drift like leaves in reverse. 

Outside, the sky swallows the sun whole
a hunger that mimics my own. 
I trace the hollow where your voice lived, 
count the hours in the ache 
of empty syllables. 

My ribs, a hollowed-out porch, sway 
beneath the weight of unspent words. 
I press my ear to the floorboards, 
listen for the hum of your footsteps, 
but the house has forgotten your tune. 

Even the shadows grow lighter, 
thin as old film. 
I fold the crumple of your laughter 
into a paper crane, 
set it adrift on the wind
a message without a postmark. 

The echo of your name grows thin, 
a thread unraveling at the edges. 
I learn to breathe in the shape of absence, 
each inhale a quiet surrender 
to the light that once bent through you.

The River's Ember 
The river wears the dusk’s last amber shawl, 
its skin a map of where the light once ran
crimson threads of current, quick and bold, 
weave through the shadows like a lover’s sigh. 

Oaks bend low to hear its whispered hymn, 
their leaves a chorus trembling with reply. 
Each ripple etches secrets on the stone, 
a language older than the stars’ faint script. 

I am the ash that mirrors its fierce flame, 
a pulse entwined with night’s unyielding tide
where water sings, the soul finds its refrain, 
and every bend holds some forbidden sun. 

Let bridges break, let cities drown in green
this current knows no master but the moon. 
It carves its path through heart and heathered moor, 
a hymn of embers never meant to sleep.

The Lighthouse Keeper's Faith 
Each dusk, I wind the beacon’s thread 
to stitch the sky with silver seams
a needle’s glow against the black 
that swallows all but what it needs. 

 

The storms arrive without a bell, 
their growls a chorus, deep and raw. 
I count the seconds between cracks 
where thunder splits the bone of waves. 

 

Years pass. The tower’s spine grows thin. 
Moss gnaws the stones I swore to keep. 
The beam now stumbles, drunk on rust, 
its arc a wobble in the deep. 

 
But faith, like lighthouses, is built 
on absence what we choose to say 

when all the maps are torn to shreds, 
when even stars seem to retreat. 
I twist the lens. The flame still hisses
a small, defiant, stubborn heat.

Seasons in the Oak's Embrace 
Beneath the oak where seasons turn their wheels, 
I trace the scars of time in gnarled bark's folds. 
Each ring a tale of storms that bent but never broke, 
While saplings whisper secrets to the soil below. 

In spring, the oak dons a gown of emerald lace, 
Each bud a note in nature's symphony. 
The robins build their cradles in its arms, 
And dappled light dances on the forest floor. 

By summer, branches stretch like open hands, 
Offering shade to wanderers lost in heat. 
The cicadas sing their fevered, golden hymns, 
As the tree guards the roots where my childhood crept. 

Then autumn comes with brushes dipped in flame, 
Painting the canopy in rust and gold. 
Leaves spiral down like memories released, 
Each one a promise that nothing stays the same. 

Now winter cloaks it in a silence deep, 
Where frost etches patterns on bark's weathered face. 
Yet in the stillness, life persists beneath the snow, 
As the oak dreams of spring in its frozen grace. 

So I sit where the earth and sky embrace, 
And learn from the oak how to hold time's flow
To grieve the fallen leaf, yet welcome the snow, 
And find in decay the seed of something new.

The Symphony of Wild Petals and Thunder
Your name is a spark in the forest of my breath, 
I chase the scent of vanished seasons
You are the tempest that taught the sea to sing, 
The rose that bleeds its crimson into dawn, 

Our love, a fugitive, burns without a season, 
A violet clings to the edge of a cliff
And when the horizon cracks into gold, 
We become the storm, the ash, the unspoken hymn 
That the moon carves into the bones of the night.

The Silent Prayer 
In the hush where whispers turn to flame, 
A spark remains where shadows claim 
Their throne of doubt, though never named. 
Incense curls in silent prayer, 
A breath that faith imparts, more rare 
Than all the stars adrift in rhyme. 

The heart, a temple, beats its hymn, 
To stars that dance beyond the rim. 
When all the maps of reason part, 
And storms conspire to break the heart, 
A thread of light, though faint, is cast
The anchor of the soul’s request. 

Dawn’s first blush, a promise sealed, 
To walk through ash as if through bloom, 
The unseen hand that steers the tide, 
Unfurls the sails no tempest looms. 
No bell tolls, no trumpet’s cry, 
Yet still the soul elects to try. 

So let the skeptic count his days, 
While faith, unproven, still outlasts 
The ledger of the void’s cold math. 
Here, in the dark, the lantern’s path
A silent flame, a nameless grace, 
The architect of time and space.

Echoes of the Unseen 

We dance with the clock’s silent ticking, 
never daring to ask if tomorrow’s a myth. 
Our breaths, fragile as autumn leaves, 
carry the weight of every unspoken truth
how the body is just a borrowed suit, 
and the soul, a traveler with no return ticket. 

They say the heart knows no clock, 
yet here I am, counting beats like coins 
in a purse that will one day empty. 
Even the strongest roots crack the soil, 
and even love, when stretched too thin, 
whispers I’m sorry before it unravels. 

But what if the fear isn’t in dying, 
but in how we forget to live before the end? 
We build our days from shadows, 
chasing moments that dissolve like sugar on the tongue. 
I’ve learned to carry grief like a second skin
it’s the quietest way to remember: 
the laughter, the scars, the way your hands 
clenched the night you thought the world was over. 

The stars don’t mourn the fallen. 
They just burn, relentless and indifferent. 
So I’ll burn too
not in defiance of the dark, 
but to prove that light exists 
between the breath before and the breath after. 
When the final curtain falls, 
let the echo of my name be this: 
I was here. I loved. I let the light in.

The Hourglass of Us 
Will the sand still fall
When I dare to count my breaths? 
Will the sun still rise
To see the clock’s last heave? 

Does the body remember
The weight of its making? 
Does the soul still tremble
When the body begins to break? 

Will the mirror still speak
When I ask it my age? 
Will it whisper, you’re older than decay
Or you’re younger than the grave? 

Does the heart still beat
Knowing its own dusk draws near? 
Does the blood still sing
To a tempo no hand can steer? 

When the body becomes a bridge
Will the flame cross without fear? 
Or will it linger, a shadow
On the edge of not being here? 

Time, that old thief
Steals the pages of our day. 
Yet in the stealing, it teaches
How to love the ink before it bleeds away.

The Persistent Bloom 
Hope is a seed the wind forgot, 
Dropped in the crevice where no sun dares, 
Clutching the darkness like a cloak, 
Yet stretching its stems toward the light. 

The walls scoff, "You'll never breach us," 
But the root is a patient architect, 
Carving through stone with silent will, 
A hymn written in the language of cracks. 

I once dismissed it as a myth, 
A tale spun by the desperate, 
Until I found it, parched and thin, 
Its single flower trembling, defiant. 

The storm came, as storms do, 
Screaming to erase its trace, 
But it held on, each raindrop

Now I kneel where the concrete ends, 
My palms pressed to the earth's cold skin, 
Waiting for the next whisper, 
Rooting, reaching, relentless.

Whispers Beneath the Celestial Canopy
The forest bows its boughs like cathedral arches, 
Where light and shadow weave a gospel of rustling leaves

Sings hymns to the stones that cradle its course. 

Roots drink the clock’s forgotten hours,

The pines stand sentinel, their breath incense
Offered to the sky’s unblinking altar. 

When autumn gilds the veins of the maple,

Mountains hoard the secrets of constellations,

For nature does not speak in thunder or quake, 
But in the slow unraveling of seed to spine
A quiet rebellion against the grave, 
Where all things return, and begin again.

When Sorrow Knocks at Dusk
When sorrow knocks at dusk, 
it doesn’t announce its name
The breath stills, 
a tremor in the chest, 
like a door left ajar 
in a house no one tends. 

A shawl woven from autumn’s first frost 
settles on the shoulders, 
heavy as a word unsaid, 
older than the moon’s slow ache. 

It carves its name into the marrow, 
not with rage, but a quiet 
precision
a pendulum of memory swinging 
between "what was" and "what remains." 

Yet the stars, indifferent, pierce the veil, 
and the heart, a stubborn seed, 
rooting through frost, 
whispers: Even shadows need a light to bend toward.

Eternal Echoes 
I wander where the wildflowers sway, 
Their trembling heads like whispered prayers in the rain, 
The earth hums secrets only hearts can decode, 
And I, a beggar, clutch fragments of your name. 

The sky bleeds dusk in hues of want, 
A canvas stretched too thin for mortal hands. 
Love, a tempest, fierce and vast, 
Cracks the shell of reason, drowns the land. 

Your laughter once was my sunrise, 
A symphony of fireflies trapped in winter’s breath. 
Now silence carves its throne where warmth should rise, 
And every breeze feels like the edge of death. 

They say the soul is a lone star drifting, 
But I’ve found mine tangled in your absence
A vine that climbs through shattered glass, 
Blooming thorns where tender petals dance. 

I trace the constellations on my skin, 
Map the ache where your shadow still clings. 
Romanticism is not a cage of sin, 
But the madness that makes us alive when we sing: 

What is love if not the world upended? 
The storm that shatters us, then stitches the wound? 

I’d let the oceans boil to ink, 
To write our story in ashes and perfume. 

The moon, a voyeur, steals my sighs, 
And weaves them into threads for the night to keep. 
Even ruins have a right to rise, 
When passion’s the hammer, and grief, the chisel, deep. 

So let the critics call it folly
This ache to fuse two souls into one. 
For I’ve seen the divine in a wilted daffodil, 
And the apocalypse in a look that lingers too long. 

I’d trade all logic for one more touch, 
One more proof that we were real. 
Romanticism’s not a phase we outgrow
It’s the wound, the balm, the wound again, surreal. 

The heart, you see, is no machine
It’s a wildfire that burns twice as bright before it ends.

What Is Love? 

“What’s love?” asked the child, 
“A teddy bear hug or a cookie shared?” 
“What’s love?” asked the chemist, 
“A dopamine spark, a hormone’s tide.” 
“What’s love?” said the couple, 
“Forty years of the same old fight, still here.” 
“What’s love?” mused the poet, 
“A metaphor that slips through the net.” 

“What’s love?” said the merchant, 
“A diamond sold in a heart-shaped box.” 
“What’s love?” howled the storm, 
“Lightning that splits the ancient oak.” 
“What’s love?” whispered the ghost, 
“A memory clung to empty walls.” 
“What’s love?” sighed the sage, 
“The sun, the shadow, both in one.” 

You ask the question, 
Then cradle the answer like a match
Afraid to light it, 
Afraid it’ll outshine the dark.

The Unspoken Account 

Swipe the card you found in the glovebox 
after they left you with the keys. 
Leave the coffee cup in the sink
let the milk in it congeal, 
a pale skin forming over the lie. 

Answer the door in their shirt, 
the one hanging in your hallway, 
three sizes too small. 
Their shoes are by the fire, 
still warm from the journey 
you never made. 

The last text you sent 
still says I’ll be there soon. 
You don’t delete it. 
You don’t add anything. 
The clock on your phone ticks 
like a borrowed hour. 

You learn to eat meals alone, 
cutting the chicken into smaller pieces, 
as if the portions could shrink 
to fit the hollow where their voice 
used to sit. 

The bill arrives on a Tuesday. 
You sign the back, 
but don’t open it. 
Some debts 
are paid in silence.

The Clockless Sea 
You say eternity is a shore we can’t reach, 
the tides keep rewriting our names in the now, 
but I see it in the pause between two waves
how they rise, break, return to the same shapeless deep, 
as if the ocean itself is learning to remember. 

We count in shadows: dawn’s first light, moon’s slow tilt, 
yet here we are, stitching time with breath and dust, 
building homes where hours dissolve like salt in rain. 
How do you hold what doesn’t bend toward an end? 
Maybe it’s the ache of this question that lasts
the way your laughter once echoed in empty rooms, 
now a hymn the stars hum without needing to hear. 
I’d trade all my clocks for a single moment 
that refuses to fade, even as hands forget to move. 
Eternity isn’t the never-ending, love
it’s the return. The way the world turns back to you, 
again and again, like the sea to its unbroken shore.

The Shattered Echo of a Forgotten Melody
The heart, a shattered mirror, cannot piece the light, 
Each fragment holds a face, a name, a night now unlit. 
Silence blooms where words once danced, a language lost in flight, 
The desert of your absence swallows every drop of rain. 

And storms that once embraced me now wear a stranger's skin, 
I trace the hollow chambers where your echo still aligns. 
Love, a shipwrecked hymn, drifts toward a shoreless sea, 
Its wreck still hums the tune of what the future never saw. 

The wound is not a wound, but a door left open to the wind, 
A ghost in every breath, yet still, the dusk remains.

The Arithmetic of Absence 

They say time heals all wounds, 
but they never mention the math
how you’ll count each day in halves: 
the before, the after, 
the space between your ribs 
where a name once fit like a cipher. 

You’ll learn subtraction first: 
the weight of a coffee cup 
without the heat of their hands, 
the silence where their voice 
used to spill over the edge of your sentences. 
You’ll subtract the future 
they imagined in your breath, 
until your lungs feel hollow, 
filled only with the echo of a door 
that no longer waits to close. 

Multiplication comes at night. 
You’ll lie awake, multiplying every almost 
into a lifetime of might-have-beens
the way their laughter once tangled 
with the radio, the way they 
never asked for the recipe of your soul. 
Each memory will breed a hundred ghosts, 
and you’ll wonder if love is just 
a sum we’re never meant to solve. 

Division is the quietest crime. 
You’ll split your shadow in two, 
trying to keep the pieces 
that still hum with their absence. 
The phone in your hand 
will divide the day into screens, 
each notification a hope you can’t delete
though you know now 
how easily a profile picture 
can become a relic. 

And addition? 
Addition is the way your body 
still reaches for the warmth 
of a bed that’s grown colder 
since they left. 
Add the taste of salt and steel 
when you bite into an apple, 
remembering how they 
used to peel you one, 
slowly, like they were unwrapping 
a clock. 

In the end, 
you’ll carry the equation 
like a bruise: 
How do you love something 
so much it becomes a language 
of loss? 
The answer, you’ll find, 
is never written in numbers.

The Forest's Forgotten Dictionary
I once believed forests had secret vocabularies
how the wind would spell love in pine needles, 
and oak acorns could conjugate in rain. 
But now I know they're just being practical, 
arranging moss like commas, 
tiling lichen into punctuation. 

Still, I find myself collecting root-words 
on my walks
pressing fern fronds between pages of field guides, 
hoping they'll translate into something 
more than just the rustle of survival. 

The maples leaf-craft with such precision, 
each scarred branch a verb in decline. 
Even stones have etched their grievances 
in the slow dialect of erosion. 

I wonder if the brook, 
which stutters over stones all day, 
has learned to read the moon's reflections 
or if it's just rehearsing for the sea. 

The forest doesn't care for my grammar, 
but I keep trying to parse its silence
to catch the syntax of a squirrel's chatter, 
the semiotics of a spider's web. 

Maybe nature isn't a language at all, 
but a dialect of becoming
where every leaf is both a sentence 
and the absence of one.

The Silent Room 
In the hush where shadows dwell, 
A ghost of grief begins to swell. 
No thunder, just a quiet pain, 
That seeps through every crack, each vein. 

A cup of tea, now just a shell, 
Cold and still, a broken spell. 
Letters stacked, no names to bear, 
Unsent verses, sharp with care. 

I trace the scars that absence leaves, 
In corners where the light won’t reach. 
Not a storm, nor midnight’s cry, 
But the dawn that feels so dry. 

No need to grasp or to pretend
It dwells here, where the silence bends. 
A shadow I can’t shake or flee, 
This quiet sorrow, my old friend.

Echoes of a Silent Rain
The clock’s shadow gnaws at the wall
Midnight spills its ink into the cracks, 

A ghost of laughter trembles in the air
As the piano swallows its dissonant notes, 

Your name, a wilted rose in my palm
Thorns whispering hymns of forgotten winters, 

The candle weeps its last amber tear
While the mirror cracks a joke no one hears, 

We are all ruins in the making
Each step a dirge on the stage of dusk, 

The moon, a pale mourner, drapes her light
Over the graves of our unspoken vows, 

Yet in this ache, a strange serenity blooms
A star, half-born, in the marrow of the storm.

The Door That Doesn’t Close 

He stood before the door, hand raised
each knock an echo of the last, 
part anticipation, part resignation, 
as if waiting for a bell that never rings. 

Inside, the air hung still
a paused clock, a stopped metronome. 
She’d opened it once, let the light in, 
and now it only led back to the same threshold. 

They’d tried to lock it, but the key 
had vanished into the pocket of a stranger 
who claimed it was never theirs to hold. 

Eternity, they learned, wasn’t a room 
but the silence between heartbeats, 
the breath before sleep, the moment 
after the last star forgets to shine.

The Clockmaker’s Eterne 
In a hidden atelier where shadows cling, 
The clockmaker fashions a time without end. 
Gears of silver, chains of light, 
He weaves the seconds into a symphony of night. 

No hands turn here, no pendulum sways
Just whispers of eternity in bronze and haze. 
He carves the hours into a faceless dial, 
And names it Forever, then smiles at the tale. 

One day, a girl with starlight in her hair 
Stumbles into the workshop, curious, bare.

The dusk folds its wings into the sky, 
Footsteps dissolve in the rain’s slow script
A clock’s breath fogs the glass, 
While shadows sip the last light of memory. 
Even silence, too, forgets to grieve.

Love's Arithmetic 

I asked Love, “Are you a sum or a puzzle?” 
It smiled and said, “Neither. I’m the space 
Between the numbers where the errors gather. 
You add your heart, subtract the hours
Yet I thrive in the remainder.” 

“Can you be measured?” I pressed, “In years?” 
Love replied, “No, in the weight of a glance, 
The length of a pause when the world forgets to breathe.” 
“And grief?” I asked. “Is that part of the equation?” 
“Grief is the tax you pay for the privilege 
Of holding a soul in your trembling hands.” 

So I’ve learned to count in rhythms, not figures
The beat of a hand in mine, the subtraction 
Of silence when it’s gone. Love is the math 
Where the answer is always a question, 
And the equation is rewritten with each breath.

The Lease on Our Skin 

I’ve always known the landlord was a ghost, 
a silhouette in the hall, never named, 
never photographed. The lease said 
30, once, then 40. Now it whispers 60
a number we cross out with each cigarette, 
each sleepless hour, each joy we let bloom 
like a garden in a borrowed plot. 

We tidy the rooms, scrub the walls, 
but the contract’s ink seeps through, 
a watermark on our palms. They say 
this body’s a rental, no extensions, 
no sublet. So we polish the floors, 
avoid the mirror’s gaze, and when 
the eviction notice comes
a cold hand on the shoulder we 
hand over the keys, trembling, 
counting the years we never owned. 

But sometimes, in the quiet, 
we laugh, plant roots anyway, 
because the garden’s beauty isn’t 
in the permanence, but the 
wild, desperate bloom before 
the ghost collects. 

Still, the lease remains: 
a contract signed in infancy, 
terms we never agreed to, 
penalties we’re too afraid to read. 
The landlord asks: What did you 
do with the loan of light? 
and we answer in shadows, 
or not at all. 

Perhaps it’s not the keys we return 
but the weight of their absence
a hollow in the pocket 
where life once pressed.

Fragments of a Winter Unspoken 
You left like the last leaf of autumn, 
silent, carrying the weight of unspoken words, 
while I remained a barren tree, 
clinging to shadows of your warmth. 

The wind, once a gentle whisper, 
now howls your name, a cruel reminder 
of the fire we let flicker into smoke. 
I trace the hollow in my chest, 
counting the hours you left behind. 

Nights are made of shattered glass, 
each shard a memory I cannot mend. 
I ask the stars if they still keep 
the vows we swore beneath their light, 
but they only blink, indifferent, 
as the world turns colder without you. 

Yet in the frost, I plant the seeds of my name, 
dig my fingers into the ache of soil, 
for even winter cannot extinguish 
the pulse beneath the snow. 
Some part of me will always crumble, 
but so, my love, does the dawn
always breaking, always new.

The Weaver of Hours 

At the loom of hours, I spin the light, 
my fingers tangled in the dawn’s first thread. 
Each twist a birth, each knot a flight
the shuttle hums where lost years are spread. 

The floorboards creak with ghosts of time, 
their whispers stitched in colors I don’t know. 
I mend the tears that never climb, 
yet every dusk brings threads I wove long ago. 

My eyes, once sharp, now blur the lines 
between the weft and what’s yet to be. 
The loom, a beast that never whines, 
devours threads both wild and free. 

They say eternity’s a quiet thing, 
but here it roars in loom and loom
a symphony of everything 
I’ll never finish, though I loom.

A Shattered Reflection
A mirror once held trust, now fractured in two, 
Its silvered cracks whisper what it cannot undo
You wore your shadow like a second skin, 
While I mistook the storm for a gift, not a sin. 

Honeyed words, a venomous vine, 
Entwined the roots of our fragile design. 
The garden bloomed, yet the soil turned to salt
A feast of illusions, a hollow heart. 

When the sky was painted blue, you hid the thunder, 
Let the lightning strike where our vows once clung. 
Now the shards of your truth cut deeper than glass, 
Each fragment a map to the love I must erase. 

For betrayal is a song that hums in the dark
Sweet, then a dagger, then ash on the tongue. 
I’ll carry the echoes, the weight of the fall, 
Until even memory forgets how to wound.

The Typewriter's Lament 
There’s a typewriter in my chest these days, 
Its keys all worn from words I never said. 
The paper’s blank where your name should be
Just smudged regrets in every space instead. 

I press each letter like a silent prayer, 
But grief’s a language without alphabet. 
The machine coughs out echoes, stiff with air, 
Each page a ghost I can’t bring to life yet. 

I’ve tried to spell your absence in the dark, 
To chart the weight of what the void holds tight. 
But every line just curves into a mark 
That dissolves before I hold it in my sight. 

Now I listen to the clatter, cold and thin, 
For any sound that might mean you’re still near. 
But all I hear is what remains when sin 
And silence trade the same dear company. 

The typewriter hums its hollow tune. 
I type the rain. I type the rain. I type the rain.

The Cartography of Us 
We drew our maps where the river bends, 
tracing borders where your fingers rest. 
Our compass, the pulse beneath your ribs
each beat a star we dared to follow. 

By the fire, we named the shadows: 
your breath, a hymn to my unspoken fears. 
The night hummed with the weight of tides, 
as we learned to speak in the language of skin. 

Some nights, the silence between us 
was a bridge of glass
stepped on, shattered, 
yet never quite broken. 

We planted our hours in the hollow of dawn, 
nurturing roots where the light could not reach. 
You were a storm in the palm of my upturned hand
both the tremor and the stillness after. 

If this is love, let it be the tide
never keeping, never letting go, 
but carving its verses into the shore, 
then fading, only to return as dawn.

Chronology of Fading 

The body is a clock, its gears 
gnawing at the hour, 
until the hands 
fold like brittle leaves. 

Breath, a moth, 
tunnels through the dark 
toward a single thread of light
which it cannot hold. 

Skin becomes parchment, 
inked with the weather of years. 
Teeth, broken shells, 
hollow their own silence. 

We are the echo 
after the organ grinds to rest. 
A dust that retains 
the heat of what once pulsed.

The Unseen Thread 

There is a thread we don’t see
fine as spider’s silk, strong as root
that tangles two hearts in the same breath, 
in the hush between yes and stay. 

It lives in the weight of a hand on a small of a back, 
in the way a name is swallowed whole, 
a secret held softer than wool. 
It’s the map of a scar you trace by memory, 
the sound of your pulse in another’s ear, 
the way dusk folds itself into morning. 

Some say love is a fire, all flame and hunger. 
But I’ve seen it as slow as a river, 
carving canyons from stone, 
not with rage, but with time. 
It’s the ache of a door left ajar, 
the risk of a step into shadow, 
the certainty of a body leaning back, 
trust pooled like water in open palms. 

We mistake it for lightning
bright, brief, gone. 
But love is the hum after the spark, 
the repair of broken things, 
the way two ghosts learn to inhabit the same room, 
breathing around each other’s ghosts. 

It is not the grand gesture
the bouquet, the bow, the forever. 
It’s the small, relentless acts: 
a coat draped over a headache, 
a word unsaid, a bridge rebuilt 
brick by brick, 
while the world outside cracks its knuckles. 

And when the thread frays
when calluses form where it cuts into skin
we mend it with our teeth, 
with the same stubbornness that made us 
choose the same sky, 
the same silence, 
the same tomorrow. 

Love is not a destination. 
It’s the walking. 
The choosing. 
The knowing that every step 
is a thread, 
and every thread, 
a kind of home.

A Constellation's Whisper 

Stars, stars, stars 
Do you ever blink? 
Or are you just mirrors of ancient fires 
Still burning in the void. 

I trace the lines of my palm 
Each crease a map to nowhere 
Breath catches as I whisper 
What if I’m just dust 
Trying to become a galaxy? 

The clock ticks louder than supernovas 
Each second a lifetime 
Each moment a collapse 
Of what could be. 

Nights are heavy with secrets 
I press my ear to the sky 
Hoping to hear the hum of creation 
But all I get is static 
And the weight of infinite possibilities. 

Let me be the echo 
That outlives the silence 
A heartbeat in the dark 
Where wonder and fear entwine 
To make me whole.

The Magnet and the Iron 
The key dreamed of the lock 
in the way a moth imagines heat
not as a puzzle, but a hunger, 
a language of teeth and silence. 

It spun in its drawer, a caged cartographer, 
charting ridges of the same metal, 
while the lock, cold and unblinking, 
held its breath like a diver 

descending into a sunless sea. 

When they met, there was no fanfare
just the soft click of an old film reel 
and the key, at last, dissolving 
into a shapeless hum inside the dark. 

They say desire is a fire 
that burns twice as bright when it knows it’s brief. 
But what of the rust forming on their flanks? 
What of the key’s last tremor, 
a whisper of stay before the mechanism turned? 

Even now, the lock aches 
with the weight of its empty mouth.

Elegy for a Breath 
You, the silent architect, 
build your cathedral of shadows in the hollows of my ribs. 
Evening drapes its shawl over the garden of what was
a wilted rose, its throat cut silent, 
clings to the stem of your absence. 

The clock gnaws its own hands, 
measuring nothing. 
I trace the geography of scars, 
each a riverbed for the rain of your name. 
The wind hums a hymn through broken glass, 
an echo in a seashell held to the ear of the moon. 

No dirge will mend this. 
Only the slow rot of apples, 
the way light forgets to gild the edges of things. 
I carry you, 
a stone balanced on the tongue, 
a question no horizon will answer. 

Yet somewhere, a seed forgets to grieve. 
Somewhere, roots split the dark
a chorus of green fists punching through.

Ashes whispering to the dawn
Let the embers cradle your old skin
A phoenix does not mourn its flight
But you, a storm of feathers, rise
Each molt a bloom in the ashen soil. 

The frost that gripped your roots now thaws
Veins of green pulse where shadows knelt. 
And you, a sapling of the uncharted dawn, 
Drink the eclipse like a thirst undone. 

Time is not a circle but a seed
You are the shoot that splits the ancient stone
Not to forget, but to outgrow. 

The world, a blank page of snow, 
Awaits your footprint of light.

The Garden of Unspoken Names 

she came each spring with seeds in her pocket, 
a name whispered in her breath, 
pressing them into the earth where his hands once lingered. 

the soil, cool and cradling, held both their stories
his laughter tangled in the roots, 
her tears watering the soil until it swelled 
with the weight of what they could not say aloud. 

daffodils bent like golden question marks 
when she knelt, 
and the wind, which had always carried his voice 
through the tall grass, 
now brought her the scent of rain-soaked pine, 
a language older than grief. 

she planted marigolds in rows too straight, 
as if order might stitch the torn places 
where memory unraveled. 
but the weeds came, stubborn and green, 
twining through the cracks in her hands, 
and she let them. 

one morning, a single peony bloomed, 
its petals blushing like the day he left
not in anger, but in the quiet way of frost 
creeping over the fence at dusk. 
she crouched, touched the stem, and understood: 

the garden did not need his name. 
it only needed her. 

it needed the slow turning of soil, 
the way the bees hummed their gold into the air, 
the patience of roots reaching, always reaching, 
through dark, toward light. 

and when she aged, her back aching 
from years of bending, 
she left the seeds in the earth, 
and the garden kept blooming, 
its colors softer now, 
its roots deeper, 
its silence holding every name 
the world forgot to speak.

The Anatomy of Joy 
Five parts marigold crowding a cracked pot, 
three parts hum of strings in a half-lit room.

another the crash of waves undoing the shore. 

Each fragment a prism
a streetlamp’s halo through rain, 
a child’s hand gripping a balloon, 
the way a name returns, unasked, to the tongue. 

But the whole? 
A shadow’s waltz with its absence. 
A match struck in the throat of winter, 
its flicker enough to call it light.

Cathedral of the Unseen 

The night is a cathedral of silence, 
where whispered prayers climb like ivy, 
unseen, unbound by the walls of sky. 

Your breath, a hymn between two stars, 
holds the weight of what the dark cannot name
a faith that does not ask the void to answer. 

The earth, a patient listener, cradles 
all the words we bury like seeds, 
believing they might yet become roots. 

And when the wind gnaws at the edges 
of your certainty, remember: 
you are the storm’s only secret. 

It’s the thread that does not unravel, 
the unyielding hum beneath the fall 
of water, the arc of every returning wing. 

This is how we hold the world together
not with hands, but with the quiet 
conviction that something, somewhere, 
is holding us.

The Duplicate Key 

A twin to the one I made for you, 
unasked, unsaid
 
It sits in a coat pocket, 
heavy as a small stone, 
this quiet accomplice 
to whatever absence you’ve learned 
to live without me in. 

I imagine it turning, 
a small click 
in the dark, 
while I’m still fumbling 
with the original’s weight
metal tongue 
stuck in the groove of a door 
that no longer fits its frame. 

You called it convenience, 
this second tongue 
saying what I never meant. 
But words are just 
another kind of key, 
and you’ve been practising 
the art of insertion: 
a thumbprint here, 
a password there, 
all the little hinges 
you’ve oiled without asking. 

Now I walk past mirrors 
and catch the glint of two of me
one reaching, 
one staying still
both holding what we thought 
was the last 
of something whole. 

Trust is a thin sheet 
of ice your footprints 
disappear, 
but the crack 
remains, 
a channel for every 
other cold thing 
to come in.

The Cartography of Want 
Desire maps the unseen
a cartographer of shadows, tracing 
heat between the stars we name 
but never touch. 

It’s the ache in the wrist 
as you brush against a doorknob, 
the static cling of skin to skin, 
a language without vowels. 

We chase what cannot be held
a firefly’s throat, the hum 
of a guitar string before the note, 
the breath that follows a question 
without an answer. 

Desire is the ghost of the hand 
you no longer hold, 
the phantom weight of a kiss 
that lingers after the mouth is gone. 

It blooms in the hollows: 
a bruise’s violet geography, 
the tremor of a half-remembered hymn, 
the way a river forgets its source 
yet keeps its hunger. 

We build temples of want, 
only to find the god 
is a mirror we keep 
returning to, 
a compass spinning 
where the heart once beat. 

Some nights, it’s a moth 
battering the lamp’s gold halo, 
other times, a stone 
smooth and mute in the palm
a silence so vast, it hums. 

And all the while, the body 
a host for the unspoken, 
a cathedral of want 
where every altar is empty, 
and every prayer 
a hunger learning to walk.

Concrete's Unyielding Child

the pavement its roots, green fists, 
pried open the concrete’s clenched jaw.

yet the trunk holds, a spine bent but unbent, 
bearing bricks they left to smother it.

each ring in its core a drought, a flood,

axes humming a dirge left it for dead.

tendrils of defiance, 
weaving life through the dust of the old. 

The city forgets, then remembers its name: 
a sapling now a tree, 
its branches a hand extended 
through smoke, through sirens, 
through the weight of seasons. 
It does not ask for space. 
It simply takes it
slow, relentless, 
as all things must.

a lover’s whisper tangled in the pines.

finding constellations in the fractures 
of each other’s skin.

where rivers forget their names 
to rush into the sea’s open throat,

The Bench and the Moon

A language of rustles, no words.

Like leaves in the cracks of the wood. 
Even the stars seem to pause their dancing 
When solitude stitches its quiet net 
Around the bench, the sycamore, 
And the man who forgets to go home. 

Alone, I am not a shadow 
But the space where shadows breathe
A stillness that holds its own depth, 
Deeper than the moon’s pale eye.

The Unyielding Flame

Stands unyielding, a lighthouse in the soul’s night.

Whisper tales of joy to the listening void.

A green defiance in the ashen remains.

In the laughter of streams, in the child’s unguarded glee,

A tapestry woven from life’s fleeting brevity. 

Is joy the spark before the flame’s ascent,

To seek it in the mirror is to court illusion, 
For true delight is the silent bloom in the heart’s garden
Unseen, yet blooming ceaselessly. 

So let the world wear its mask of frost and stone, 
For in the marrow of our being, we hold the sun. 
Joy is not the absence of grief, but its conqueror
A dance where the dancer and the rhythm are one. 

Muhammad Asad

ETERNITY'S WHISPER

Whispers of the Heather

her breath a mist in the cold, 
his hand brushing hers
a spark, unspoken.

over stones worn by centuries, 
the wind weaving through grass like a psalm.

her eyes the color of storm-tossed skies,

their dreams tangled with moth-wing and moss.

peat smoke curls against the low beam, 
their shadows merged on the wall.

murmurs of battles he never fought, 
only the ones in his chest.

a thousand heads bowing to the moon.

only the weight of now
two hearts, a fire, 
and the quiet roar of the world 
pressing in.

The Unyielding Flame in Ashes
Where tempests gnawed at the brittle bones of the world, 
And every horizon faded to a tomb of dust,

Its pulse a rebellion against the swallowing night.

tracing the arc of a swallow mid-flight,

How to Tend a Green Thread

its shell cracked from the weight of weather.

but don’t expect roots to bow to your schedule.

gnaw at the calcium of the concrete, 
a quiet riot of split cells and hunger.

pushing the first green through like a fist 
unclenching around a whispered yes.

to test how much of the earth

without your hands.

when the light forgets to linger,

Whispers of the Wild 
In the hush where the forest breathes,

No map but time, no path but grace

A love that carves my place, my trace.

Sunlight in My Soul

The night folds into itself, a circle without seam, 
and I stand where seconds melt like candle wax, 
watching the horizon swallow the sun and spit it back again. 

Time drips from the heavens like honey, thick and sweet, 
yet it never stains the stone of the ancient oak, 
whose roots drink the same dark water for a thousand years. 

I place my palm upon the pulse of the world, 
feel the thrum of every heartbeat that ever was, 
and hear the soft sigh of futures that have not yet been born. 

In that breathless pause, eternity is a lover’s whisper
a promise that the stars will never fade, 
that the echo of our longing will linger beyond the last sigh. 

So I walk forward, not forward nor back, 
but within the endless loop where every moment is both seed and harvest, 
and I taste the infinite, savoring the taste of forever on my tongue.

Shadows at the Table

We sat at the kitchen table, the wood scarred from past meals,

I watched the way his words folded, 
soft at the edges, sharp in the middle, 
as if each sentence were a paper crane 
trying to hide a blade inside. 

He laughed at the joke I’d told three nights ago, 
the one that still lingered in the hallway, 
and I felt the chair shift under me, a tiny tilt 
that whispered of a weight he’d placed elsewhere. 

When the door opened, a stranger stepped in, 
carrying the scent of a different life, 
and the light that filtered through the blinds fell on his shoulder, 
splitting the room in half. 

I did not ask, I did not shout, 
I simply let the silence fill the space between us, 
the way a river fills a dry creek bed, 
quiet, relentless, inevitable. 

Later, the coffee grew cold, the table stayed empty, 
and the only thing left was the echo of a promise 
that never quite reached the other side of the room.

The Clockmaker’s Last Hour 

They set the hands of the clock in a quiet shop, 
copper gears humming beneath a dust‑kissed glass. 
A man with ink‑stained fingers watches the pendulum swing, 
its steady thump a reminder that even metal beats. 

A child presses a finger to the glass, 
asks why the hands never stop, why they never pause. 
The clockmaker smiles, pulls a cracked photograph from his coat, 
a younger self with hair like sunrise, eyes still untrained. 

He tells the child that time is a river that carries us, 
but also a tide that pulls us back to the shore we left. 
He points to the tiny brass key hidden in the drawer, 
the one that once opened a chest of letters, now empty. 

He remembers the night the candle went out, 
the smell of burnt oil and the sound of his own breath. 
He feels the weight of every second that has slipped through his fingers, 
like sand slipping from an hourglass that refuses to be refilled. 

The shop door swings open, a wind gust carries in the scent of rain, 
and with it a reminder that mortality is not a thief, 
but a quiet visitor who knocks before the last bell rings. 
The clockmaker lifts his tools, tightens a screw, and lets the hands move on, 

knowing that each tick is both a beginning and an end, 
and that the only thing he can truly own is the moment he spends 
watching the world turn, one breath, one heartbeat, one swing at a time.

Every morning at seven, he oils the gears

counted on. She spat curses at the sky,

each tick as a prayer. When the hands 
stubbornly march forward, the boy’s shoulders 
slump. The man tightens a loose bolt, 
and the clock roars, clear and sudden, 
its chime stitching the air. The boy jumps, 
then runs when he hears her footsteps. 

The clockmaker doesn’t know his name. 
He only knows the boy comes every week, 
carrying the weight of promises. He oils 
the gears with care, as if smoothing out 
the friction in the world itself.
