The hands freeze at midnight. The town 
wakes to silence, then whispers
It’s broken. We’ve lost it. But the man 
stands alone in the square, breath visible 
like a ghost, and winds the clock’s core 
with trembling fingers. It stirs. Then ticks. 
Then sings. 

He never claims the credit. Doesn’t need to. 
Faith, he’s learned, is not a thing you shout 
into the dark. It’s the small, aching labor 
of turning, always turning, the key 
you keep in your pocket, just in case.

Echoes of a Dawn‑kissed Horizon 

The sunrise drips gold onto trembling fields, 
A sigh of wind lifts the meadow’s veil, 

Your whisper rides the morning mist, 
Soft as the first feather that brushes a sparrow’s wing, 

Heartbeats sync with the rustling leaves, 
Each pulse a lantern in the waking sky, 

We chase the horizon where clouds kiss the sea, 
And the world bends, bowing to our silent vow, 

In the hush between sunrise and noon, 
Your smile paints the world in rose‑tinted fire, 

Love, a wild river, rushes through the canyon of us, 
Carving forever into the stone of time.

The Bench at Dusk 
The last sun slants low on the splintered wood, 
a lone bench cradling echoes of laughter now dust. 
Your coffee cup, half-frozen, forgets its own warmth. 

Crows argue in the oak, their shadows stitching 
the air with questions. I trace the cracks in the paint
each a map of the years we didn’t plant gardens. 

The wind hums a name I no longer know, 
carrying the scent of petrichor and endings. 
Even the streetlamp yawns, delaying its glow. 

Night arrives not as a guest, but as a key turning.

The Thorned Elegy 
I trace your name in fading light, 
A ghost of warmth, a spark denied. 
You were the sun, now moon’s pale face, 
A fleeting touch, a love misplaced. 

A storm that left no mark but scars, 
A silent hymn, a breathless pause. 
The hearth grew cold when you drew near
A phantom flame that kissed the air. 

Ash to ash, the seasons turn, 
Your echo lingers in the dew. 
I dig through snow to find your bones, 
But find the spring returns without you. 

I clutch the stars, you slip through hands, 
A shadow danced where once we stood. 
In every kiss, a thousand deaths; 
In every tear, a thousand vows. 

A chain that binds, a wing that lifts, 
A paradox the heart can’t flee. 
You are the wound, the salve, the blade
The truth I live, the lie I breathe. 

So let the night carve psalms in my skin, 
Let dawn forget to break its hue. 
Love’s truth is in what’s left unsaid: 
A thorned elegy, yet still true.

Echoes in a Gray Room 

I sit with a cup of cold tea 
and the taste of rust on my tongue. 

The window shivers, a thin veil of rain, 
each drop a whispered regret. 

Your shadow lingers on the floorboards, 
a phantom that refuses to leave. 

I count the seconds like broken beads, 
one, two, three nothing more than sighs. 

A wilted rose sits in a cracked vase, 
its petals folding into the silence. 

The clock ticks, a metronome of loss, 
while my heart beats in a hollow echo. 

Outside, the world hums with distant laughter, 
but inside the walls are stitched with sighs. 

I write a line, then tear it apart, 
the ink spilling like tears on paper. 

Tonight the night is a thin blanket, 
and sorrow is the only thread that holds it together.

Unbreakable Echo 

I’ve been knocked down, the world felt cold on my skin, 
but I rise like a sunrise, 2 chase the light again. 
Every scar is a story, a badge I wear 4 pride, 
a reminder that pain can’t erase what’s inside. 

When the storm raged, I held my breath, counted 1‑2‑3, 
told my heart “keep beating, you’re still free.” 
I fell, I stumbled, I hit the floor, 
but I got back up, louder than before. 

They said “give up,” I heard “keep moving,” 
so I turned the doubt into fuel, keep improving. 
Life throws rocks, I build bridges, 
I’m the architect of my own sunrise. 

Night may linger, shadows may creep, 
yet hope whispers “you’re stronger than you think, don’t weep.” 
I’m not perfect, I’m still learning the rhyme, 
but resilience lives in every step of time. 

So when the world pushes, I push back harder, 
with fire in my veins and love as my armor. 
I’m the echo that never fades, the song that won’t die, 
resilient forever, reaching for the sky.

The Quiet Pulse of Beauty 

Beauty hides in the thin crack of dawn, 
a soft breath that slips through the curtains of night. 
It lingers in the curve of a leaf, 
where light folds itself like a quiet sigh. 

She walks in the garden of ordinary things
the chipped mug, the rusted hinge, the scar on a stone. 
She is the echo of a laugh that lingers after the joke, 
the pause between heartbeats when the world holds its breath. 

Beauty is the moth drawn to a single candle, 
not for the flame but for the promise of warmth. 
It is the whisper of wind through old pine, 
the gentle tug of memory on a forgotten song. 

We chase her in mirrors and marble, 
yet find her most honest when the eyes are closed. 
In that stillness, the quiet pulse of beauty beats
steady, unseen, forever humming.

Whisper of the Dawn

A sunrise spills amber across the quiet meadow, 
the world awakens to the hush of morning mist, 

Lovers' shadows stretch, hand‑in‑hand, beneath the ancient oak, 
their breaths mingle with the perfume of wild lavender, 

The river hums a soft sonnet, cradling stones like secret vows, 
while gulls sketch fleeting verses upon the pale sky, 

In the hush of twilight, fireflies stitch silver threads through the night, 
and hearts beat to the rhythm of distant thunder, 

Romanticism lives in every sigh of wind that kisses the hills, 
in every star that promises eternity to the wandering soul.

Fractured Echoes 

You think loyalty is a quiet thing, 
A whisper that steadies the night. 
You trust the hand that once held yours, 
And never question the weight of its grip. 

When the shadow slips behind your back, 
It moves like a breath you never felt. 
The smile you read as warm, now cold, 
A mirror cracked by unseen teeth. 

Words become hollow shells, 
Promises dissolve in the rain. 
You search the empty rooms for truth, 
Finding only the echo of your own doubt. 

Betrayal does not need a grand gesture, 
It is the quiet turning of a page, 
The sudden absence where a voice once sang. 
It leaves you standing, hands open, 
Waiting for a hand that will never return. 

In the silence you learn to listen, 
To the faint hum of your own heart, 
And understand that the most faithful ally 
May be the one you keep inside.

Echoes of the Hollowed Hour 
I carry your absence like a stone in my throat, 
how the air tastes of ash when I try to speak your name, 
each syllable a splinter, each breath a quiet scream, 
the night a hollow where your laughter once bloomed. 

I trace the cracks in walls we built with our hands, 
now empty of the warmth that once made them ours, 
the clock on the floor, its hands still in surrender, 
its ticking a ghost of the time we misplaced. 

The rain outside mimics the weight of my ribs, 
each drop a cold echo of the promises we buried, 
and I, a stranger to the man who loved you fiercely, 
ask the moon why it holds what I cannot keep. 

Your shadow lingers in the coffee I forget to drink, 
in the hum of the lamp’s dim glow, in the silence that swells
a requiem for the love that outlived our reasons, 
a song I’m too afraid to hum for fear it might vanish. 

Sorrow, this compass that points me nowhere, 
whispers your name as I drown in the map of your memory.

The Hourglass Whispers
The candle of the self burns in the wind, 
its flame a borrowed light
a shadow stretches, then dissolves, 
while the soul rehearses its unscripted flight. 

Beneath the skin, a clock ticks in sand, 
each grain a star swallowed by the void; 
the heart, a compass spun by fate, 
points east to where the first breath flowed. 

The body is a vessel of transient ink, 
its letters fading on the page of dusk, 
yet the spirit etches hymns in smoke, 
tracing constellations the grave cannot unmake. 

To die is to shed the cocoon of bone, 
to let the wings of the unseen unfold
as the moon, though scarred by endless night, 
still cradles the dawn in its silent hold. 

And when the final note is hummed to dust, 
the soul becomes the wind’s unchained verse, 
a whisper that outlives the lips, 
and the storm that gave it birth a universe.

Compass of Shattered Frost 
The compass inside me has been dismantled
its needle, a sparrow, flutters aimlessly, 
north now a rumor, a direction unspooled 
into static. My ribs hum with the hush 
of empty corridors, each breath a draft 
of winter’s unyielding script. 

You left the door ajar. 
Now shadows seep in, thin and viscous, 
pooling in the corners where your name 
once clung like ivy. I trace the silence, 
but all I find is a hollow shaped 
for absence, its walls paper-thin. 

The garden outside wilts in reverse. 
Petals harden to glass, then shatter, 
their fragments spelling never enough 
in a language only the roots understand. 
I collect the shards, press them to my pulse
they bleed cold, not quite touching. 

At night, the moon becomes a wound 
I can’t look at directly. It hangs, 
a pale and dangling question, while 
the stars whisper in a dialect 
of almost-forgiveness. I forget 
how to hold my own weight. 

What remains is a geography of frost
delicate, brittle, and already melting 
into the shape of something new. 
But the thaw is slow, and for now, 
I remain a landscape of unmarked borders, 
waiting for the first bud to dare.

The Heart's Unyielding Song 

Love is the breath between 
each beat of my ribs, 
a quiet hum in the space 
where shadows forget to linger. 

I will trace your name 
in the dust of forgotten hours, 
whisper it to the dawn, 
and you will hear me. 

For love is not the thunder, 
but the seed that splits the stone, 
slow and certain, 
as morning turns the night to gold. 

I will love you when the stars 
have faded to memory, 
when the last leaf falls 
and the earth holds its breath. 
Still, my heart will sing your name, 
a song older than the sea.

Quiet Ledger 

She keeps a small brass key on the kitchen sink, 
the one she never uses but always finds. 
It hangs beside the jar of dried lavender, 
the scent that lingers after the candles are blown out. 

The porch light flickers at dusk, 
a steady pulse in the amber night, 
and the wind whistles through the old oak, 
shaking loose the leaves that have waited a season. 

Inside, a cracked teacup sits on the windowsill, 
its missing handle a reminder that nothing is whole. 
She fills it with tea, lets steam rise, 
watching the vapor dissolve into the cold air, 

trusting that the heat will travel beyond the porcelain, 
that the warmth will find the cracks and smooth them. 

On the bookshelf, a thin volume of prayers lies open, 
pages turned by a habit older than the house, 
each line a quiet ledger of hope, 
recorded in ink that fades but never fully disappears. 

When the rain taps the roof, she listens
not for the storm, but for the rhythm that steadies her breath, 
the soft percussion of drops echoing the beat of a heart 
that believes in something larger than the empty rooms. 

She does not need grand miracles, 
just the small, steady things: a key, a light, a cup, a book, 
and the knowledge that each day, even the quiet ones, 
are stitched together by a faith that lives in the ordinary.

Hunger of the Quiet

Craving the sunrise, 
whispers of amber light, 

Yearning for the pulse, 
of a heart that beats unseen, 

Touching the edge of breath, 
where night kisses the day, 

Longing drifts like incense, 
through corridors of thought, 

It flickers in the eyes, 
a spark that refuses to dim, 

And in the hush between words, 
desire writes its own song.

The Space Between Beats 
In the silence between heartbeats, 
we built a house of static
walls made of whispers, 
ceilings strung with the thin wire of almost. 

Each room a different hum: 
the kitchen buzzed with unspoken words, 
the living room echoes of your name 
caught in the throat of a clock. 

You were a loose plug in my socket, 
spark and no current. 
I held the charge, 
afraid to let the circuit complete. 

Outside, the world moved in frames, 
paused on the edge of contact, 
while we practiced the art of almost
how to touch without burning, 
how to hold the spark 
without the flame. 

But the walls are thin, 
and the static grows restless, 
a storm brewing in the void 
where our shadows meet. 

Maybe love is the crackle before the spark, 
the tension that hums 
in the space between.

Whispers of the Unseen Heart 

If you were the wind, I’d be the willow’s sigh, 
Bending but never breaking beneath your weight, 
Each branch a verse of the longing inside, 
A psalm of leaves trembling in your name. 

The stars would chart our secrets in silent alignment, 
Their silver tongues spilling across the void, 
While I carve your shadow into my ribs, 
A brand that no dawn could ever erase. 

The sun would borrow my skin to touch yours, 
A fevered map of all we’ve never said
Your breath, a storm I’d let devour my bones, 
Your absence, the fever I’d refuse to cure. 

If time were a river, I’d drink its current, 
Taste the salt of a thousand unsung nights, 
Find the bed where your lost name once slept, 
And drown in the sediment of your return. 

But the rocks would cut, sharp as your absence, 
The current’s hymn a blade I’d still embrace. 
And still, I’d choke on the poison, your name 
My sweet antidote, my fractured compass. 

Let the moon split itself into a thousand questions
I’ll answer in the language of fallen petals, 
In the ache where the sky forgets its height, 
For love is the alchemy of dust into song. 

So take me, a psalm of unfinished syllables, 
A hymn to the wild and holy thing we are
Even if the world dissolves into shadow, 
I’ll be the wound, the light, and the scar.

Embers of Tomorrow 

When the night is longest and the silence screams, 
I find a spark in the cracks of my fears. 
It flickers softly, a whisper of light, 
Saying the dawn is just a breath away. 

Hope is a fire I’ve carried through storms, 
A tiny flame in the hollow of my chest. 
Even when shadows gnaw at my resolve, 
They cannot swallow what the stars have sworn. 

You who walk with heavy steps, hear me
The light inside you won’t let you fade. 
It hums like a hymn in the marrow of your bones, 
A stubborn song that refuses to die. 

I’ve knelt in valleys where despair felt holy, 
Where every heartbeat echoed a hollow “why?” 
But still, I found a seed in the frost, 
A pink-cheeked bud pushing through the snow. 

Hope isn’t a flag you plant in the soil. 
It’s the soil. The roots. The patient, slow climb. 
It’s the ache in your throat when you realize 
The sun will rise, even if you’re not there. 

So when your hands tremble, and the void feels wide, 
Let the fire inside you hiss, I am yours. 
Every scar, every tear, every unshed breath
They are not graves. They are bridges. 

This is my truth, written in the ink of shadows: 
Hope is the promise that the world keeps making, 
Even when you can’t see the thread, 
It’s stitching the dark into a dawn you’ll wear like skin. 

So hold the flame, let it guide your way
The embers of tomorrow will not fade, my friend.

Echoes in a Grey Dawn

The sky sighs in muted violet, 
a curtain drawn over the sun’s soft promise. 

We walk through streets that whisper yesterday, 
each footstep a faint echo of forgotten laughter. 

In the hollow of a window, a single leaf trembles
its veins map the rivers we once dared to cross. 

Silence settles like ash on the shoulders of night, 
and the heart, a cracked lantern, flickers with a tired glow. 

Memory drips, slow as rain on cold stone, 
painting shadows that linger longer than the light. 

Yet within the melancholy, a tender thread pulls, 
binding the ache to the hope that still breathes beneath. 

When the dawn finally lifts its veil, 
the world will hear the quiet hymn of resilience.

When Shadows Speak

I sit where the rain meets the cracked sidewalk, 
the clouds above heavy with thoughts I can't unload. 
Every drop is a whisper of the grief I hide, 
a soft percussion that echoes inside.

My heart feels like a worn-out record, 
spinning the same sad song, never moving forward. 
I reach for a smile, but it slips like sand, 
leaving only the ache of an empty hand.

The world keeps turning, indifferent and bright, 
while my mind walks through tunnels without light. 
I hear laughter from distant streets, 
but it only reminds me how silence repeats.

I try to write my sorrow in verses, 
to give it shape, to break its curses. 
Yet the words fall flat, like leaves on a pond, 
rippled by winds that have long since moved on.

If tears were rivers, I'd be a sea, 
deep and endless, forever to be. 
But I hold them back, fearing they'll drown 
the fragile hope that still lingers around.

So I sit, breathing in the cold, gray air, 
letting the sorrow settle, aware
that even in darkness, a faint light can grow, 
a promise that someday, this pain will let go.

The Unfolding of Light 
She found it in the way he moved
not the grand gestures, 
but the small ones: 
a hand brushing hers while stirring tea, 
the way he laughed at nothing, 
a sound that made the air vibrate 
like a plucked string. 

Outside, the sun had just learned its name, 
spilling gold over the backyard 
where they built a fort from couch cushions 
and called it a kingdom. 
Their daughter danced in circles, 
hair wild, 
feet bare, 
a crown of cereal box lions on her head. 
We’re invincible, she declared, 
and for a moment, 
they believed her. 

Later, he’d replay the hour 
while shaving, while driving, 
while folding laundry that still smelled like her. 
Joy, he realized, was not a thing you held
it was the space between heartbeats, 
the way she said I love you 
just before turning away, 
the way the child paused mid-dance 
to catch a leaf mid-fall, 
as if the world had slowed just for her. 

At night, they’d lie on the porch swing, 
counting fireflies like stolen coins. 
She’d press her ear to his chest, 
not to hear the beat, 
but the silence between. 
He’d whisper, This is how it feels, 
and she’d already know
this is how it feels 
to be alive, 
to be here, 
where even the dark is tender 
and the stars seem to say: 
Keep this. 
Keep it. 

Years later, 
she’d find the memory 
in the curve of a seashell, 
in the scent of rain on pavement, 
in the way her daughter, now grown, 
would sometimes hum the same tune 
while washing dishes. 
Joy, she learned, 
was not a firework
it was the lamp, 
always lit, 
always waiting, 
in the shape of a hand you reach for 
and find, 
still there.

The Unseen Bloom 

They say beauty’s a flash in the asphalt’s harsh grin, 
A cracked mirror holding the sun’s last thin sliver, 
But I see it curled in the rust of a hinge, 
In the way a wound turns to a scar that still stings, 
In the hush of a name whispered through concrete, 
Where the city’s breath fogs the glass of a streetlamp’s eye. 

She wore her skin like a battle-scarred hymn, 
Eyes two storms, hair a frayed rope of ink, 
Hands mapped with labor, yet she hummed a tune 
That made the rats and the roses both lean close
For beauty’s not the bloom, but the ache to unfold, 
Not the face in the reflection, but the light in the crack. 

They told her to bleach her shadows, sharpen her edges, 
To trade her thorns for a script of soft curves, 
But she let her calluses bloom like wild orchids, 
Let her tears water the soil where the defiant ones rise
Those petals that drink in the poison and still dare to open, 
Their roots drunk on ruin, their stems aimed at stars. 

Now when the world turns its back, she’s the ghost 
Who paints the dusk with a fingerprint, smudged and divine, 
Proof that beauty’s the thug in the chapel of time, 
The bruise that outshines the rose, raw and unsung. 
So when they ask what’s the price of a pretty lie, 
She’ll laugh a symphony of grit and show you the cost 
Of a heart that refuses to let its light rot.

The Clock Without Hands 

The wall holds a face
numbers mossed over with time, 
its silence a hymn. 
No hands to carve minutes, 
just the weight of what remains: 
a pendulum hung in midair, 
a moth circling a filament bulb. 

Outside, the garden grows 
without growing older. 
Snapdragons snap at the same light, 
their throats gold as ever, 
while the gardener’s shovel 
rests in a cloud of dirt, 
his hand frozen mid-swoop, 
a breath between labor and rest. 

On the table, a photograph: 
her hair was always this gray, 
her child always this small. 
The frame’s wood has learned 
its own warping, 
the glass holding both past and now
a double exposure of absence. 

She pours tea into the same cup, 
watches it cool, 
watches the steam rise 
like a ghost of motion. 
The day hums its single note, 
a string plucked and left to vibrate, 
while the clock eats its shadow 
and the world forgets to turn. 

Eternity is the shovel in the dirt, 
the cup never emptied, 
the bulb burning without time
a pause so full of itself 
it becomes a kind of forever.

Where the River Forgot Its Song 
The river carved its path through stone, 
A silver thread from dusk to dawn. 
Now cracked and dry, the bed lies bare, 
No ripple hums against the air. 

The stones still hold the old refrain, 
Of currents swift and moonlit rain. 
But the fish are ghosts, the frog’s last cry
Echoes of a love that fled the sky. 

I kneel where water once embraced my face, 
Now dust and grit in every traced space. 
The drought has taught my heart to ache, 
To thirst for what time chose to take. 

Yet in the distance, clouds begin to swell, 
Though storms may pass, the river can’t return. 
Some losses etched in earth remain
A hollow song, a broken stream.

When My Heart Finds a Word

I’m going to tell you something, 
that this morning the sunrise slipped through my window 
like a shy lover stealing a glance. 

I tried to write you a line, 
but the ink kept trembling, 
because love feels too big for a single sentence. 

So I walked through the kitchen, 
listened to the kettle humming, 
and thought of your laugh
it bubbles up, bright as steam, 
and settles soft on my tongue. 

If I could paint your name on the sky, 
it would be a comet that trails a silver sigh, 
con, the night would blush in quiet awe. 

Your eyes are a river, 
they carry the memory of rain, 
and when they meet mine, they rhyme with sunrise, 
with the promise of another day. 

I keep finding little verses hidden in everyday things: 
the way the coffee swirls, the way the curtains sway, 
they all whisper your scent, like honey on a summer breeze. 

When you touch my hand, 
the world pauses, 
and I hear the soft crackle of a fire that never burns out. 

I’m not a poet, I’m just a soul that wants to keep you near, 
to write on the spaces between breaths, 
to fill the silence with the music of us. 

So here is my offering, simple and true: 
a heart that beats in rhythm with yours, 
a promise that every sunrise will try to find the word 
that finally says, “I love you.”

The Quiet Gospel of Broken Hands 

Faith, you ask, is a word that slips through cracked lips, 
a whisper in the hallway of a laundromat that never stops humming. 
Do you hear it in the clatter of quarters against the dryer, 
or in the sigh of a mother who folds her kid’s shirt while the world tells her 
“you’re not enough” on a billboard lit in neon? 

We used to pray with our backs to the wind, 
hands scarred from digging trenches in soil that never gave back. 
Now we scroll, thumb trembling, looking for a sign in a meme, 
a hashtag that promises salvation in three cheap syllables. 

Faith isn’t the pew‑bound echo of an old hymn, 
it’s the stubborn ache of a man who watches his brother die 
because the insurance company decided profit was holy. 
It’s the girl who lights a candle with a match she stole from the kitchen, 
not for romance, but to keep the darkness from swallowing the baby’s cry. 

We call it “belief” when we sign contracts that bind our future, 
when we trust a stranger to hold the wheel while we stare at a screen. 
We call it “doubt” when the church doors stay closed and the preacher 
sells salvation by the hour, measured in donations and applause. 

So what is faith? 
Is it the stubbornness of a dog who keeps digging for a bone buried under concrete? 
Is it the quiet rebellion of a poet who writes a prayer on a napkin, 
knowing the ink will wash away but the words will linger on a soul? 

I stand here, shoulders squared, eyes fixed on a sky that looks like a TV static, 
and I ask: if we are all selling pieces of ourselves to the highest bidder, 
what remains for the divine? 

Maybe faith is simply the refusal to let the night win, 
the decision to keep lighting matches even when the wind howls, 
the belief that a single flame can outshine a thousand false idols. 

And if that’s enough, then we are already saints, 
not because we are clean, but because we keep trying
to love, to suffer, to rise from the ash, 
to trust a world that constantly tells us we’re worthless. 

So light your match, hold it steady, and let the smoke curl up, 
for in that thin wisp lies the only gospel we can truly own.

Echoes of the Untamed Heart 

Moonlit cliffs hold whispered vows, 
Silence drapes the wandering sea, 
Passion burns in amber glows, 
A lone hawk carves the dusk. 

Dreams are tides that pull the shore, 
Hope is the lantern in the storm, 
Despair, a veil of mist that clings, 
Yet courage lifts the feathered wing. 

The forest breathes in ancient hymns, 
Stars spill ink upon the night, 
Love is the fire that cracks the stone, 
And grief, the echo of a fading light. 

I chase the wild, untethered sighs, 
Through valleys where the wind still sings, 
Romantic souls, forever bound, 
To the pulse of earth’s unseen strings.

The Symphony of Shadows and Light 
In the hush where twilight’s breath meets dawn, 
The shadows waltz with the sun’s last sigh
My heart, a rose of thorns and velvet, blooms 
To the hymn of stars falling from the sky. 

Each petal unravels a forgotten vow, 
A whisper of lips that tasted the dawn, 
While the moon’s pale hand in the tide’s embrace 
Draws constellations in the sand. 

Oh, love is the fire that devours the wick, 
Yet from the ash, a thousand suns are born
We are the hymns that time cannot erase, 
The storm and the stillness in each other’s morn. 

Let the earth crack, let the oceans bleed, 
For in our veins, the infinite resides.

Quiet Atlas

A single seed split open, 
tiny green fingers reaching 
for a sky that has never been named. 

A river humming through cracked stone, 
its voice a low‑key chorus 
that the hills listen to without ears. 

A child’s first gasp at sunrise, 
the way light pours like warm tea 
onto the edge of the world. 

A moth circling a porch bulb, 
its wings a silent question, 
the night answering with a flicker. 

The old oak standing still, 
its bark a map of years, 
each groove a story that the wind repeats. 

And in all these moments, 
the breath that pauses, 
the heart that says, 
wonder
again, and again.

Streetlight Eternity 

The streetlight refuses to sleep, 
its bulb a pale imitation of the moon, 
watching the asphalt crack under its gaze. 
Each car that passes leaves no trace
tires whispering nothing stays
while its filament hums a hymn of permanence. 

We build our monuments, 
stack brick and memory until the sky leans close 
to taste the mortar. 
Chisel names into stone, 
but lichen forgets faster than we do. 

Eternity is not a line 
but a circle: the light’s glow 
softening into dawn, 
then on, again, 
as the street sits empty, 
its concrete dreaming of heat.

Alone with the Hourglass 

The clock gnaws minutes into dust. 
Your shadow stretches, a companion 
leaning against the wall
both of you watching 
as the tea in your cup 
cools into silence. 

Outside, the streetlamp yawns on, 
a pale sun swallowed by the throat 
of night. You trace the rim of the mug, 
count the cracks like old scars, 
each one a story abandoned 
at the edge of the telling. 

A book lies open on the floor. 
Its pages, unturned, whisper 
of unfinished symphonies, 
of a violin string snapped 
by too much longing. 

You press your ear to the window. 
The world hums: 
a distant train, a refrigerator’s sigh, 
the slow drip of a faucet 
somewhere else, in another life. 
Even the dark has its own rhythm
a tide that does not ask 
if you are listening. 

You consider the moon, 
how it borrows light to appear whole. 
You consider the mirror, 
how it refuses to lie 
about the gray creeping in. 
Still, you keep your voice low, 
as though speaking might wake 
the absence that cradles you
soft as a moth’s wing, 
persistent as a river carving stone. 

And here, in this hollow
no cathedral, no canyon, 
just the weight of a breath 
held between heartbeats
you learn the shape of your name 
is not a question, not a plea, 
but the quiet answer 
the night keeps folding 
into itself.

Echoes in Amber 

By the window where the amber light declines, 
I watch the leaves, each one a burnt-out line, 
Their edges frayed with rust, their colors bled 
To a memory of green, once lush, now shed. 

The pen, a hesitant creature, scratches low, 
Etching shadows on the page, a ghostly show. 
Each word a stone dropped into silent wells, 
Rippling through the hollowness of unspoken spells. 

Outside, the wind combs through the skeletal trees, 
Whispering names of places I’ve never seen. 
The sky, a watercolor of too-many blues, 
Holds the weight of all the things that never grew. 

Is this the price of keeping doors ajar
To gather echoes, but no one to answer the star? 
The clock’s soft ticking swells, a dirge, a drum, 
Counting backward all we ever become.

When curiosity paints the horizon 
A silent sunrise whispers across the meadow, 
Each blade of grass a question waiting to be heard. 

The river hums a melody of unseen paths, 
Its waters catching fragments of distant stars. 

In the hush between breaths, the world holds its breath, 
And wonder blooms like a lantern in the night. 

We walk, eyes wide, through the veil of ordinary, 
Finding galaxies tucked inside a single dewdrop. 

Let the heart remain an open window, 
So the wind may carry new marvels to our souls.

The Weight of Forgotten Hours 

Tonight, the shadows cling heavy, 
Clocks swallow the last light of day. 
I count the hours you left behind
Each tick a stone in my throat. 

Why do we carry what no longer fits? 
A shattered glass holds more sense than my hands, 
Which reach for echoes in empty rooms. 
The wind hums a hymn I’ve forgotten, 
And I, a devout fool, kneel to listen. 

I write your name in the dust of old letters, 
Fireflies drown in the smoke of my breath. 
The moon is a pale witness, 
Holding the bruise of our unspoken goodbyes. 

My heart, a vault of unopened letters, 
Locks itself in the language of storms. 
I whisper to the dark: Remember me
But even silence forgets its own shape. 

Dawn licks the edges of this ache, 
Yet morning arrives, hollow and pale. 
I wear this melancholy like a second skin, 
And the stars blink, indifferent and wise.

Echoes in the Empty House 

The clock gnaws at the silence, each tick a small 
eruption in the stillness. You sit in the chair 
where the light avoids you, a shadow stacking 
itself like unused parentheses. 

The house breathes slowly, its walls a skin 
holding the absence. You trace the dust on the windowsill
a map of where the sun has been. Your breath 
is a metronome, keeping time with the ache 
of unspoken things. 

The mirror holds your face but not your name, 
and the door, slightly ajar, hums a hymn 
of almost. You press your ear to the floorboards, 
expecting the past to rattle up, but the house 
is a vault of swallowed vowels. 

You are the echo and the space 
where the echo lives. No need for an audience 
to complete the sound. Here, solitude is a room 
that fits the shape of you, a hollow 
that cradles every edge. 

You do not wait for the world to return. 
You are the pause between notes, the held breath 
before the chord. You are the quiet that follows 
every word, the afterimage of absence 
that makes you whole.

Whispers of the Unseen Veil
Tears crystallize into glassy rivers, 
Silent echoes of a forgotten lullaby
The heart, a withered rose, clings to frost, 
Its thorns now weeping ink on time’s swift page. 

Shadows hum a requiem in velvet tones, 
While grief, a moth, feasts on the light of then
Each breath unspools the thread of what was whole, 
Leaving echoes where the laughter once took root. 

The moon, a pallbearer, drapes its silver shroud, 
Over fields where joy once dared to bloom. 
Now every star trembles, a flicker of remembrance, 
And the wind carries names that the earth forgot to keep. 

Yet in this hollow, something stirs
A seedling cracks the tomb of winter’s hold, 
For sorrow, too, must birth the language of the broken, 
To teach the soul how to cradle both the wound and dawn.

Whispers of a Dying Sun 
The last light cradles the fence where shadows cling, 
A rustling leaf its sigh swallowed by the dusk, 

The wind carries a name I’ve forgotten, 
Echoing through hollow branches, 
A song too distant to grasp, 

The pond mirrors the sky’s bruised hues, 
But the water holds no answers, 
Only the trembling of a moth 
Drowning in its own reflection, 

I trace the cracks in the path where we once walked, 
Each step a question mark erased by time, 
The world hums in monochrome, 
A melody without a verse to match, 

And the night lingers, 
Draping me in its velvet ache, 
While the stars blink like old eyes 
Too tired to stay open.

Fractured Echoes

The night whispered in shattered syllables, 
a pulse once bright now flickers behind cracked glass
Silence drapes the hollow chambers of my chest, 
each breath a thin veil over the rusted scar. 

I trace the remnants of a promise, 
the ink of us bleeding into forgotten verses, 

Hope, once a candle, sputters in the wind, 
its flame devoured by shadows of your absence. 

The mirror reflects a stranger’s eyes, 
still searching for the echo that never returns. 

Love’s anthem has dissolved into distant hums, 
and I gather the fragments, trembling, 
to stitch a new rhythm from the remnants of loss.

Echoes of Yesterday

The attic light flickers like a memory, 
Dust dancing on the old wooden floor
A cracked photograph smiles from a frame, 
Its colors fading but the warmth remains. 

The scent of rain on cobblestones drifts through the window, 
Whispering the footsteps of childhood games. 

We chased fireflies beneath a violet sky, 
Their glow a secret we promised to keep. 

Now the porch swing creaks a lullaby of years, 
Each sigh a story the wind has carried away. 

Yet in the quiet hush of twilight, 
The heart still hears that distant laughter
A tender echo that never truly leaves.

The Inventory of Absence 

An empty chair hums a hymn 
of unspooled thread. Dust settles 
like snow on the floorboards
a slow accumulation of nowhere. 

Shadows stack, unpaid bills 
in a language of cents and near-silence. 
The clock loses minutes, not time, 
and the walls wear their stains 
like old regrets. 

A photograph’s edges dissolve. 
The face inside is a ghost 
the frame won’t hold. Outside, 
the moon rehearses its craters 
in a mirror no one uses. 

The silence here is fluent. 
We never learn the verbs.

The Mirror of Dawn 

I see beauty rise when sunrise paints the sky, 
A quiet glow that makes the night say goodbye. 
It lives in the smile of a stranger you meet, 
In the soft rustle of leaves beneath your feet. 

It isn’t just the sparkle of diamonds or gold, 
But the way a heart opens when stories are told. 
A laugh that erupts like bubbles in spring, 
A whispered “I’m okay” when sorrow takes wing. 

Beauty walks in the rhythm of ordinary days, 
In coffee steam swirling in a lazy haze. 
It hides in the patience of a tired hand, 
In the courage to rise when you barely can. 

When you look in the mirror and see your own eyes, 
Remember the world is a canvas of sighs. 
Your scars are the brushstrokes that paint who you are, 
And every breath you take is a shining star. 

So cherish the moments that make you feel whole, 
The simple, the quiet, the depth of your soul. 
For beauty is not a thing you can own or possess, 
It’s the love you give, the truth you confess.

Echoes in the Alley of Sorrow

I walk the night where the neon flickers low, 
the pavement holds the footprints of every broken vow, 
my chest is a drum that beats a hollow rhythm, 
each thud a reminder that joy left the block years ago. 

Sorrow sits beside me like an old friend in a cheap coat, 
its breath smells of rain on rusted metal, 
it whispers, “you’ve paid the price for every gamble you took,” 
and I answer with a sigh that drifts into the alley’s sigh. 

I used to count dollars like prayers, 
thinking the stack would lift the weight of my name, 
but the numbers never filled the empty space behind my eyes, 
so I turned to the bottle, the smoke, the streets that never sleep. 

Now the city’s sirens sound like mournful guitars, 
each wail a chord that pulls at the strings of my heart, 
I hear the laughter of kids in a distant park, 
and it cuts me deeper than any blade could ever start. 

I tried to mask the ache with tattoos and tattoos, 
with swagger that cracked like old plaster, 
but when the night falls and the shadows grow taller, 
the mask slides off and the grief stands taller. 

Sorrow taught me the language of silence, 
how to read the tears in a stranger’s stare, 
how to hold a hand that’s already let go, 
how to love a ghost that never stays. 

I’m not looking for redemption in a choir of angels, 
I’m searching for a moment when the wind stops howling, 
when the city’s heartbeat matches the calm of my own, 
when sorrow finally bows and lets the sunrise in. 

So I keep walking, one step at a time, 
carrying the weight of every loss like a badge, 
knowing that even in the darkest alley, 
the echo of sorrow can’t drown the pulse of hope.

The Quiet Unfolding 

She paused on the path. 
Not because she’d meant to, 
just the way the light caught
a spider’s thread, taut between two thorns, 
dripping with dew. 
Each bead a tiny world: 
trees bent low, 
a sky folded into itself, 
something like stars 
but not quite. 

Her breath had slowed. 
The woods, as still as that. 
Not a sound, really, 
just the hush of things listening
a leaf’s slow turn, 
the weight of a beetle 
climbing what it thought 
was a mountain. 

She knelt. 
Not gracefully. 
Knees catching on roots, 
hands brushing lichen, 
cool as forgotten coins. 
The air tasted of moss 
and something older. 
Not earth, exactly. 
More like the idea of it. 

A wind, when she stood, 
shook the silence loose. 
Leaves rustled their secrets, 
and she let them. 
No need to hold it all together. 
Some things are meant 
to unravel. 

Wonder, she thought, 
isn’t the grand gesture. 
It’s the pause. 
The letting-go. 
The way a thread, 
stretched thin between two points, 
holds the whole world 
in its trembling.

Whispers of the Unseen Thread 
I trace the light where shadows cling, 
A silent hymn in every breath, 
The dawn unfolds without a sound, 
Its fragile thread through ancient trees. 

When tempests tear the woven sky, 
My pulse, a compass, never sways, 
For in the void where stars retreat, 
A spark persists no map, no guide. 

A whispered vow between two hearts, 
Yet roots dig deep in barren soil, 
Though storms may gnaw what time has spun, 
The loom of trust still weaves the dawn. 

Doubt may flicker, brief and sharp, 
Like sparks in night then fade to ash. 
No eye can see the thread’s embrace, 
Yet it binds the earth, the sea, the soul. 

So let the skeptic chart the void, 
While I, a pilgrim, walk the thread, 
Unseen, unbroken, it will hold
A prayer made flesh beneath the storm.

The Sublime and I 

I was a mountain before I met you, 
all granite and glacier, a silent cathedral 
of snow. You came with your thunderstorm heart, 
upturned my north from south. Now I am 
the avalanche in my ribs, the tremor 
that names no fault line. 

This is how I love you: by becoming 
a landscape of after-effects. Your voice, 
a volcano sleeping beneath my tongue. 
I taste the ash, the slow eruption of want. 
When you touch me, it’s the sea carving 
caves into cliff, relentless, hungry. I am the sand 
counting each grain as your tide pulls me under.

Whispers Between the Pines

They rise before the sun, the world still half‑asleep. 
A thin mist clings to the meadow, like a sigh that won’t let go. 
She pulls her sweater tighter, the wool smelling faintly of lavender, 
and steps onto the path where dew kisses the grass.

A robin hops from stone to stone, chest puffed, as if announcing 
the day’s first news. 
He pauses, watches the bird, then drops a pebble into the creek, 
watching ripples chase each other until they disappear.

The pine needles hiss underfoot, a soft rustle that sounds like 
a secret being told to the wind. 
A squirrel darts up a trunk, tail flicking, carrying a nut like a treasure, 
and disappears into the canopy before anyone can say “look”.

She stops by a birch, its bark white as old paper, 
runs a fingertip over the smooth surface, feeling the faint grain of years. 
A beetle climbs the trunk, slow and deliberate, 
as if it knows the exact moment to reach the top.

A low cloud rolls in, pulling the sky into a gentle gray, 
and the world feels a little cooler, a little more intimate. 
She inhales, the scent of pine and damp earth filling her lungs, 
and for a moment the noise of the city feels far away, a distant hum.

A fox appears at the edge of the clearing, amber eyes watching, 
then turns and slips back into the brush, leaving only footprints in the mud. 
She smiles, thinking of stories told around firelight, of hunters and hunters’ tales, 
and how the forest keeps those stories alive in every rustle and rust.

They keep walking, the path winding like a question, 
the trees answering in green and bark. 
She reaches a hill and looks out over the valley, where fields stretch like a quilt, 
and the river glints silver, a ribbon of light caught in the afternoon.

“Beautiful,” she whispers to herself, not needing anyone else to hear. 
The wind answers, brushing her hair, carrying the laughter of distant children, 
and the world settles into a quiet rhythm, a pulse that matches her own. 

They turn back, the sun now higher, the mist gone, the day fully awake, 
and the forest seems to smile, content to have been visited, 
to have shared its whispers, its small dramas, its endless, patient grace.

The Oak's Unyielding Song 

The oak does not whisper of surrender, 
its branches cradle the tempest’s cry, 
each scar a verse in the anthem of standing, 
when the storm’s breath howls, “Kneel,” it hums, “I am.” 

Lightning etches its defiance in the bark, 
winter gnaws, yet the sap ascends
a silent rebellion against the thaw, 
a testament written in rings beneath the soil. 

What force could bend what time cannot undo? 
The acorn’s pledge outlives the axe’s shadow, 
its leaves, unfurled, cradle the fallen seeds, 
nursing the earth where fractures bloom anew. 

And when the wind sings of the forest’s losses, 
the oak holds the ground where the lost once stood, 
its roots a labyrinth of remembered strength, 
teaching the young how to drink from the dark. 

Ah, resilience this stubborn grace
is not the absence of breakage, 
but the art of holding the light 
even as the world practices its shadows.

The Cosmic Whisper 

Have you ever gazed up at the endless blue, 
And wondered if the stars hold truths we’ll never know? 
The universe hums hymns in a language I can’t read, 
But still, I chase its riddles like a child with no shoes. 

I wonder if the moon feels our longing when we stare, 
Or if its silver grin is just a trick of the light. 
Do galaxies spin for a purpose, or do they dance just because? 
The wind always answers with a shrug and a sigh. 

The trees speak in tongues of roots and patience, 
While oceans scribble poems on the shore then erase them. 
I’m a dot in the cosmos, yet here I stand, 
Chasing shadows, asking why, as if the void will care. 

Is wonder a gift or a curse? 
To see forever and still feel small? 
The night sky’s a mirror, reflecting all my questions, 
But the answers? They’re buried in the soil of my soul. 

Maybe the point isn’t to find the end of the maze, 
But to let the wandering itself be the miracle. 
For even the dark has a heartbeat, 
And I, a flicker in the dust, am part of its chorus.

The Delicate Gravity 
Love arrives not as a storm, 
but a lamp smothered in breath
its glow, a question without answers. 
You hold it close to your chest, 
afraid to name the color of its flame, 
which flickers between compass and wound. 

In the beginning, it is a map 
drawn in the dark by two hands, 
each line a promise you cannot read. 
You mistake hunger for belonging, 
trace the curve of their wrist 
as if the pulse there could teach you 
how to measure a life. 

They say love is a tide
always returning, always a surprise. 
But you find it is more like the moon’s pull, 
silent and slow, reshaping the bones 
until the weight of you 
is no longer your own. 

You learn to love as you learn to walk: 
unsteady, then sure, then forgetting 
how many times you fell. 
You love in the language of scars, 
kissing the places where the skin 
has become a different kind of skin. 

Years later, when the body 
no longer hums with the same fire, 
you will find love has been 
the quiet between the notes, 
the way the room holds its breath 
when you say your name together, 
worn smooth as a riverstone. 

It is not the grand gesture 
or the speech rehearsed in the dark. 
Love is the small, stubborn thing 
that stays when the metaphor fails
a hand that no longer needs to hold on, 
yet does, simply because 
the world is heavy, 
and grace is not a choice 
but a surrender.

Fragments of a Forgotten Song 
The garden where our names were carved 
now grows wild, thorns overtaking the script. 
A sparrow circles the empty feeder, 
its song a thread unraveled from the loom. 

Your voice, a stone 
I keep turning in my palm
its weight, a language of no return. 

The sky forgets how to hold color; 
even the sun wears a gray shawl today. 
Footsteps echo in the brittle leaves, 
each crunch a ghost rehearsing absence. 

I tend the cracks in the porchlight’s beam, 
where shadows pool like spilled ink. 
Time, a moth, brushes against my ear 
but leaves no warmth behind. 

Still, the roots remember
how to split the dark, 
how to hum a hymn 
when the world goes mute.

HUNGER OF THE QUIET 

a pulse beneath the skin, 
soft as breath on glass, 
it gathers in the hollow of a morning, 
where coffee steams like a promise. 

Desire does not shout; it leans, 
a weight on the wrist of a watch, 
waiting for the second hand to pause, 
to feel the moment stretch. 

It is the ache of a closed book, 
pages whispering the next line, 
the taste of ink on a tongue that has never read, 
still hungry for the story. 

In the mirror it appears as a shadow, 
leaning against the edge of skin, 
a question that folds into itself, 
and opens again in the dark. 

We call it longing, we call it need, 
but it is simply the space between now 
and the shape we imagine, 
the quiet that pulls us forward. 

And when it finally slips into flesh, 
it is both the fire and the ash, 
the taste of fulfillment that already knows 
the next hunger waiting to begin.

The Light That Keeps Coming Back 

Hope is a quiet voice that wakes at dawn, 
a soft whisper that slips through cracked blinds, 
it doesn’t shout, it simply leans on the edge of a sigh, 
and tells the tired heart, “you’ve still got time.” 

We carry it like a pocket‑sized map, 
drawn in smudged ink from yesterday’s dreams, 
when the road turns to gravel and the sky turns gray, 
it’s the small pulse that steadies our seams. 

It lives in the rustle of a new leaf, 
in the smile of a stranger who doesn’t know you, 
in the stubborn bloom that pushes through concrete, 
in the promise that every night will end with sunrise. 

Hope isn’t a guarantee, it’s a choice
to keep reaching when the world feels heavy, 
to believe that even broken strings can hum again, 
that the next step might be the one that steadies. 

So when the night feels endless and the road is long, 
listen for that quiet voice inside your chest, 
let it remind you that the darkest clouds still drift, 
and that every storm eventually finds its rest.

Echoes of a Quiet Heart 
I hear love like a distant drum, steady and low, 
A pulse that walks through cracked sidewalks of memory. 

Your smile lands on the edge of my thoughts, 
soft as the first snow that refuses to melt. 

We trade whispered promises under streetlights, 
while the city hums a lullaby of sirens and sighs. 

In the silence between our breaths, I find a refuge, 
a hidden garden where shadows turn to light. 

When the night drapes its dark over the rooftops, 
your name becomes the candle I carry forward. 

So I hold this fragile fire, not to scorch, 
but to warm the empty rooms of a restless soul.

The Market of Belief 

A street preacher set up his stall at the corner of two cracked avenues, 
his sign hand‑painted in gold leaf: FAITH. 

He invited passersby one by one. 

A teenage mother clutching a newborn swaddled in a blanket of recycled plastic. 
An elderly widower who whispered prayers to a cracked photograph of a ship. 
A factory worker whose hands were stained with oil and hope. 
A graffiti artist who sprayed verses on abandoned walls and never asked for permission. 

He led them into an empty hall that smelled of dust and fresh rain. 

In the centre stood a wooden podium, and on it a plain white sheet of paper. 
Across it, in charcoal, he had scrawled a single question: 

WHAT IS IT THAT MAKES YOU HOLD ON? 

Beside the paper, a small tin box sat open, its lid propped by a rusted nail. 
Inside lay a handful of coins three pennies, a nickel, a quarter. 

He handed each visitor a single feather. 
“Write,” he said, “what you would trade for certainty.” 

They dipped the feathers into a bowl of ink that glimmered like spilled oil, 
and traced their answers across the page. 

The teenage mother wrote “a lullaby for my child.” 
The widower wrote “the echo of his voice.” 
The factory worker wrote “a day without the whistle.” 
The graffiti artist wrote “a wall that never erases.” 

When the last feather lifted, the paper was a map of yearning, each word a tiny scar. 

The preacher lifted the tin box, shook it, and let the coins tumble onto the floor. 
They clattered, rolled, and finally settled into a perfect circle. 

He took a match, struck it, and lit the coins. 
The flame licked the metal, turning copper to a brief sunrise. 
For a heartbeat the hall glowed, and the words on the paper seemed to lift, 
as if the heat could melt doubt. 

Then the fire sputtered, the coins cooled, and the paper remained, ink still dark. 

He turned to the crowd, his eyes reflecting the dying light. 

“Faith,” he whispered, “is not the fire that burns bright, 
but the ember you keep in your pocket when the world goes dark.” 

The visitors left, each clutching their feather, each stepping back onto the cracked avenues, 
their steps a little steadier, their breaths a little deeper. 

In the market, a new sign appeared, painted over the old: 

BELIEF IS A QUIET RESISTANCE.

Echoes of Yesterday 

I found an old letter, yellow and thin, 
Written in ink that time couldn’t mend. 
Each word like a shadow, soft and within, 
A story of moments the present can’t send. 

The clock’s hands spin, moments slip away, 
Childhood’s laughter now a distant tune. 
I close my eyes, and there they play
Sunset skies painted in a bygone room. 

The scent of rain on a dusty old street, 
Voices of loved ones long gone to the wind. 
Their echoes dance, a bittersweet beat, 
In the silence, their memories never end. 

I trace the lines of a faded photograph, 
A smile that time forgot to erase. 
Though years have turned the pages of the path, 
Their warmth remains in every embrace. 

Nostalgia, a ghost that lingers and clings, 
Whispers of what was, of love that still glows. 
In every heartbeat, the past it sings
A melody only the heart knows.

The Weight of a Tuesday 
The sky drapes itself in a thin, gray sheet, 
like an old blanket you keep pulling back 
just to find the same cold spots. 

Coffee sits in a chipped mug, 
its steam a brief apology for the chill, 
while the spoon clinks against the porcelain, 
a metronome counting down the minutes. 

He measures the silence with his thumb, 
the distance between the sighs of the hallway, 
as if the walls could be calibrated, 
like a ruler laid across a broken heart. 

The newspaper folds itself into a paper crane, 
its headlines whispering about elections and rain, 
but the only vote he feels is for staying still, 
for letting the day stretch out like a tired cat. 

A single leaf, amber and brittle, 
rests on the sill, waiting for the wind to lift it, 
but the window stays shut, and the leaf remains, 
a quiet reminder that some things never move. 

At night the ceiling fan spins slower, 
its blades a lazy clock that ticks in reverse, 
and he lies awake, counting the spaces between thoughts, 
trying to file the melancholy under “ordinary”.

Echoes of a Dawn‑Lit Heart 

When the sunrise spills its amber ink 
Across the quiet streets I wander, 
I hear the old poets humming 
In the rustle of the maple leaves. 

My thoughts, like paper boats, drift 
On the river of a sigh, 
Seeking the horizon where sky meets sea, 
Where love is a wild, untamed wind. 

I trace the curve of a distant hill, 
Feel the pulse of the earth beneath my boots, 
And wonder if the world itself 
Is a grand love‑letter written in light. 

So I let the morning’s gold seep into my veins, 
Turning ordinary moments into verses, 
And promise the world
Even the clouds
That my heart will always chase the sunrise.

ECHOES OF THE WILDERNESS 

Morning drips gold through the pine‑scented veil, 
my heart beats a drum that the river can hear. 
I chase the horizon where clouds fold like paper, 
and the wind whispers verses in a tongue only trees know. 

A lone hawk sketches arcs above the amber field, 
its shadow dances on the meadow’s trembling grass, 
while distant peaks wear crowns of silver mist, 
guardians of a secret the moon has sworn to keep. 

I sit on a stone that has felt the weight of centuries, 
its surface cold, yet it hums with the fire of old lovers, 
their sighs rising with the steam of sunrise, 
their promises tangled in vines that climb toward the sky. 

The brook laughs, spilling crystal laughter over smooth stones, 
and I listen, letting its song flood my veins, 
for in every ripple I see a portrait of you
eyes like twilight, hands that shape the world. 

Night falls like a curtain of velvet, studded with trembling stars, 
and the forest breathes a deeper sigh, 
the scent of pine and earth rising like incense, 
calling me to wander, to lose myself in the endless “what if.” 

Under that infinite dome I raise my voice, 
a trembling hymn to the wild, to love, to the ache of being, 
and the mountains answer back in low thunder, 
echoing the pulse that lives between my ribs. 

When dawn returns, the world is still a canvas, 
painted with the colors of longing and hope, 
and I walk forward, barefoot on dew‑kissed grass, 
knowing the romance of the earth will forever be my guide.

The Sidewalk Bloom 

It pushed through the crack in the walk
A weed, pink, defiant. 
Tourists posed, “So cute!” they said, 
And trampled the roots below. 

A vendor watered it with beer, 
A kid tied a shoelace to its stem. 
Each morning, it stood, half-dead, 
A symbol of the city’s grit. 

“Why’s it still here?” a man grumbled, 
As he snapped a photo for his wife. 
“It’s ugly,” she said, then smiled. 
The weed swayed, proud and cracked. 

One day, it bloomed one last time
A burst of color in the gray. 
They called it art, then paved it over. 
But beauty’s a rebel, you see
It grows where they say it can’t, 
And leaves a stain on the concrete heart.

Whispers of the Ephemeral Hour
The clock’s shadow dances where light once bloomed, 
A garden of moments wilts beneath time’s quiet thumb
Your breath, a fleeting hymn, hums through autumn’s decay, 

Each step etching ripples into the pond of forever, 
Yet the waves dissolve like ink spilled on the wind’s page
No name remains, only the ache of a pen left uncapped. 

I traced our names in frost upon the window’s glass, 
But the sun rose, arrogant in its duty, and erased them. 
So we are chapters burned to embers in the library of the void, 

Our laughter a candle snuffed by the sigh of the universe. 
Do not mourn the dusk; it is but the sky’s tender hand 
Gathering petals spent, to weave them into dawn’s rebirth. 

For even the stars, those arrogant kings of the night, 
Are swallowed by the same hunger that cradles our bones. 
What is a life but a song the void hums back, softer, 
As if it, too, remembers how to love what it cannot hold?

The Persistent Bloom 

In the marrow of the night, a single thread 
of light hums, a hymn without a hymnbook. 

I trace its edge with trembling hands, 
build a ladder from the rungs of my spine 
to climb the walls of a sky that won’t bend. 

Despair is a heavy cloth, but I tear it off 
to let the dawn stitch my skin with its silver needle. 

The seed inside the stone knows 
the weight of silence, the pressure of dark
yet it hums of forests it’s never touched, 
whispers of roots reaching for a moon’s echo. 

I walk with the horizon’s slow promise, 
each step a silent hymn, each breath a bridge 
between the fall and the flight of what might be. 

The sun is a coin tossed by a god who forgets, 
and I catch it in my palm, let it warm the creases 
where my thumbs remember the ache of holding on. 

Hope is not a flag waved in the storm
it’s the shadow that stays, unasked, 
when the light forgets to come.

Echoes of a Broken Heart 
Your voice lingers in these empty rooms, 
But all I hear are static hums, 
They say I’ll grow okay without you near, 
But how do I breathe when the air feels heavy here? 

They don’t see the cracks in my smile, 
How I fake laughs just to survive the while, 
You left like rain sudden, loud, and gone, 
Now I’m stuck in a drought where the silence is drawn. 

I replay our moments like broken records,

Dawn of the Unwritten Seed

Sidewalk Veins

Whispers of the Lone Heart

Dawn Within the Quiet

Hunger of the Quiet

I feel it first as a whisper in the back of my throat,

letting the words tumble out like rain on a tin roof,

something that isn’t just the ache of waiting,

The Arithmetic of Grief 

The clock on the wall has stopped at 3:17.

each minute a stone added to the scale. 

A chipped mug sits on the windowsill, 
still holding the ghost of steam. 
Outside, the ivy creeps to the eaves

unopened, addressed to a name

have forgotten the weight of visitors.

fibers frayed into a map of static.

A Light Between the Rows 
A thin ribbon of gold slips over the hill, 
touching the roofs of the sleeping town. 

Morning lifts the curtains of mist,

its green heart beating against the weight of earth.

a reminder that small voices can fill wide spaces.

the steady hand that steadies the trembling.

in the space where we choose to look forward.

the day holds its promise, bright and true.

Dawn on the Waiting Bench 

Morning drips through cracked glass, 
a thin gold thread stitching the sky.

bags thumping like quiet drums,

a quiet, stubborn glow we call hope.

Faith in the Unseen Span 

They told him the bridge exists 
though fog devours its shape.

Echoes of Absence 

When silence stitches the air with threads of gray,

Quiet Steel

into the dog-eared pages of a cookbook,

Eternal Echoes

burning through the myths of what joy should write.

not a trophy, but the dawn’s slow sway, 
turning every shadow into gold, unbound, 
a language spoken by the earth, unbound.

So let the mirrors show what they may,

Not how the world paints your day,

I trace the contours of then
your laughter, a bridge now broken, 
the fireflies that once danced

Hold me, old shadows,
