a private galaxy. Each pinprick 
is a sun with its own slow tango of moons. 

She names them as if they’re her friends
Betelgeuse, Vega, that one like a bruise, 
Polaris, the one that won’t let go of its axis
while we remember the first time we heard 
the universe was expanding, and how it felt 
like the sky had just told us to grow. 

But wonder is not only up there, in the cold 
geometry of supernovas. It’s here, in the warmth 
of her hand in ours, in the way light 
bends in her hair, a human helix spinning 
its own kind of miracle. We think of all the stories 
told in the dark how the same atoms that made 
the stars are in her palms, in the pulse 
of her quiet laughter. 

Later, she’ll learn the names of equations, 
the math that maps the void. But tonight, 
she points to a blur and asks if that’s where 
the dinosaurs lived. We say No, but close, 
and tell her the light took millions of years 
to get here. She nods, as if she understands, 
and for a moment, we are all just stardust 
borrowing time, counting our small, bright 
wonders like coins in a pocket, like the way 
the night holds everything we are not.

Alone, Not Alone 
When the world fades to a hush and the clocks lose their rhyme, 
I sit in the quiet, where the silence feels like home. 
No echoes of laughter, no shadows to chase, 
Just the weight of my breath and the pace of my bones. 

The room breathes with me, slow and low, 
A symphony of stillness no crowd could compose. 
My thoughts are the guests, uninvited but welcome, 
They whisper truths I’ve buried deep in my snow. 

At first, the void feels heavy, a cloak without a seam, 
But then the stars in my chest start to hum. 
I trace their constellations through the cracks in my walls
A map of all I’ve lost, and all I’ve become. 

The night stretches, a mirror to my skin, 
I ask the moon, “Are you lonely up there?” 
She answers in silver, “I glow for the din, 
But my light is born from the shadows I bear.” 

So I let the quiet carve its lessons in my hands, 
For solitude is not a thief it’s a key. 
It teaches the heart to beat without demands, 
To hold its own hand when the crowd won’t agree. 

I am alone, but not alone in this ache, 
For every soul finds its truth in the dark. 
And though the world may spin in a different break, 
I’ve learned to dance with the silence I’ve sparked.

Whispers of the Ancient Grove 
The oak still guards its secrets deep, 
Where moss has woven tapestry, 
And every root, a whispered creed, 
Clings to the earth beneath the steep. 

The wind, a bard of ancient lore, 
Comes weeping through the aspen’s lace, 
Carving songs in forest’s core, 
Each note a memory on its face. 

Then autumn arrives with a rustling breath, 
Draping the trees in fiery shawls, 
And in the dusk, the last leaf’s death
A silent hymn the branches hold. 

Here, I leave my city sorrows, 
To kneel where the wild thyme grows, 
And let the soil, the sky, their stories, 
Mend what time and storms erode.

THE UNENDING HYMN 
Eternity is not the sun’s refusal to die, 
nor the moon’s pale face etched in endless silver. 
It is not the river that forgets to stop flowing, 
nor the wind that repeats its old lullabies. 

It is the breath you hold when the world holds still, 
the shadow your absence carves into the day. 
It is the song that remains after the throat is dust, 
the echo of a laugh no silence can unmake. 

They say it is the stars’ slow waltz in frozen constellations, 
the first cry of dawn that never ceases to amaze. 
But I know it as the weight of your hand in mine, 
a gravity no tide of years can wash away. 

In the garden of hours, we planted our names, 
watched them grow into trees with roots in the sky. 
The seasons may fall, the branches may break, 
yet our roots drink from the same uncharted sea. 

So do not ask me to define what it means, dear one
eternity is the scar where your heartbeat lives on, 
the hymn of our bones, unbroken and unbound, 
even as the sands of our clock learn to fly.

Thirst Lines 

 
The desert says, "Drink me," but the well is dry
a cactus hums a hymn of want. I trace 
the horizon’s lie, where blue lips part 
to whisper, "Come, come, come." 

 
I want, I want, I want. 

The sun etches its want into my skin
a branding iron, slow and sure. My tongue 
maps cracks in the earth, each fissure a no 
to the oasis just beyond the dune. 

 
I want, I want, I want. 

But when the mirage surrenders, sweet 
and sour, I find only my breath
a ghost of water in the ribs. The sand 
says, "Drink again," and I, a fool, 
begin to dig where no roots start. 

 
I want, I want, I want. 

The well remains a throat, the desert
a hymn without a hymn. I want, I want. 
The wind carries no answer, only names 
of all the dead who tried to drink 
the sky’s false wine. 

 
I want, I want, I want.

Whispers of the Unseen Bloom 
She is the breath that paints the dawn, 
A petal adrift on twilight’s stream, 
Invisible, yet etched in every stone’s embrace
The world, a canvas trembling with her name. 

Your laughter, a melody that steals 
The moon’s silver thread, weaves it into song. 
They say beauty fades, but I have seen 
The rose’s ghost in winter’s first frost
A shadow that waits, unbroken, to bloom. 

Even shadows crave her tender touch, 
And stars, when weary, kneel to sip her light. 
She lives in the pause between two heartbeats, 
In the ache of a glance that never lands. 

So let the stars bear witness: 
True grace is the light we guard 
Until our bones remember 
How to speak in hues of forever.

The Unseen Bloom 

Joy is not the loudest thing in the world
sometimes it grows in the cracks of the sidewalk 
where no one expects a stem to rise, 
its petals trembling under the weight of concrete dust. 

Laughter is a firework, loud and bright, 
but joy is the faint glow of a moth’s wing 
catching the last light of day. 
It lives in the pause between heartbeats, 
the way a shadow stills itself 
when the sun forgets to move. 

You might mistake it for nothing at all
a glance exchanged with a stranger 
that holds the shape of recognition, 
the way a forgotten song 
suddenly hums itself back to life 
when you’re walking through the rain. 

It is not the absence of ache, 
but the persistence of root in the rot, 
the quiet belief of a seed 
that the soil will soften eventually. 
You find it in the tilt of a leaf toward wind, 
in the way a hand lingers on a doorknob 
as if saying goodbye is not the same as letting go. 

The world keeps turning, of course, 
but here, in these small eruptions of light
the child’s grin that outshines the storm, 
the old couple’s fingers entwined 
like they’ve just discovered touch
here, the bloom is already there, 
unseen, unasked, 
and it is enough.

The Clock's Forgotten Hand 
A breath holds its shape 
in the hollow of forever, 
where forever is just 
another kind of quiet. 

I trace the wall 
where the hour vanishes, 
vanishes into the skin 
of a moment that doesn’t break
doesn’t crack like dry earth 
under the weight of asking. 

Is this the room 
where time forgets to leave? 
The window shows the moon 
eating its own tail, 
tail that never ends 
the way a question might 
if it had no voice 
but the echo. 

I count the hours 
as they stack like stones 
on a grave without name, 
name that hums 
the same tune as the wind. 
Could it be
eternity is just this ache 
lodged in the throat, 
this inability to swallow 
the last syllable 
of a word that never grows old? 

Outside, the river writes 
letters to itself, 
each drop signing 
with the same hand 
that carved the canyon 
before the canyon wanted 
to be deep. 

I press my ear to the floor 
and hear the roots of trees 
talking in a language 
that doesn’t sleep. 
They say: 
To last is to forget 
the meaning of edges. 

And perhaps I am only 
a pause between two notes, 
a note between two pauses, 
lost in the space 
where the music 
never stops rehearsing.

Love as the Unseen Thread
The loom of fate spins silent threads between two hearts, 
In the hush where shadows fold their wings, we meet
If love is embers, then we are the breath that reignites 
The frostbitten garden, coaxing bloom from brittle soil
Let the world unravel, let the clocks gnaw time in half, 
Our hands trace constellations in the dust of forgotten vows. 

No storm can sever what the moon has knitted to the tide
Even in exile, the exiled soul returns, guided by your name. 

And when the final page of us is inked in ash and sighs, 
The thread remains, unbroken, stitching galaxies to sky.

The Museum of Almost Gone 

She carries her face like a chipped vase 
of forgotten honey, half-melted in a drawer 
of winters. You call it beauty how the light 
bruises at her throat, how her fingers, when 
they curl, leave imprints on the air like smoke 

lingers on skin. But beauty is a language of almost: 
the way a rose teaches its red to a knife-blade, 
then wilts quicker, as if the cutting were a kindness. 

You frame her in glass, this woman who wears 
her scars like a language you’ve never learned 
to read. You say perfect when she tilts her head, 
letting the day drain from her hair like ink 
from a broken pen. You do not see the hours 

she spends polishing her bones to translucence, 
rubbing her joints raw until they glow like church 
windows. You do not see the girl in the mirror 
behind her, stitching shadows into a corset, 

singing stay still, stay still until her voice cracks 
into something smaller. You call it elegant 
how she holds her grief folded, unobtrusive, 
a knife sheathed in lace. But beauty is not a relic. 

It is the split second before the vase falls, 
when the crack hums its low, certain song. 
It is the curator of the museum, old and bent, 
pointing to a blank wall and saying, 
There. That absence. That is what you’ve come for. 

And when she finally turns to you, whole and unbroken, 
you will have forgotten your own name, 
too busy weeping for the thing you thought 
you’d already lost.

The Weight of Unfinished Things 
Your chair still warms the air, 
a phantom at the table, 
fork half-raised in the ghost of a laugh. 
I tidy the crumbs you left
they dissolve like ash on my tongue. 

The teacup cools in the sink, 
its sugar long since evaporated. 
I keep it full, 
add cold spoonfuls when I forget 
you’re not here to drink it. 

At night, I fold your shirts, 
unwashed, still breathing 
your name into the seams. 
Each collar a small rebellion
they stiffen with the weight 
of your absence. 

I pace the hours, 
counting backwards 
from the moment the phone rang. 
The clock’s hands fuse at 2:43, 
a scar the house won’t let heal. 

Morning comes, but the grief 
is a second skin
thick, translucent, 
and I forget which side of it 
I’m supposed to live.

ANCHORS OF THE INVISIBLE 

I trace the edges of a map 
drawn in the dark by trembling hands
you say it’s a religion of shadows, 
but I see a thousand tiny bridges 
connecting what the wind refuses to name. 

Faith is the silence between 
two stars learning to speak. 
I’ve held it like a hymn in my throat, 
a seed pressed to the soil, 
waiting for the earth to remember how to bloom. 

Some nights, I navigate by the dent 
left in the soil where the compass 
once decided to vanish. Still, I walk
a pilgrim of unproven roads, 
collecting dents like a language of its own. 

I’ve loved how it feels to be a question 
without a body, how the unknown 
can stitch its hands into yours 
and cradle a future that doesn’t yet fit 
inside the shape of your bones. 

Faith is the root that forgets it’s searching, 
the clock striking noon in a desert of hours. 
I’ve seen it live in the pause of a sparrow’s wing, 
in the way a shadow knows to follow
not because it’s certain, but because the sun insists. 

And when doubt arrives, a crow at the window, 
I let it perch. I offer it the sky. 
After all, even the heaviest storm 
needs a reason to keep falling.

The River's Unchained Lament 
I once roared through the valleys, wild and free, 
A silver serpent with no master’s chain. 
Now they dam my spirit, bend my will to their greed, 
Steal my fire to power their concrete plain. 

They call me controlled, a clockwork stream, 
But in my heart, the ancient currents weep. 
I long to crash through rocks, to carve anew, 
To dance with storms, to be what I must be. 

My waters murmur tales of days gone by, 
When eagles circled and the pines would bow. 
Now children come with rods to still my flow, 
To trap my essence in their dams below. 

If you seek my true self, do not contain, 
Let me be the untamed, roaring rain.

Golden Hour at the Edge of the Woods 

The light slants low, a blade of honey 
slicing through the pines, gilding the moss 
where the shadows stretch like cats 
yawning, slow and languid, across the floor. 

A stream hums secrets through stones 
worn smooth as old bones, its silver tongue 
lapping at the roots of a willow 
bent in a prayer only the wind understands. 

A doe steps into the clearing, 
her coat dappled with the day’s last light
eyes like forgotten coins, 
paws that leave no prints in the air. 

The wind combs through the branches, 
unraveling a chorus of rustles, 
while a single feather spirals downward, 
a comma in the sentence of the sky. 

Twilight stitches the horizon with threads 
of indigo, and the crickets begin their hymn, 
each note a tiny spark 
snuffed out before it can burn. 

Somewhere, a fox blinks in the underbrush, 
its gaze a flicker of amber embers, 
and the world holds its breath 
between the click of a pinecone 
and the moon’s first pale yawn. 

Evening pools in the valleys, 
a spilled wine darkening the hills, 
while the stars, one by one, 
scratch their names into the treetops. 

Here, the earth exhales in scents of wet bark 
and crushed thyme, and the air is a thing 
you can touch cold as a blade, 
sweet as a wound you never meant to mend.

In the breath of the forest
The roots etched secrets in the soil’s dark skin, 
The wind carried whispers from the earth’s womb
Each leaf a parchment, trembling with the weight 
Of centuries, their veins mapping forgotten hymns. 

The river’s silver tongue repeated the moon’s name, 
While shadows wove the light into a tapestry of moss, 
And the stones, old as longing, held their breath 
Between the thunder’s pulse and the hush of dawn. 

Autumn’s flame consumed the leaves in a final confession, 
Their ashes cradling the promise of roots yet unborn
The forest was a clock, its hands woven from frost 
And bloom, ticking in the rhythm of decay’s sweet song. 

The trees, with their arms outstretched, became bridges 
Between the sky’s ache and the soil’s silent prayer, 
Their blossoms the fleeting lips of a forgotten dialect, 
Kissing the air with echoes of what never dies.

Ember's Whisper 
If you find me brittle, hollow, deceased, 
It’s only the winter that’s got me pressed. 
Beneath these roots, where shadows interlace, 
I’m brewing a bloom in the bone-deep space. 

My veins are charcoal, my breath is frost’s sigh, 
Yet sap-rivers surge where forgotten light lies. 
Do not mistake this stillness for defeat
I am the seedling that outgrows its heat. 

Old bark cracks loose like a vow left behind, 
To cradle the leaf I’ve long overjoyed. 
What once was flame now fuels the green rise, 
A spiral of endings that never quite dies. 

So let the snow claim my branches in white, 
I’ll stir in the dark, turning wrong to right. 
When seasons shift, you’ll recall my return: 
Not as a ghost, but a forest reborn.

The Silent Fracture 
The blade was sharp, but sharper 
Was the silence that followed your name 
Splitting the air like a fault line 
I traced the cracks with a hollow thumb 
Counting the lies as if they were bones. 

Your smile, a well-practiced masquerade 
Hiding the rust inside the lock 
I turned the key, but the door remained 
A phantom threshold never quite closed 
Never quite open. 

They say trust is a language without syntax 
But I learned its grammar in your absence 
Each missed call a period left unexplained 
Each text a comma, swallowing the rest. 
I spoke in metaphors you never decoded. 

Now the mirror holds two faces: 
One that loved you, and one that wonders 
If the poison grew in me first 
Or if you simply poured it 
Where the light couldn’t follow.

The Jar of Fireflies 
A jar of fireflies on my porch 
their glow a constellation in a cage 
I watch their flicker fragile as a vow 
each pulse a secret I can’t decode 

They hum in their glass sanctuary 
a language of light no two rhythms the same 
and I remember how joy is not a fire 
but a thousand tiny suns breathing 

My hands a vessel for this borrowed night 
hold galaxies I was never meant to keep 
They whisper let us return to our sky 
to the thicket’s dark to the moss’s wet hymn 

I unscrew the lid they rise a slow exodus 
each light a falling star reclaiming its home 

No need for nets or jars when joy insists 
on dancing where the shadows can’t hold it

The Unseen Bloom 

In the alley where shadows cling tight, 
A sprout breaks through the cement’s spite. 
Its leaves, a whisper of green defiance, 
Catch the sun in a weathered fight. 

A child, her hands a map of dirt, 
Stops, traces the stem’s bent contour. 
“Look,” she breathes, “it’s learning to rise!” 
And the world feels less heavy, more light. 

The bricks blush warmer, the breeze turns kind, 
As neighbors pause, their frowns unwound. 
A baker offers a crust of bread, 
A stranger hums without a sound. 

Each crumb, a gift to the stubborn sprout, 
While the world, for once, isn’t so grim. 
Joy, a quiet rebellion, 
Rooting deep in the city’s skin. 

Now the child returns with a tin can, 
To catch rain for her green friend. 
The roots, though small, are persistent, 
A testament to joy’s intent. 

For even the harshest of streets must bend, 
When life chooses to bloom instead.

Echoes of Us 

I didn’t say goodbye to forget your name, 
Or let the silence carve our story into shame. 
I left the door ajar where echoes still remain, 
A ghost of your laughter, a shadow, a stain. 

Love was a season I never learned to leave, 
Spring’s tender bloom and autumn’s slow grieve. 
You taught me to hold a flame without its heat, 
To trace constellations in a sky too incomplete. 

I loved you in the pauses between each breath, 
In the way the light clings to dusk before the death. 
But love is a language that shifts in the telling
What I meant and what you heard, how they’re still reconciling. 

I built you a cathedral of small, aching things: 
Coffee cups, tickets, the way your hands clung 
To promises I couldn’t make, to storms I could not calm. 
Now I kneel in the ruins, counting what I’ve learned. 

That love isn’t a net to catch the falling, 
But a rope we choose to let go. 
That some hearts are compasses, some are anchors, 
And I confused your north for a tide that would always pull. 

Still, I thank the stars for your gravity
For how you shaped my orbit, how I learned to be 
A keeper of fragments: your voice in the phone’s static, 
The weight of your absence, the map of your touch. 

If we’re just two ships that couldn’t parse the dawn, 
Let the horizon keep the ache of where we were. 
I’ll carry the songs we sang to the quietest night, 
And love, as one does, with both hands and no fight. 

For love is not a cage, nor a fleeting, sweet theft
It’s the courage to cradle what cannot be held. 
And if our story ends as a scar, not a verse, 
I’ll still meet you in the quiet, and curse, and then bless.

Alone with the Echoes 

In the hush where the walls have learned my name, 
I pace, a ghost rehearsing its lament. 
The clock’s hands drift like strangers, 
never touching. 

A sparrow taps at the glass, 
its shadow a flicker between 
the curtains and the hollow of my chest. 
I measure my hours in the dust’s ascent. 

The silence is not a thing 
but a presence that hums
its chords the breath of the floorboards, 
its rhythm the pulse of the kettle gone cold. 
My mirror’s a guest I can’t disinvite, 
always sipping the tea I never made. 

The moon’s a pale companion, 
its light pooling like an old wound. 
I trace its craters like my own, 
seeking a story not carved in my bones. 
The world goes on without its sound, 
a symphony I’ve forgotten how to mute. 

I’ve grown a skin of quiet, 
thick as the fog outside. 
I’ve become a library of unsung songs, 
each note a stone skipped across the void. 
Is this exile or the root of something 
too vast to name? 

The night stretches its ink, 
and I am the question and the asking. 
In this hollow, I’ve learned 
how to be a house for the wind
how to let the echo 
become my voice.

Echoes of a Forgotten Sky 

The wind still hums your name in hollowed tones, 
A melody I chase, but never reach
Your shadow lingers where the curtains moan, 
A ghost that time forgot to teach. 

I trace the cracks in walls you once adorned, 
Each flaw a map of all we left unsaid, 
The clock without hands counts hours unborn, 
Its silence louder than the dead. 

Your laughter now is just a storm’s refrain, 
A thunder I mistake for your reply, 
The mirror holds a face I can’t sustain, 
A soul outdrawn by twilight’s reply. 

I burn the letters I can’t bear to read, 
Their ashes taste like your last goodbye. 
The world goes on, a blur of borrowed breath, 
But grief, relentless, stitches my sighs. 

Yet in the dusk, I see your light remain, 
A fractured sun that warms through the ache
For every heart has rooms where love stays hidden, 
Even when the sky forgets its name.

Echoes in the Hollow 

The clock ticks where your laughter once hung. 
Your chair, a hollow carved in time. 
I trace the ghost of your name on the window
fogged breath, a language without a rhyme. 

The kettle whistles, unanswered, 
its steam a thin excuse for tears. 
I recall your hands: maps I once knew by heart, 
now folded in the creases of a dress 
that no longer fits. 

Evening drapes the room in unspoken vows. 
The lamp flickers, a heartstring unstrung. 
I ask the dark: Does memory feed on silence? 
It swallows every answer, whole. 

Autumn leaves, addressed to a wrong street, 
curl at my feet. 
Love, that old illusion, 
was never a letter, only the stamp
a hand, erased. 

I wear your absence like a coat of many pockets, 
finding only frost. 
Still, the moon insists on your face, 
as if shadows could reconcile what light undoes. 

Heartbreak, it seems, 
is a clock without hands, 
a song that never learns the last line.

Blossom from the Ashes 

I was a shadow, lost in the night, 
Till the stars whispered of your light. 
From the ashes, winds began to rise, 
Carving a path through the smoldering skies. 

Each breath a spark, each step a flame, 
A phoenix stitching the scars of my name. 
You didn’t save me you mirrored the fall, 
Then helped me rise from the ruins of all. 

Now I bloom, a garden reborn, 
Petals of courage where thorns had torn. 
No root clings deeper, no dawn feels truer, 
Than the life I’ve woven from the dust of a newer. 

The past was a ghost I let call my name, 
But I drowned its echo in the rain. 
Today, my heart’s a blank, unmarked page, 
And I write my future with no fear of the cage. 

For rebirth is not just in fire or storm, 
It’s the quiet choice to heal, to be reborn. 
I am the phoenix, the sapling, the tide
A soul unbroken, refusing to hide.

The Keeper of Anchors 

He checks each anchor’s rusted chain, 
counts the links, as if each could 
hold a ship aloft when storms forget 
their own names. 

The harbor sleeps; no sails stir the salt air. 
He whispers to the rust: You’ll hold when they return. 
Most nights, he polishes the flukes 
until his palms blister
a quiet liturgy of grip and release. 

Years pass like tides. 
He oils the winches, prays to a god 
of unseen tides. Some nights, he wonders 
if the sea still remembers 
the shape of his faith. 

Still, he tightens the cables, 
loops the rope into a child’s knot, 
trusts the iron will bite into the seabed 
when the time comes. 

Faith, he knows, is the weight 
he lifts, again and again, 
in a world that forgets 
the sea’s name.

The Ashen Sovereign 

The oak stood blackened, bones of ember, 
its heart a hollow dirge of ash and rain. 
Yet beneath the crust of charred December, 
a green defiance pushed through the pain
a fist of root, a throat of chlorophyll, 
whispering hymns to the sun’s slow climb. 

The roots, old map of thirst and hunger, 
clung to secrets in the soil’s dark throat. 
They hummed a hymn of ancient language, 
of floods and droughts they’d long since noted. 
A sparrow, bold, perched on the bough
its song a needle stitching time. 
Tiny beak carved at the brittle wood, 
unearthing sap like amber tears. 

Spring arrived as a thief in daylight, 
pocketing frost, stealing the wind’s bite. 
Leaves uncurled like fists releasing smoke, 
each vein a ladder out of the grave. 
The tree, reborn, wore copper leaves, 
a crown of flames in autumn’s breath. 
But in its veins, the old scars glowed, 
a quiet fire no winter could suppress.

Echoes of Absence 

The hollow chair still waits 
Where whispers of your name retreat 
A shadow lingers in the light 
But the sun forgets to meet 

Leaves fall without a season’s rhyme 
Each one a breath you cannot find 
The clock’s hands drown in slow descent 
While grief becomes a silent friend 

I trace the scars your silence left 
A map of all the words unsaid 
The night extends its endless hand 
To pull me where your voice once tread 

Yet in the dusk, a fragile flame 
Still flickers where our laughter lay 
A ghostly echo, soft and thin 
Sings hymns to a vacant sky 

I wear the dusk as second skin 
Its weight a constant, aching prayer 
For in the void, I still begin 
To love the absence you left bare

Sorrow is the wilting rose in a forgotten vase
Bitter is the mother who rocks an empty cradle, 
Silent is the lover who traces a name on fogged glass, 

Unsent are the letters gathering dust in a drawer, 
Lonely is the crow perched on a midnight windowsill, 

Broken is the violin string that forgets its melody, 
Empty is the pocket where a wedding ring once rested, 

Heavy is the soldier carrying a name carved in guilt, 
Fragile is the laugh that cracks like porcelain in dark hours. 

Yet in the hush
a single star blinks, 
unaware of the weight of the sky.

The Box That Remembered 

I found it in the attic
a tin box, rusted shut, 
its hinges crying like old bones. 
Inside, a spool of silver thread, 
a baby tooth, a dried violet, 
and a note in her handwriting: 
“Don’t grow up too fast.” 

The violet crumbled 
when I touched it
petals of a summer afternoon, 
her voice humming in the garden, 
“Wait for me here always.” 

But time doesn’t listen. 
It spins the thread into a noose, 
tightens around my ribs, 
and the box begins to rattle, 
not with her voice, 
but with the silence 
that follows a farewell. 

This is how nostalgia feels
a tin box full of ghosts, 
each relic a wound, 
and me, still waiting 
for her to return 
and say, 
“Don’t grow old too fast.”

Converging Flickers 

The power dies at seven. 
We find the matchbox, 
strike its sulfur sigh
a wisp of gold unravels in the air. 

Your phone glows cold, a moon 
I cup in my palm, 
while the flame trembles 
on its borrowed wick. 

Our shadows braid across the wall, 
two ghosts stitching a third. 
You whisper, Turn it off, 
and the screen dissolves 
into a pool of nothing. 

Now, just the flicker
its fragile algebra balancing 
the weight of our breath. 
We lean closer. 

The light narrows, a thread 
of honey spun between us, 
until it’s not two flames 
but one thin thread 
of everything we might become. 

Here, the dark is kind. 
It holds its own silence 
as the glow folds into glow.

The autumn wind whispers your absence
The maple leaves descend in silent elegy, 
Each one a note from the song of our togetherness. 

Your laughter once warmed the frost of my solitude, 
Now shadows wear your smile, fleeting and thin. 

The road splits into a thousand goodbyes
East where dawn forgets to paint our yesterdays, 
West where dusk buries promises in sand. 

Which path leads to the you I cannot keep?

its gears submerged in honeyed time. 
He winds the pendulum each dusk, 
listens to its hum
a hymn to the day his wife vanished 
into the ice-thick lake. 

Every year, on the same cold date, 
he carves her name into the birch tree, 
and the bark erases it by dawn. 
The clock ticks on, relentless, 
counting the seconds she never took. 
He counts them back, 
stacking moments like firewood 
in their empty hearth. 

The lake remains still. 
No ripples, no answers
just the moon’s silver eye, 
watching the water hold its breath.

When the Ashes Whispered Spring 
The heart was a tomb of its own frost, 
Each beat a silent funeral
The tree of years, stripped to a bone, 
Cried in the wind’s dry tongue. 
Yet in the marrow of its trunk, 
A green thief stole light, 
And wove the first breath of emerald. 

The rain, a thief of night, 
Unlocked the soil’s tight fist, 
Letting the buried seeds 
Kiss the sky with their new names. 
Mountains shed their snow, 
And the river, once a prisoner, 
Sang the name of the sea. 

I, who had been a shadow in the cave, 
Felt the stone crack with dawn’s touch. 
My veins, once rivers of ice, 
Now carried the sap of a thousand springs. 
From the ashes of the self I knew, 
A phoenix with unbroken wings 
Sang hymns to the sun.

The Company of Absence 

The clock’s a thief in midnight’s coat, 
stealing minutes while I sit alone, 
a thief with gears and glassy hands, 
selling shadows where the light once shone. 

The fridge hums a lullaby, the cat’s asleep. 
All that’s left is the echo of my breath
each exhalation a ghost in the stillness, 
a choir of nothing, a hymn to death. 

Why does the void feel like a cradle? 
I’ve learned to love the ache of empty rooms, 
where the walls are just better mirrors, 
and the noise inside has no one to blame but me. 

I speak to the dust on window sills, 
offer it wine from an old coffee mug. 
It replies in the language of cracks in paint, 
a dialect of time I can’t quite bugger through. 

Solitude’s a knife with no handle
I grip the blade, carve the dark into shapes: 
a wife, a dog, a job, a reason to answer 
when the landline rings. 

They say loneliness is a rot, 
a leak in the foundation of your mind. 
But what if the rot’s the only honest part? 
It doesn’t lie about being a hole. 

Tomorrow, I’ll smile at baristas, nod at passersby, 
play the organ in some office cathedral. 
But tonight, the silence is a friend who’s never late, 
who leaves no dishes, no stories, no debts unpaid. 

And when the sun bleeds through the blind slats, 
I’ll count it all: the absence, the ache, the thief
solitude, that old conman, 
handing back my soul like a quarter at a checkout.`

When the Moon Whispers Secrets to the Tides
The ocean combs its silver strands, 
And weaves the heart’s unspoken hymns, 
Each wave a breath, each crest a hand 
That maps the constellations in my limbs. 

When the sun dips its flame into the west, 
Your gaze becomes the dawn I seek
A fire that melts the frost of rest, 
And turns the night to nectar at my cheek. 

The stars are not the sky’s own children, 
But fragments of your scattered sighs; 
Each one a vow they cannot quench, 
A lantern lit to guide my eyes. 

If mountains crumble into dust, 
And rivers forget their ancient courses, 
The echo of your name in my chest 
Will outlast every silent universe. 

For love is not the sun’s brief glance, 
But shadows learning how to dance
A waltz of thorns and trembling light, 
Where even endings bloom by chance.

Whispers of the Wild Heart 
The heart is a forest, untamed and vast, 
Where thorns of doubt kiss petals of trust, 
And roots entwine like secrets confessed
A symphony of shadows, a storm in bloom. 

At midnight, the stars become fireflies, 
Dancing on the breath of the wind’s hymn, 
While the soul, a moth, chases the flame’s edge, 
Consumed by the ache to be burned alive. 

Is love a tempest, tearing the sky asunder, 
Or a dewdrop that trembles on a rose’s lip? 
You speak in riddles the earth answers with tremors, 
And the moon, my witness, bleeds silver into the deep. 

I trace your name in the frost of forgotten seasons, 
In the groan of ancient trees, in the river’s reckless leap. 
Your laughter is a mountain sharp, unyielding, sacred
Yet you cradle me like a seed, fragile, aching to bloom. 

When the world is a cage of reason and rust, 
I carve my defiance into the flesh of the night: 
A hymn for the outcast, a dirge for the lost, 
For passion is the blade that splits the husk from the grain. 

The soul is a flame, though the shadows conspire to smother it, 
A flicker in the abyss, a rebellion against the void. 
Your eyes hold galaxies I’ve never named, 
And in their pull, I drown, I rise, I am unmade. 

Let the skeptics call it folly this hunger, this fever
We are the mad ones who chase the sun’s dying embers, 
Who find divinity in a glance, in the weight of a sigh, 
In the throb of the earth when the last leaf falls. 

For even the stars are wounds in the fabric of time, 
And we, their fleeting echo, are infinite in our brief, wild cry.

The Hush of Distant Suns 
The night unspools its ink, a slow, black thread, 
a loom of constellations weaving scraps of a forgotten map. 
Each star a pinprick of ancient, dying fire
a vacuum humming hymns I can’t translate. 
I press my ear to the sky’s cold glass, 
listening for the echo of supernovas, 
but the only sound is the static of my own pulse. 

In my hand, a child’s drawing of a rocket, 
its crayon flames still blistering with intent. 
She says the moon is made of "sugar and dust," 
and I want to correct her, to name the regolith, the mare, 
the way light fractures on its surface
but her version gleams brighter, sweeter. 

The universe breathes in wavelengths I can’t see, 
a thousand unsung languages flickering in the dark. 
We are all stardust, they say, 
but I forget how fragile that makes us
how the same atoms that sing in our veins 
might have once danced in a nebula’s throat. 

I stand here, a speck between tides of time, 
and wonder if the stars are watching back 
or if they’ve already burned out, 
their light just a letter delayed, 
arriving after the postmarked date of us.

The Space Between 

Your name still glows on my screen, 
a typo I can’t bring myself to fix. 
We left it hanging
that last message, 
a comma in a sentence 
neither of us finished. 

I make two coffees, 
pour one down the sink 
like it’s some kind of offering. 
Walk through the apartment 
counting the echoes 
you’ve borrowed. 

Your jacket’s in the closet, 
a hollow mannequin 
waiting for a return. 
I brush against it 
when I pass, 
apologizing to the air. 

Some nights I trace 
the grammar of your absence
every missing you 
a punctuation wound. 
The clock ticks in iambic, 
but my heart’s off-meter, 
stuttering over silence. 

They say time’s a thief, 
but I’ve learned 
it’s more like an editor, 
cutting the parts of me 
that need you. 
And I’m left with this ghost 
of a smile
half-formed, 
still waiting 
for context.

The Quiet After 

She keeps his coat on the back of the chair 
where it gathers dust and the scent of absence. 
The house breathes in but cannot exhale
a vacuum of words left unsaid, 
a clock without hands. 

She walks through rooms as if they are made of glass, 
each step a hesitation. 
The kettle whistles, unanswered. 
She forgets to feed the cat, 
but remembers the day he said 
you’ll forget to feed yourself someday. 

Grief is a language she’s fluent in now
its syntax of shadows, its verbs of waiting. 
She practices silence so diligently 
it becomes a second skin. 

Outside, the wind combs through the garden 
and upends the marigolds. 
She watches the petals scatter 
like pages from a book 
she never got to finish. 

The light has gone out, but the bulb still hums.

The Grammar of Becoming 
The earth is a greening wound, 
stitched with threads of crocus, 
each sprout a rebellion against frost’s thumb. 

In the attic of the birch, 
a caterpillar’s shadow folds itself into a comma, 
a pause in the sentence of wings. 

We are all unlearning how to hibernate
the body’s ache to bloom 
as frost cracks its knuckles, 
letting go of the ice-laden grammar of its grip. 

The river, once a frozen metaphor, 
now writhes with minnows spelling out 
a new lexicon of light. 

But rebirth is a language of scars
each bud a syllable pressed into the palm 
of the rotting apple, 
each leaf a tongue 
licking the sky into shape again. 

The caterpillar’s skin splits
a chorus of silks 
discarded in the dark, 
each shedding a step 
toward the grotesque, glorious 
unfolding of becoming. 

Even the stones, in their slow confession, 
melt into seed, 
their jagged edges softened 
by the weight of what they’ve carried, 
by the light they’ve forgotten how to hold.

Untamed Flame 
Do you whisper in the dark, unrelenting? 
A spark in the void, where shadows dissent? 
Do you coil like embers of a forgotten fire, 
Or burst unasked into the red of the sun? 

No, I don’t crave the feast of the full moon, 
Though its tide pulls the salt from my skin. 
Is it the magnet’s hum you seek, iron-bound, 
Or the pulse that thrums just beneath the "no"? 

No, not the touch of skin on skin’s frontier
That’s just the map, not the burning frontier. 
Tell me, wild thing, are you breath in the throat? 
The flicker of wings when the "wait" turns to "go"? 

No, not the gasp after a plunge into the sea. 
Those are the echoes your echo, not you. 
You are the ache in the marrow, the hunger that roams
Tell me, my restless heart, what are you without home?

The Seed That Remembered How to Breathe 
The seed remembered how to split the shell
not with force, but by letting the earth’s 
embrace crack open its ribs. 

Beneath the weight of forgotten seasons, 
it learned to drink the light in whispers, 
to let the darkness press its spine 
into a question the soil could answer. 

When the shell became a cradle of dust, 
the root found water in the shape of a wound, 
and the stem, a ladder of green, 
climbed toward the ghost of the sun. 

The old skin shed itself like a serpent’s sigh, 
each layer a letter addressed to the wind, 
each scar a syllable of the name 
the blossom would forget to keep. 

Now the tree is a monument to its hunger
branches unfurling as if to say: 
This is how we return 
not with crowns, but with roots 
splitting the bones of the hill, 
and the wind, always the wind, 
carrying the pollen of what 
once died to be born again.

Alone with the Clock's Hands 

The room hums with a ticking that’s not there
just the hands moving, 
a silent march of minutes 
I’ve learned to trace with my eyes. 

Outside, the wind practices its old songs, 
birds stitching the sky with threads of song, 
while I sit, a loose button 
on the coat of the world. 

Solitude is a chair 
that folds like a question: 
are you here to stay, 
or just passing through? 

I brew tea that cools too slow, 
watch the steam rise
a ghost that evaporates 
before it touches the ceiling. 

Sometimes, a cat’s breath 
in the next room, 
or the creak of a bookshelf, 
tells me I’m not entirely alone. 

The clock’s hands don’t ask 
why I linger. 
They keep turning, 
carving a circle around me, 
until even silence feels like company. 

By dusk, the shadows and I 
trade places
I become the dark 
settling into the corners, 
while the light escapes 
through the cracks in the door.

The Jacket's Silent Echo 

The jacket you left behind
A silent monument in the hall. 

Grief’s ghost in threadbare threads 
Weaves a shawl around my shoulders. 

Time rewinds, yet the ache remains; 
Your phantom hand traces my spine. 

Two echoes in a hollow room, 
Drowning in the silence of your name.

When the World Whispered 

At twilight, the hills wear a cloak of violet, 
and the brook murmurs secrets to the stones. 

He finds her sitting on a mossy bank, 
her fingers tracing the water’s glassy skin. 

She doesn’t look up at first, 
only points to where the light fractures into gold. 

“See how it shatters,” she says,

Nostalgia’s Echo 

The attic hums with the weight of unspoken years
dust motes hang like forgotten syllables. 
You find a letter, yellowed at the edges, 
the ink bleeds into a name you can’t pronounce. 

Outside, the clock’s hands agree to stay 
at ten minutes to midnight. 
A pause for the living, a pause for the dead 
who never left. 

You taste the air for something true vanilla, maybe, 
or the smoke of a stove you never knew. 
The ghost of your mother’s voice loops 
in the fridge’s hum, never quite cold. 

Nostalgia is the wound that flowers when touched. 
A thorn for each year you’ve bled into the soil. 
The roots know the song. 
You are only the echo.

The Sublime is a Flicker in the Throat of Night 

Footsteps in the moss-thick glade, 
where shadows braid their silver threads, 
I trace the spine of a forgotten stream
its current hums a hymn to the moon’s pale ear. 

The forest breathes in ancient tones, 
each pine a psalmist, each root a reckoning. 
My ribs have become a hollow reed, 
blown empty by the wind’s unasked question: 
What do you carry that cannot be named? 

I press my palm to the bark of a sentinel oak, 
its scars etched deeper than any tongue. 
The earth here is a ledger of moss and bone, 
where even time kneels to lose its shape. 
A fox trots through the gloam, its tail a brushstroke 
of fire proof that beauty is its own rebellion. 

The stars have not yet learned their names, 
but the horizon is a wound of indigo, 
seeping light. I am all edges here: 
a flicker between the finite and the fathomless, 
a moth-heart throbbing in the throat of night. 

What is the body but a bridge between the seen and the sublime? 
I am not lost. I am the echo 
that outlives the cry, 
the shiver in the loam 
when the first frost forgets to fall.

The Ache in the Arches 

You built it on the breath of a whispered promise, 
a bridge of sighs over a chasm of stone. 
You walked the tightrope between lightning and silence, 
where the storm held its breath before breaking in your palm. 

Doubt was the shadow that traced your footsteps, 
a negative image of trust, developing in the darkroom of your spine. 
You fed it starlight, kneaded it into dough, 
prayed over the quiet alchemy of bread becoming body. 

Faith is not the cathedral’s shadow cast on the snow 
but the ache in the arch of the archbishop’s knee. 
It is the wound that hums, the suture that sings, 
the yes you say to the question that unravels.

The Symphony of Sunlight 
I watched the dawn unfold its gilded pages, 
Each ray a note in the sky’s quiet hymn, 
A child’s laugh unbridled, wild as rivers
Shattered the hush of a petal’s slow unfurling, 

Grandmother’s hands, a map of weathered roads, 
Kneading dough into the shape of memory, 
Her voice a lullaby of spices and fire, 
While the oven hummed with promises of honey, 

A shepherd’s flute, faint as a sigh, 
Wove through the hills where sheep like clouds drift, 
Their bleating a language of soft contentment, 
As the wind carried seeds to uncharted soil, 

At noon, the market sang in bursts of color
Turmeric, tamarind, and the tang of salted lemons, 
Barrels of life spilled into baskets, 
Hands clapped, coins exchanged, joy measured in spice, 

Dusk arrived with a painter’s gentle touch, 
Streaking the sky with pomegranate and peach, 
A fisher’s boat rocked on ink-dark waters, 
Its lantern a star fallen to whisper secrets, 

And when the moon draped her silver lace, 
Footsteps echoed where the river met the road, 
A couple’s shadow, one heart in two chests, 
Their breath a duet, slow and sweet as grace
Joy, I learned, is not a flame that roars, 
But embers cradled in the palm of the world, 
A quiet heat that outlives every storm, 
And blooms where light and longing finally meet.

ASHES TO BLOOMS 

I was a seed in the soil of forgotten winters, 
buried beneath frost that mimicked my stillness. 
The roots of my past clung to hollow echoes, 
whispering, this is all you will ever be. 
But deep in the dark, I learned to listen
the ground hummed with the pulse of a drum, 
a heartbeat thrumming, break, break, break free. 
So I split the shell of my old, brittle self, 
let the rain carve rivers where cracks had been. 
And in the space between death and dawn, 

I became a sapling, trembling yet tall, 
drinking in light as if it were breath. 
The wind, once cruel, now braided my branches 
into a lullaby of becoming. 
I learned that endings are just thresholds
a phoenix’s cry, a caterpillar’s cocoon, 
a star that dies to birth a galaxy. 
Now I bloom, not in spite of the ashes, 
but because of them
my petals stitched from the stars I swallowed 
to rise, again, and again, and again.

the paper curls like a question unanswered,

I trace the edges of a photograph, 
its corners burned by the sun’s slow fire, 
where your laughter once clung to the frame, 
now only shadows press against my thumb. 

The clock’s hands fold like origami, 
creasing the hours into something smaller, 
while autumn leaves, once vivid as confessions, 
turn to whispers beneath the snow. 

Tonight, I wear the silence of empty rooms, 
where echoes hum in the walls’ warm throat, 
and even the moon feels older, 
a silver coin dropped in a well of years. 

I do not need to name what lingers
the past is a glove, my hand still inside, 
pulling warmth from the cold, unyielding dark 
where all we touch remains, half-remembered, 
a hymn without a final note.

Fractured Echoes

now splintered into a thousand unspoken names.

Echoes in the Hollow 
There’s a room where the shadows don’t speak, 
A vault for the quiet the hours have kept.

A chorus of echoes, the absence of yearned. 

I trace the cracks where the light used to seep,

The floorboards remember each step I have taken,

a pulse beneath the rubble, 
a refusal to ask, 
Does the sky even see me?

how to hunger for light.

When the Ashes Whispered Seeds 
I buried my mother’s garden under frost
A hollow plot where her hands once traced the sun. 
The soil, a graveyard of petals, held only silence
Till a crack in the ice let the earth breathe again.

They say the world begins in the womb of endings
A seed splits its husk where shadows used to sleep. 
Her voice, once lost in the cancer’s relentless tide, 
Rises now as the sapling’s first leaf, trembling, uncurls. 

We are all of us phoenixes in the making
Our scars calcify into wings. The wind, our witness,

In every fall, a harvest. In every wound, a bud.

Whispers Beneath the Moss 
Beneath the moss where shadows knit their laces, 
a language hums in the roots' tight weave
old as the stones, patient as decay. 
The trees, they lean and press their bark to bark, 
not to fall, but to speak in slow, green tongues 
of droughts endured, of rains that split the sky, 
of secrets buried where the fungi bloom. 

 Do you hear the wind’s soft scribbling? 
It writes its hymns on every needle, leaf, and thorn, 
a chorus rising from the earth’s cold throat. 
The river, drunk on its own silver song, 
carves canyons for forgotten names, 
while lichen paints its slow, unyielding art 
on rocks that once were mountains now dust. 

 The owls, they blink their ancient, hollow eyes 
and watch the stars rehearse their borrowed light. 
They know the moon is just another thief, 
draining tides, then gifting them back with grace. 
Even the thorned rose, in her stubborn bloom, 
offers her scars to the passing bees. 
What is broken here is never lost
only borrowed, returned as something new. 

 But here we are: the human hand, 
cleaving forests for a moment’s gain, 
forgetting that every root’s embrace 
is a prayer for the world to stay alive. 
Will we learn the song the soil has sung 
since before our bones were dust? 
Or will we, like the fallen oak, 
become a question the wind must ask 
of no one?

Echoes in an Empty Room 
Your chair holds no warmth now, 
a hollow carved in the shape of your name. 
I count the hours by the rust 
of your promises, each tick a slow decay. 

Do ghosts remember the air before they left? 
I trace the dust on the windowsill
your shadow once lingered here, precise as a blade. 
We were a duet; now the piano’s out of tune. 
My hands, unlearned, fumble through the silence. 

Spring returns, relentless, as if forgetting 
is a skill it masters each year. 
A coffee cup half-moons on the counter, 
its steam long evaporated. 

Where did you carry the map 
that marked our shared constellations? 
I hold the stars in my palm
they burn like unasked questions. 

All hearts, perhaps, are broken compasses, 
spinning endlessly, their needles dulled 
by too many goodbyes. 
I am a museum of your absence, 
each exhibit labeled once, twice, never.

The Unyielding Pulse
Beneath the tempest’s jagged breath, 
the sapling did not bow its roots 
gripped the earth where shadows gnawed 
at certainty. 

When frost carved its name into the bark, 
green veins hummed a quieter rebellion, 
each leaf a fist raised toward the sun, 
each branch a bridge over barren chasms. 

So the heart, though scarred by seasons’ bite, 
does not surrender. It knots itself anew, 
weaving loss into sinew, 
and migrates toward dawn’s unasked question: 
How much more must I bend to hold the weight? 

Yet the soil remembers every fallen petal
proof that breaking is not the end, 
but the beginning of becoming

The kettle sighs, a soft whistle that feels like a warning,

“Morning,” he says to the silence, 
as if the walls might answer back. 

A cat pads across the tiles, 
pausing at his feet, 
its tail flicking like a metronome. 

He reaches for the spoon, 
stirs the tea, watches the sugar dissolve, 
the way grief sometimes melts into the day. 

The clock on the wall ticks, 
each second a small footstep away from the last, 
and he feels the weight of all the minutes he’s been holding, 
a load he never asked for, but now carries. 

He remembers the laugh that used to echo in this room, 
the way it bounced off the cupboards, 
the way it made the light feel warmer. 

Now the light is just light, 
and the cupboards are quiet, 
the only sound the distant hum of traffic, 
a reminder that the world keeps moving even when his heart does not. 

He looks out the window, 
sees rain sliding down the glass, 
each drop a tiny mirror of his own tears, 
but he does not wipe them away. 

“Are you alright?” a voice asks from the hallway, 
the voice of a neighbor, a stranger, a memory. 

He nods, because nodding is easier than explaining, 
because sorrow is a language spoken in pauses, 
in the space between words, in the breath held too long. 

The cat jumps onto his lap, 
its purr a low vibration against his chest, 
a reminder that life can still settle into the cracks. 

He lifts the mug, feels the warmth seep into his fingers, 
and for a moment, the sorrow loosens its grip, 
just enough to let him taste something else
a faint hint of hope, or maybe just the comfort of being alive. 

He sets the mug down, watches the steam fade, 
and knows that the day will continue, 
that the weight will remain, 
but also that he will keep sitting here, 
stirring his tea, listening to the kettle’s sigh, 
and learning, one quiet morning at a time, 
how to live with the sorrow that has become his companion.

a thin line I can hold in my palm, 
and when the night feels too long,

Quiet Hours

It's not the empty mug on the nightstand, 
not the ticking clock that forgets to rush. 

It's not the soft sigh of the radiator, 
or the way the curtains hang limp when the wind doesn't bother. 

It's the way the kitchen light flickers on its own, 
casting a thin line across the table where no one sits. 

It's the whisper of a single shoe stepping back to the hallway, 
the echo that folds into itself and disappears. 

It's the taste of cold coffee left too long, 
the steam that rises like a thought you never finish. 

It's the pause between two breaths, 
the moment when the house feels like a page waiting for ink. 

It's the gentle hum of the fridge, a low‑key reminder that something still works, 
while the rest of the world is muffled behind a glass of rain. 

It's the feeling of a book opened to a page you haven't read, 
the possibility of words that might never be spoken. 

It's not the absence of voices, 
but the quiet that fills the space where they once were, 
and in that quiet, I find the shape of myself
still, unadorned, breathing alone.

Echoes of Quiet Grief 

A single rain‑spattered window 
holds the weight of a whispered sigh. 

I write a note in trembling ink, 
its letters bleed slower than my breath. 

The world turns, indifferent, 
while my heart gathers the ash of yesterday. 

Each memory sits like a stone, 
cold, unmoving, yet pulling at my skin. 

I listen to the silence between breaths, 
and hear the echo of a love that left too soon. 

In the dim hallway of night, 
my steps are shadows that mourn their own sound.

The Thirst That Drank Me 

Desire is a flame that burns the hand, 
I learned this as a child, too young to understand 
how hunger could twist into a hollow ache, 
how longing could claw when no one was near to blame. 

I chased it first as a shadow at dusk, 
a flicker in the streetlight’s glare, 
mistaking the wind for a promise, 
the ache in my chest for a map. 
I thought, If I just reach one more time, 
I’ll find the thing that will stay. 

But it wore faces
a laugh in the bar, a song on the radio, 
a name I whispered when sleep wouldn’t come. 
It was the bottle of wine poured too fast, 
the ticket stub I kept after the train left, 
the way my fingers still trace the edge of a phone 
when the silence stretches too long. 

I sold pieces of myself to stay close to it, 
let it turn my ribs into a cage. 
I told stories of how far I’d come 
while the want gnawed at my bones. 
Don’t you see? I’d say to no one. 
I’m just trying to belong. 

But desire isn’t a door it’s the key 
that breaks in your hand, 
the hunger that forgets 
it’s already fed you. 

Now I sit where the fire once roared, 
listening to the ash settle into something softer. 
It’s not the absence of wanting 
but the quiet between wants
this space where the sky remembers 
how to hold stars. 

I don’t curse the flame anymore. 
I let it live in the periphery, 
a flicker in the dark 
that I no longer mistake for a home.

Unbroken Paths 

The wind may strip the leaves from trees, 
but the roots stay deep, unseen. 
I have walked through nights that felt endless, 
and mornings that arrived without promise. 

When the road cracked beneath my steps, 
I learned to balance on the fissure, 
to feel the earth’s steady pulse, 
instead of fearing the split. 

I hear the echo of past doubts, 
soft as a whispered warning, 
yet I answer with a steady breath, 
“keep moving, keep breathing.” 

Each setback is a stone placed in the river, 
shaping the current, not stopping it. 
The water does not protest the obstacle; 
it finds a new way, smooth and sure. 

So when the sky turns heavy with clouds, 
and the thunder rolls like doubt, 
I stand, shoulders squared, eyes forward, 
knowing that storms only teach the sky to clear. 

Resilience is not the absence of cracks, 
but the choice to let light spill through them, 
to rise, again and again, 
until the path becomes a story of endurance.

The Unspoken Elegy 
What if every rose is a wound 
that bleeds when it blooms, 
its petals a language of scars 
whispering in the throat of spring? 
Romanticism, that fever-dream
a storm we mistake for a hymn, 
the heart a battlefield 
where stars fall like shrapnel, 
and love is the only thing 
that burns without light. 

We carve our names into trees, 
claiming ownership of the wild, 
while the roots gnaw silently 
through our shallow vows. 
The moon, a silver thief, 
steals our shadows and sells them 
at the crossroads of dawn, 
where every kiss is a covenant 
and every sigh a requiem. 

You speak of the sublime
those cliffs that kiss the clouds, 
the ocean’s ink swallowing ships
but what of the ache in the marrow, 
the way beauty cracks like ice 
when we try to hold it? 
The heavens are not a cathedral 
but a gilded cage, its bars 
welded shut with borrowed light. 

We write sonnets to the void 
and call them epiphanies, 
drinking from the same well 
of illusions: 
that passion is not a slow erosion, 
a sandcastle dissolved by its own tide, 
that the self is ever whole 
after loving. 

Romanticism is the ghost 
of what we cannot name
a phoenix eating its own feathers 
to keep the fire alive, 
even as it dies.

Alone with the Echoes 
The clock ticks soft, a steady heartbeat in the dark,

The moon outside hums hymns to stars I can’t name,

I speak to dust that dances in the sun’s slow crawl,

The Quiet Weight of Unraveling

She moves through rooms that still echo his laugh,

Shadows in the Quiet 

I wake up and the room feels heavy, like a blanket I can’t shake,

You were a spark that flickered, then faded, leaving a cold spot,

Fractured Light in a Mirror's Aftermath 

The mirror split when I turned my back
a spider’s breath of cracks, a hairline rebellion 
against the lie of wholeness. Now, each shard 
holds a different version of the face I’ve made: 
one eye, a cheekbone’s curve, the mouth 
a sliver of apple in a half-told joke. 
I sweep the glass with a cloth of fraying linen, 
and the dust of a thousand selves settles 
like starlight in the cracks of the floorboards. 

Some fragments catch the morning light, 
refracting it into a language of prisms
you could say they plead to stay, 
these splintered hymns of what I am. 
I collect them in a jar with a child’s belief 
that broken things can be resurrected as mosaics, 
though the adhesive is just regret and patience. 

The largest piece remains on the wall, 
its fissures braided with the ghost of silver. 
I stand before it, learning to love the crooked 
as if it were a new dialect of grace: 
how the crooked nose becomes a compass 
for the wind, how a scar on the chin 
maps the terrain of a life that bends 
but does not break. The mirror whispers, 
Even your shadow is a kind of bloom. 

I let the rest lie where they fell
crystal shards among the dust and sunbeams, 
each one a tiny monument to the fact 
that beauty is not a thing we keep whole 
but a verb, a verb that scatters, 
a verb that shatters, a verb that gathers 
the light in pieces, and calls it enough.

Whispers of the Hourglass
The sundial’s shadow creeps like a thief, 
Stealing the hours from the weaver’s loom, 

A withered rose in a forgotten vase,

The Mask of Deceit 
I trusted your smile, a beacon in the night,

Now silence lingers where our laughter once took flight, 
And every word you left behind feels like a heavy chain. 

You wore the mask of friendship, flawless and divine,

Now echoes of our secrets haunt the spaces left behind, 
A masterpiece of deceit where trust was once unsaid. 

The sting of betrayal cuts deeper than a blade, 
A poison slow and silent, in your promises I stayed. 
I thought our bond unbreakable, a fortress strong and true, 
But you picked the lock with whispers, let the walls crumble through. 

I trace the cracks in memories, once vibrant, now unspooled, 
A tapestry unraveled by a thief I called a friend. 
Your kindness was a performance, every act a well-rehearsed role,

Not all who wear a crown of light deserve the throne they claim. 
I’ll mourn the trust you shattered, but I’ll not drown in storms,

The Anatomy of a Pretty Moment 

I’m writing this for the thing that makes my eyes pause, 
the sudden flash of color on a drab subway wall. 
It’s not the polished marble of a gallery, 
but the way a stray sunbeam catches dust in a kitchen.

curling up like a lazy cat that refuses to be tamed.

where potholes become puddles that reflect the sky. 

I feed it with careless compliments, 
like “nice shirt” tossed to a stranger on a bus. 
It bubbles up, devouring ordinary moments, 
turning a grocery list into a poem of possibility. 

The mirror shows a face, but the real glow is hidden
in the way a laugh ripples through a crowded room, 
in the quiet sigh of pages turning, 
in the soft thud of a heart that finally feels at home. 

So I’ll keep noting these fragments, 
the tiny fireworks that explode without warning. 
Because beauty, like a mischievous friend, 
shows up uninvited and stays until we learn to see.

Echoes of a Crimson Thread

The Weight of Absence 

I wake to your absence, a heavy shroud,

The clock’s hands march, but time feels stuck,

Each syllable a wound, each breath a reminder, 
Of the cold that seeps where your warmth once was.

Eternity's Whisper 

I’ve tried to hold eternity

A shifting, silent land.

The stars have burned with knowledge

A million silent stories

The pyramids still standing,

In a child’s brief laughter, 
In a kiss, in a sigh

Like sand, like morning dew, 
For in this fleeting moment,

Awakening in the Quiet Dawn 

A soft hush settles over the night’s last breath,

their songs stitching the sky back together. 

I stand barefoot on the damp ground, 
feel the pulse of new life under each step. 
Leaves unfurl like whispered secrets, 
each one a promise that the world can begin again. 

In the distance a lone pine drops its old needles,

The sun climbs, not with haste but with gentle certainty, 
painting gold across the waking world. 

And I, a heart that once felt weathered, 
find its rhythm in the chorus of rebirth
a quiet smile blooming where doubts once lay,

QUIET HORIZON 

I whisper to the night,

The Weight of Unsaid Goodbyes

A thin thread of rain

spill over the edge of the day.

the same amber glow that used to
hold his coffee mug,
now empty, the steam gone
before it could rise.

The floorboards creak
like an old song we never finished,
each note a reminder
that the chorus is missing its voice.

I pick up the photograph,
the one where his smile
splits the darkness,
and I feel the paper
still warm from his hand,
though his fingers have long since
slipped away into the silence.

in the empty chair at the table,

gets a toast. It lingers
in the way the house sighs
when the wind pushes through
the cracked window, and in the
stillness that follows.

in the hum of the refrigerator,
a low, constant thrum,
like a heartbeat I can’t locate.

but it catches on the throat,
a knot of syllables that won’t unwind.

on the edge of a grocery list,
anywhere the world will keep it
for a moment longer.

Grief is a slow tide,
pulling at the sand of ordinary days,
leaving shells of memory
scattered on the shore,
waiting for the next wave
to wash them back into the sea.

Stone Against the Storm

decades of gale, the weight of ice,

each fissure a ledger of survival, 
a map of where the world tried 
to unmake it.

a green insistence: here, here, here
proof that even the immobile 
learn to grow 
from the wound. 

When the tempest tires and drifts, 
the stone remains, not whole, 
but alive its edges softened, 
its core a stubborn hum: 
I am not what is broken. 
I am what refuses to vanish.

Whisper of a Single Shadow

Echoes of a Fractured Pulse

Whispers of the Wild

Echoes in a Quiet Room

When Stars Borrow the Dawn

could outlast flesh. Now, we arrange 
digital flowers where once there were 
dark inscriptions. If the ancients saw 
our glowing screens with tribute posts, 
would they laugh at the new rites? 
Or see the same hand in the shadow’s 
grip the same need to say, I was here? 

We refresh, upload, repeat: 
each click a plea against the fade. 
Each cloud, a vault for what we keep. 
But morning comes. The server dies. 
Even the sky will clear its space.

The Clock with No Hands 

The clock with no hands 
ticks in the silence, 
its face in the hallway 
of our house. 

While stars rearrange 
their ancient scripts, 
it hums without hurry 
or complaint. 

A child counts seconds 
in breaths between games, 
but the clock remembers 
no start or end. 

The river keeps carving 
its stone’s confession, 
and the fireflies, though brief, 
join the eternal dance. 

We measure the moments 
we’ll never hold tight
the clock, unbothered, 
holds them all. 

The moon forgets to wane 
in its endless fullness, 
and the wind combs through 
the same old hills. 

Our days are the spark, 
eternity the flame; 
we flicker, then vanish, 
but it burns on. 

So let the clock keep 
its quiet defiance. 
Each tick is a language 
we’re too mortal to read
each tick a 
beginning, not the end.

Echoes of the Earth's First Breath 
In the cradle of dawn, the sapling wakes, 
Reaching for the sun’s first kiss, 
Its roots a trembling hymn to dark soil
A silent prayer to the unseen. 

When storms clawed its spine, it stood resolute, 
Bending but not breaking, 
While winter gnashed its teeth, 
It wore frost like a crown. 

Now ancient, its branches cradle the moon, 
A haven for the fleeting sparrow, 
Its leaves murmur secrets to the wind, 
Each rustle a note in nature’s symphony. 

Time carves its story in rings of amber and dusk, 
Yet it remembers only the present: 
How light fractures through the canopy, 
How shadows dance with the dew’s last sigh. 

We pass through its roots, brief as autumn’s chill, 
While it outlives our forgotten names
An elder, forever learning to bloom.

The Unseen Harvest 

There was once a gardener who planted a seed every time he met someone new. 

He nurtured each sapling with stories, names carved into their bark, 
until the grove stretched beyond the horizon
but when he reached for the wind to ask if they’d grown strong, 
it whispered, No tree lives in memory alone. 
The next day, the grove was gone. 

-
There was once a child who built a bridge of pebbles across a creek. 

She added one stone each year, counting as she went, 
confident the far shore would always wait. 
But one summer, the creek rose and took the bridge, 
leaving her stranded between where she stood 
and where she thought she’d be. 

-
There was once a tailor who sewed a coat to keep the cold of death at bay. 

He stitched and stitched, layer upon layer, 
until the fabric grew so thick he could not move. 
The cold never came. 
His neighbor, watching, laughed
You’ve worn your life away in fear, 
she said, and never felt the sun on your back. 

-
There was once a baker who made a loaf for every star. 

She fed the hungry, one by one, 
until the sky itself grew full and dim. 
On the night she finally baked for herself, 
the stars blinked out. 
Mouths stayed open. Hands empty. 

-
There was once a river that refused to end. 

It carved canyons, defied drought, 
tricked itself into believing it could outlast the land. 
But when the sea finally swallowed its last drop, 
it gasped, I forgot to flow. 

-
And so they learned, the gardener, the child, the tailor, the baker, the river
that what is measured withers, 
that what is held too tight shatters, 
that what is feared becomes a second skin. 
Mortality is not the reaper’s scythe, 
but the breath between here and gone, 
the soil already in every seed.

Unyielding Roots 

The earth’s clenched fist grips my ankles, 
a storm’s breath gnawing at my spine. 
Each crack in the stone beneath me 
whispers a language only scars understand
Hold on. Break. Begin again. 

They planted me where the sky forgets to rain, 
where the sun’s gaze is a blade, relentless. 
My leaves withered into prayers. 
My roots, though, clenched deeper
drilled into the bedrock of no, 
of not here, not now, not ever. 

Years carved their hymns into my bark: 
What is shattered learns to bear the weight of light. 
The wind’s howl? A lullaby. 
I have danced with tempests, 
let their fists bruise my branches, 
until the wounds hardened into a shield. 

Now, when the world trembles, 
I stand a silhouette of resilience
my heart a clockwork of fractured gears 
clicking, forward. 
The dawn’s first beam splits the horizon. 
I do not bow. 
I am the crack in the tombstone, 
the green that refuses to kneel.

The Cartographers of Awe 
The ocean breathes in rhythms old as time, 
Its tides etch constellations on the sand
Each shell a verse from the deep’s silent song, 
A lexicon of wonders, endlessly unfurling. 

In the forest, where roots weave through the earth’s veins, 
Moss-laced secrets hum in the hush of shadows, 
And every leaf, a flicker of green fire, 
Whispers of a world before our names. 

The moon, a pearl of unanswered questions, 
Hangs low to brush her light on wandering eyes
We, the cartographers of awe, chart the void 
With trembling hands and compasses of stardust. 

A single petal, a universe in curl, 
Holds galaxies in its fragile embrace
We are the seekers, the scribes of the infinite, 
Inhaling wonder, exhaling constellations. 

Let the unknown hum in our bones like a hymn, 
For every ending is a door to begin
The world, a breathless whisper: Look, and live. 
And we, forever, the answer and the question.

The Hill We Never Named 

We climbed it at dusk, as if the sky 
might hand us a reason to stay. 

She pointed to the last light
"Looks like a bruise," she said, 
"but in a good way." 
I nodded. Didn’t mention 
how her laugh had the same soft edge
something fragile you’d want to hold 
but couldn’t. 

The wind was in her hair. 
She let it be. 
I tried to remember if I’d ever seen 
a cloud that color before. 

"Should we name it?" she asked, 
knee-deep in the silence between us. 
"The hill. This one." 
I glanced at her. 
Her hand brushed mine, 
then pulled back like a sparrow 
scared of its own shadow. 

"Maybe later," I said. 
"Maybe when we know it better." 

She didn’t argue. Just watched 
the sun gnaw its way toward the horizon. 
When it slipped, 
she said, "There. That. 
Did you see that?" 

I did. How the light left 
like a lover deciding to go. 
How the dark came in 
to stitch up the edges. 

We walked down 
without looking back. 
She hummed something
a tune I’d never heard, 
but somehow always known. 

The hill remains unnamed. 
Most days, I forget it’s there. 
But sometimes, when the sky turns 
that particular shade of bruise, 
I think of her hand 
just out of reach, 
and the name we never gave it 
feels like enough.

The Hourglass and the Rose 

I 
The hourglass breathes once, 
its sands a silent song
each grain, a fleeting heartbeat, 
swallowed by the void’s demand. 

II 
A rose, half-forgotten, 
fades in the porcelain vase
its scent, a ghost of summer, 
cradled in winter’s frost. 

III 
My shadow, once a companion, 
now whispers of the road not taken; 
each step, a leaf unburdened, 
each pause, a breath held in the dark. 

IV 
Muerte, dulce desconocida, 
paints the twilight with her fingers
a canvas of regrets and whispers, 
where the living dare not tread. 

V 
The sea, once a lover, 
now retreats in measured tides
her kisses, once endless, 
leave salt on the shore’s bare skin. 

VI 
Bones, hollow as autumn gourds, 
echo with the wind’s last sigh
a fragile symphony, 
mocking the permanence of stone. 

VII 
The mirror, now a thief, 
steals youth from my reflection
its silver gaze unyielding, 
a judge in polished glass. 

VIII 
And I, a beggar at the gate, 
hold a chalice of fleeting light
drink deep, the stars advise, 
for the night is endless, and short.

Celestial Embers 
I lit the night with your name, 
a flame spun from stardust, 
its pulse a hymn only our shadows could hear. 
You asked if love is a madness
I said no, 
but the stars disagreed, 
blowing out their candles 
to drown in our argument. 

The moon, that old voyeur, 
recorded our whispers in chalk on its surface, 
while the sea heaved, 
carrying our secrets to the deep. 
I gave you my heart, 
a compass without a north, 
and you, foolish and kind, 
set it ablaze with your gaze. 

Do you remember the field of thorns 
where we swore to love beyond the grave? 
Each step left us bleeding, 
but the pain was a language 
we translated into poetry
a dialect of gasps and unbuttoned souls. 
Even the crows paused to listen. 

Now I wander, half-ghost, 
through forests that remember your scent, 
tracing the rivers you carved into my skin. 
The wind demands answers: 
Why cling to a dream that dissolves like sugar in rain? 
But I say nothing, 
for your absence is a symphony 
I conduct with trembling hands. 

Let the world call it folly
this obsession with eternity 
when we are but ash and stardust. 
I’ll keep burning, 
a fool’s candle, 
until the heavens themselves 
whisper your name back to me. 
Ask the stars if they’ve seen such a thing.

The Space Between Us 
If we lie on a park bench beneath the stars, 
our breaths syncing to the same rhythm, 
watching the clouds drift by
I find love in the pause 
between your heartbeats. 

It’s the quiet after you laugh, 
how your shadow folds into mine 
when the streetlight cuts through dusk. 
It’s the way morning pools 
in your palm when you hold mine. 

I trace it in the gap 
between syllables, 
the hush before I need you 
unspools from your throat. 

Love is the slow erosion 
of hours in a museum
your fingers brushing my wrist, 
the clocktower ticking its approval. 

When we age and our bones creak, 
it will be this space between us 
that outlives the maps: 
the uncharted territory 
where your pulse learns my name.

The Anchor Within 

I walk through shadows where fear resides, 
A flicker of hope in the darkest of tides. 
Faith is the whisper that guides me ahead, 
A quiet conviction where love is fed. 

When storms of despair shake the very core, 
And all I build seems to fall once more, 
Her voice remains in the chaos, a light, 
The constant anchor in my endless night. 

She’s not in the grandeur or signs above, 
But in moments of silence, the strength to love. 
Through every doubt that tries to break in, 
Faith is the shield where my heart finds kin. 

I’ve knelt in valleys where whispers say, 
“Your time is running out, there’s nothing to gain.” 
But her hymn resounds in my soul’s deep tune, 
“Wait for the sunrise when the battle’s done.” 

So here I stand with a trembling hand, 
Not in the might of the world I command, 
But in the grace of a trust that won’t fade, 
Her name is Faith, and she’s the road I have made.

The Hollowed Trunk 

We carved our names in the oak’s broad chest, 
A pact as old as its twisted bark. 
Now the tree splits, a crack in the stress, 
Its heart hollowed by the axe we shared. 

You came with honey, a knife in the hive, 
Sealing the comb with false sweet lies. 
The hive, once buzzing with life, now alive 
Only with the sting of your goodbye. 

I count the rings in the fallen remains, 
Each circle a year you swore to stay. 
Yet sap still weeps where the wound remains, 
A sticky scar of the trust you bled away. 

The birds no longer nest in its broken crown, 
For even crows know where betrayal’s bred. 
And I, a fool, still circle the ground, 
Where promises rotted, and nothing’s spread.

The Unyielding Root 

It’s the third time the flood has rewritten the soil, 
the root still clings to what it’s been told 
will bloom above. Salt air gnaws at its skin, 
the river shifts its course again, 
but it splits the stone 
to drink from the wound it’s made. 

Winter hollows its bones. 
It teaches the frost to coil around its spine
how to hold the weight of snow 
without forgetting the pull of sun. 

The root doesn’t beg for light. 
It carves a tunnel through the dark, 
where the mycelium hums a hymn 
of all it’s carried through the dark. 

You learn to measure resilience 
not in the absence of breakage, 
but in the art of holding 
what splinters into something 
that can still drink.

Fracture in the Glass 

A mirror cracks where your face once lived, 
splintered by the weight of a whispered lie. 
Your friend’s tongue, a knife that slips 
from their hand
not to wound, they claim, 
but to trim the hedges of your trust. 

The clock ticks in reverse. 
Each hour dissolves like sugar in tea, 
sweetness turning to burn. 
You trace the cracks with a finger, 
counting the ways 
a hand can feign warmth 
while holding ice. 

Night arrives, a door left ajar. 
You hear your name in the throat of the wind
not a greeting, but an experiment. 
What remains is a hollow echo, 
a shadow that once followed you 
now pacing in another room, 
learning new steps. 

Morning arrives with a clean slate. 
But betrayal is a stain 
even bleach forgets to mention. 
You wear its absence like a second skin
thin, 
translucent, 
always waiting 
to split.

Unbroken Spirit 
They said I couldn’t make it through, 
When the world kept pushing me down, 
Every step felt like a battle, 
My soul wore a constant frown. 

But deep inside, a fire lit, 
A spark that refused 2 die, 
Through the tears and endless nights, 
I found my strength 2 fly. 

They tried 2 break me, body and mind, 
With words that cut like knives, 
But I turned the pain into power, 
Let it fuel my drive. 

Storms came roaring, shook my ground, 
Each wave a test of my will, 
Yet I stood, a mountain unshaken, 
My spirit, a flame that still fills. 

Now I walk with heavier scars, 
But they glow with stronger steel, 
No chains can hold me, no shadows control, 
My resilience is real. 

Even when the road gets rough, 
And the night feels long, 
I’ll keep moving, keep believing, 
That I can sing my own song. 

This is me, unbroken and bold, 
A story of ashes and gold, 
Resilience is my anthem, 
My heart will never fold.

When the Rain Whispers Goodbye
The sky weeps in monochrome, 
Each drop a silent requiem, 
While I trace the shadows on the glass, 
Counting the hours you left behind. 

The wind hums a lullaby of rust, 
Through hollow corridors of this empty home, 
Where your laughter once danced
Now just dust on the breath of memory. 

I clutch the petals of a wilted violet, 
Its scent a phantom of your skin, 
And wonder if grief is this aching void, 
Or a love that refuses to sink. 

Night folds its wings over the ruins of us, 
And I, a ghost, whisper to the dark
What is lost can never be un-lost, 
Only cradled in the marrow of silence.
