Not by erasing the wounds within, 
But by letting sorrow make me thin
A vessel reforged from loss’s flame, 
Ready to love, to live, to claim 
The scars as proof I once embraced, 
And now must walk this earth unmasked.

The Room Where Echoes Dwell 
In the chamber where my shadow clings, 
The silence carves its name in the walls
A quiet sculptor, patient and cold, 
Molding the shape of a lonely hall. 

A clock with no hands measures the hours, 
Its breath a whisper through dust-choked air; 
I speak, but the echoes refuse to stay, 
Slipping like smoke through the keyhole’s gaze. 

A mirror holds a face I’ve learned to know, 
Yet asks no questions, demands no light
Just holds my absence like a still-life, 
A portrait of someone I might become. 

The window frames a sky without birds, 
Each cloud a page left blank and unmarked; 
I trace the glass with a finger, a writer 
Penning a story the world won’t read. 

Still, in this hollow, the truth is clear: 
Solitude is not a cage, but the air 
I hold to breathe each exhalation 
A star dimming, then remembering to shine.

A Symphony of Laughter Dancing in Sunlight

A melody that painted the sky with hues of gold, 

The sun, a golden coin, dropped into the river, 
Its ripples stitching light across the water’s skin, 

A mother’s sigh melted into the breeze, 
Her hands weaving joy into the wind’s embrace, 

Time forgot its ticking for a while, 
As shadows bowed to the rhythm of bare feet, 

The world held its breath, a paused symphony
Leaves clapped softly, a rustling applause, 

And when the stars blinked their sleepy eyes, 
The earth hummed a lullaby it had never written, 
But had always known by heart.

You ask why I wear this melody like a second skin 
It’s not the notes, it’s the pause between them

They’ve been rehearsing your name

Silently. 
With the exactness of someone who knows how grief feels in the marrow of a bone.

No one bought the notebook. 
It sat in a drawer behind the cash register, like a secret kept for a rainy day.

She did not regret writing it. 
Words do not fail, she thought. They simply wait longer than the heart is willing to listen.

She moved between the tables as if each one might hold a clue to what she was searching for.

Her eyes lingered on the rye, on the jam, on the notebook peeking out from the drawer.

She handed a folded piece of paper, its edges frayed from being read many times. 
“It’s called The Quiet Song of Evening,” she said. 

A name she’d never heard, but one that felt like a promise. 

A quiet joy rose inside her. 
She recognized the title. 
Every line. 
Every blank space where a note might have been. 

She went to the back room, opened the cardboard box, and let the notebook stare up at her with patient hope. 
She chose it, cradling it as if it were a fragile bird. 

When she returned, the woman’s eyes widened as though she had found a small miracle. 

“This is perfect,” she breathed. 

She nodded, her voice barely a whisper. 

“You’ve helped me more than you know,” the woman said. 

She did not tell her. 
She did not correct her. 
She let the gratitude settle between them, unclaimed, understood by the quiet hum of the bakery’s old lights. 

The bell chimed after the woman left, a soft period at the end of a long, melancholy sentence. 

She stood behind the counter, empty‑handed but oddly full. 
Somewhere out there, someone would read those lines, feel the weight of a quiet song, and perhaps, for a moment, let the grey light soften. 

And that was enough. 

Maybe more than enough.

The Crack in the Lock 
Hope is the crack in the lock 
where the light begins to leak, 
not a flood, just enough 
to trace the shape of your hands. 

Do you kneel for it? 
Or let it crawl through the floorboards, 
a beetle dragging its shell 
through the dust of unasked questions? 

They say it’s a myth
that the door swings both ways, 
that the dark is just pressure, 
a vacuum made of forgotten names. 

But you keep the receipt 
for the milk you never bought, 
because the expiry date 
is still three days from bleeding. 

Tomorrow, the frost will bite 
your cheeks and call it truth. 
The radio will chant: 
nothing changes here. 

Still, you hum the tune 
the power outage taught you, 
when the streetlights went blind 
and the neighborhood howled 
with the sudden freedom 
of a thousand windows 
lit by candle. 

Hope is the crack 
that refuses to become a wound. 
It’s the key 
you’ve never stopped turning. 
Even when the lock 
eats the lock. 
Even when the light 
is just your eyes 
learning how to bleed.

A Sunlit Pulse 

If laughter spilled like sunrise on my skin, 
I’d chase it down the alleys of ordinary days, 
Turn each cracked sidewalk into a golden hymn, 
And let the world spin faster just to hear it sway. 

I’d trade the quiet of midnight for the chorus of noon, 
Where children’s giggles are fireworks in the air, 
And every breath I take would hum a bright tune, 
A rhythm that lifts the weight of any care. 

The sky would blush pink whenever I close my eyes, 
Because joy is a pigment that never fades, 
It paints the clouds, it stitches the sighs, 
And leaves a trail of light on all my shades. 

So let the heavens open, let the earth applaud, 
I’ll wear this smile like armor, fierce and free, 
For in the pulse of pure, unguarded joy, 
I’ve found the place where every heart can be.

Echoes in the Unseen 

The world wakes before sunrise, 
a soft hush spilling over rooftops, 
and I stand on the edge of the street, 
feet bare, heart wide‑open. 

A sparrow darts, a flash of feather, 
its song a question that folds into the air, 
and I hear the question echoing 
in the cracked pavement beneath my shoes. 

I watch a child’s eyes widen at a puddle, 
reflections of clouds drifting like ships, 
and the ordinary becomes a map 
to a continent I’ve never visited. 

The old oak in the park shivers, 
its leaves whispering stories of seasons, 
each rustle a syllable in a language 
that only the wind seems to read. 

Even the streetlamp flickers at dusk, 
a lone lighthouse for the wandering thought, 
and I wonder if the darkness is merely 
a canvas waiting for a brushstroke. 

So I gather the tiny marvels
the scent of rain on hot concrete, 
the taste of sunrise on my tongue, 
the laugh that slips from a stranger’s mouth
and stitch them together in a quiet hymn, 
a reminder that wonder is not a distant star, 
but the pulse that beats inside every breath, 
the secret we carry, unwrapped each day.

Silent Echoes

In the hollow of an empty room, 
the clock ticks like a lone heartbeat, 
a whisper of dust drifting across the floor, 
does the silence breathe, or simply wait? 

Why does the window stare outward, 
while the walls turn inward, 
listening to thoughts that wander, 
like moths lost in a midnight lamp? 

 The chair by the pane holds a single book, 
pages flutter without a reader, 
the wind sighs through cracked glass, 
and asks, “who will hear your name?” 

Do shadows cast by absent footsteps 
grow longer as the day retreats? 
Do they keep company with the lingering dusk, 
or dissolve into the night’s soft veil? 

 I walk the corridors of my own mind, 
each step echoing a question, 
what is the shape of a friend unseen, 
when the only voice is my own? 

The world outside hums a distant chorus, 
but here, in this quiet harbor, 
the tide of thought rolls slow, 
and I learn to sit with the stillness, 

to taste the bitter‑sweet of being alone, 
to paint my thoughts on the walls of night, 
and find, in the hush, a hidden rhythm, 
a pulse that beats, unaccompanied, yet alive.

The Quiet That Holds Its Breath

His gaze is a dim hallway, 
light flickers at the far end
but the bulbs have long ago burned out, 
leaving only the cold metal of the frames.

Skin feels like parchment left in rain, 
soft edges curling, 
veins map a rusted river across his forearms, 
each pulse a muted drum.

Words linger on his tongue, 
thin as cracked glass, 
they fall without sound, 
leaving a hollow echo in the room.

The air is a thin sheet of ash, 
settling on the windowsill, 
the world outside moves in muted grayscale, 
while inside the clock ticks louder than ever.

He carries a weight that has no shape, 
it presses against his chest, 
not a burden but a presence, 
a quiet that refuses to be whispered away.

In the mirror he sees a reflection that is both there and not, 
eyes that have learned to swallow the sun, 
a smile that folds into itself, 
and the lingering taste of a song that never finishes.

Melancholy is not an absence, 
it is a slow drip of rain on a roof that never dries, 
a soft hum that vibrates through the bones, 
and the lingering scent of winter after the snow has melted.

The Cinnamon Hour 
The oven’s glow, a small sun at the room’s heart, 
as you taught her to measure cups of light
flour dusted like snow on the counter, 
her laughter rising with the yeast. 

She asked, “Is it magic or just time?” 
as the dough stretched in her palms, 
a supple thing, becoming bread. 
You said, “Maybe both.” 

Outside, the rain tapped its steady rhythm, 
but here, the heat made the air golden, 
and she spun, covered in frosting, 
a map of sugar on her nose. 

You remember how her mother never 
baked with you, how the recipe book 
sat closed, its pages yellowed with never-use. 
But here, now, the child’s hands are the reason 

the oven sings. You press your thumbs 
into the dough, side by side, 
and it rises, a quiet hymn 
to the alchemy of warmth and patience
joy, not as a firework’s burst, 
but the oven’s constant glow, 
a knowledge that the small, shared hands 
can turn nothing into something 
that fills the room, slow and sweet, 
like the way she says, “Again?”

The Unseen Clock of Dawn 

The hands of time fray into morning, 
Yet the first bird remembers each note it sang, 

Eternity is not the dawn that never breaks, 
But the song that lingers after the last feather falls, 

When the moon etches its scars on the tide’s soft skin, 
The shore keeps the rhythm of a thousand forgotten waves, 

A heartbeat between the echo and the silence, 
The moment the flame becomes the ash, yet cradles the spark, 

We chase the horizon, thinking it endless, 
But eternity lies in the pause before the breath, 
Where all that is broken is whole, and all that is whole is broken.

The Hollow Where Your Voice Lingers 

I wake to the quiet that follows your name, 
a silence so loud it carves through the walls, 
each breath a whisper against the remains 
of a fire we tried to keep from the fall. 

Your coffee cup still warms on the counter, 
a relic of laughter in ceramic’s cold curve, 
I trace its rim, now a fossil of afternoons, 
and curse the sun for refusing to grieve. 

The jacket you left hangs like a question mark, 
threads unraveling under the weight of the wind. 
I slip into it when the night feels too sharp, 
to stitch myself into something you once clung. 

The clock ticks in monochrome seconds, 
a metronome for the ache I can’t mend. 
I count each shadow your absence has sent, 
and drown in the weight of the unsaid. 

Perhaps I’ll find you in the mirror one day, 
not as a wound, but a lesson in light. 
Until then, I’ll hold this hollow away
a cathedral built from the bones of your night.

The Quiet Fire of Dawn

Knowing how the sunrise 
presses gold through the thin veil 
of night‑torn clouds, 
soft as a lover’s sigh, 

we walk the old stone path 
where moss remembers footsteps 
of poets who traced the river’s curve, 
their verses spilling like water. 

The wind carries the scent of pine, 
a promise that the world is larger 
than the walls we build, 
yet tender enough to hold a single breath. 

In the hush between two heartbeats, 
the sky blushes, 
and we, small as a leaf, 
listen to the earth’s slow, steady hum
a romance written not in grand gestures, 
but in the patient glow of ordinary wonder.

Paper Hearts 
I found a love note tucked in a coat pocket, 
the kind that smells faintly of laundry soap 
and a hint of yesterday’s rain. 
It read, “You’re my favorite person to argue with,” 
and I laughed because it was true. 

We meet at the kitchen table, 
two mugs of coffee steaming like tiny clouds, 
and the cat decides to sit on the newspaper, 
blocking the crossword I was about to solve. 
She nudges the page with her paw, 
and I pretend it’s a secret code we both understand. 

Our love is a collection of small trades: 
her favorite song on the radio, 
my willingness to share the last slice of pizza, 
the way she steals the blanket when I’m shivering. 
It’s not always dramatic, 
it’s more like the soft hum of a refrigerator, 
constant, unnoticed, but essential. 

Sometimes we argue over the correct way to load the dishwasher, 
she says “top rack for glasses,” I say “bottom for plates.” 
We end up laughing, turning the kitchen into a battlefield of suds, 
and the suds end up everywhere on the floor, on the cat, on the walls. 

At night, we sit on the balcony, 
watching the streetlights flicker like fireflies, 
and I tell her the stars are just city lights reflected in the sky. 
She rolls her eyes, but she leans a little closer, 
and that’s enough to feel the universe shift a fraction. 

Love, for us, is not a grand gesture, 
but a series of tiny moments stitched together
a paper heart tucked in a coat pocket, 
a shared laugh over suds, 
the cat’s indifferent stare, 
and the quiet knowledge that tomorrow 
we’ll argue about the dishwasher again, 
and love will still be there, waiting in the kitchen.

From Ashes, a Song 

You don’t have to be a prophet 
To see the cracks in winter’s shell. 
A single bud on barren branches 
Whispers of a world that’s new. 

The old may fall without a sound, 
Yet from their dust, the seeds take flight. 
A moth escapes its charred cocoon 
And burns its wings on borrowed light. 

Did the stones in ancient ruins 
Sense their future as fertile soil? 
Or do daffodils, breaking ground, 
Sing hymns of a forgotten turmoil? 

Rebirth isn’t a thunderclap
It’s the pause between a heart’s two beats. 
A crack in the egg, a breath in the dark, 
A melody the silence used to eat. 

So let the broken things mend slowly, 
Let the scars wear crowns of moss. 
Even shadows, given time, will bloom 
Into something soft and lost.

Whisper of the Unending

Time sighs, a soft echo of forever,

The Clock‑less Room

It sits in the corner, a window that never closes, 
the light spilling in like a patient visitor, 
steady as a breath you can’t quite catch.

He watches it, the way you watch a kettle humming, 
knowing it will keep at it forever, 
but never quite daring to measure the minutes.

A cup rests on the sill, its porcelain skin warm, 
the steam curling upward, tracing circles that never end, 
as if trying to write a word that has no last letter.

He lifts the mug, feels the heat on his palm, 
a reminder that time can be held, 
if only for the length of a sip.

Outside, the sky is the same shade of indifferent blue, 
the kind that people point to when they need a reason, 
but it offers nothing, just an open stretch.

He thinks about the idea of eternity, 
not as a grand, romantic notion, 
but as a hallway of identical doors, each waiting for a knock that never comes.

A dust mote drifts across the beam of light, 
pausing for a heartbeat, then continuing its lazy glide, 
a tiny reminder that even the smallest things move onward.

He places his hand on the windowsill, 
feels the coolness of the glass, the faint echo of countless suns, 
and wonders whether the world is a single breath held too long.

No grand revelation arrives, no thunderclap of meaning, 
just the soft, persistent hum of ordinary existence, 
the way a clock‑less room can feel both endless and perfectly contained.

He sets the cup down, watches the steam dissolve, 
and lets the light keep spilling, unhurried, unasked, 
as if eternity were simply another day waiting to be noticed.

The Long‑Lived Whisper

When I ask eternity to sit at my kitchen table, 
it shows up in a cup of tea that never cools, 
steam curling like a question mark that refuses to settle. 

I have tried to measure it with calendars, 
with the ticking of a clock that sounds like a distant drum, 
but each “tick” feels more like a sigh from a tired librarian 
who has already shelved every moment I could ever borrow. 

Eternity wears a coat of quiet patience, 
its pockets full of forgotten birthdays, 
of lovers who promised forever and then slipped into the cracks of a hallway. 
It does not rush, it does not hurry
it simply exists, a background hum beneath the daily chatter. 

Sometimes I hear it humming in the attic, 
where old photographs gather dust and stare back, 
eyes wide with the same wonder I felt when I first learned to write my name. 

I imagine eternity as a gardener, 
planting seeds of stars in the soil of night, 
watering them with the sighs of poets who have already gone, 
and waiting for the blossoms that will never be plucked. 

If I could hold eternity in my palm, I would not try to own it. 
I would trace the outline of its patience with my fingertips, 
like a child tracing the edge of a map, 
knowing that the true adventure lies beyond the ink. 

So I sit, cup in hand, listening to the long‑lived whisper, 
letting its soft cadence settle into the rhythm of my breathing, 
and I learn that forever is not a destination, 
but the space between each heartbeat that chooses to keep listening.

The Carnival of Lost Buttons

each breath a risk of ascent.

stained with ice cream and possibility. 
A carousel of painted horses 
chewed the hours into confetti. 
She won a goldfish in a plastic bowl, 
its tail a flicker of liquid sun. 

Later, he left without saying goodbye, 
took the tickets and the glow, 
leaving her with the weight of the bowl, 
the silence of a deflated balloon. 
The carnival packed up at dusk, 
wheels of the rides creaking secrets. 
She kept the fish, named it After, 
watched it trace circles in its lonely sea, 
a survivor of the feast.

Joy Unbound

We dance in the kitchen, two goofy fools,

Joy isn’t a whisper, it’s a roar that sings, 
it’s the way you hold my hand and the hope it brings, 
so I’ll keep writing these lines, simple and true, 
because every beat of my heart says joy lives in you.

Lanterns in the Dawn 

I stare at the first light, 
the way it stretches thin across the night’s edge, 
and wonder how a single breath 
can pull the shadows back. 

Hope is a quiet hum, 
like the soft thrum of a distant train, 
carrying the weight of forgotten promises, 
yet never forgetting the tracks it rides. 

When the world feels cracked, 
I gather the pieces like loose shells, 
lay them on a table of patience, 
and watch them glisten under the sunrise. 

Each ray is a question, 
each shimmer a tentative answer, 
and I whisper to the wind, 
“Stay, even if just for a moment.” 

In the hush between heartbeats, 
the sky folds its dark sleeves, 
revealing a tapestry stitched with gold, 
where every thread is a new beginning. 

So I walk forward, barefoot on dew, 
letting the cold kiss my soles, 
knowing that every step, however small, 
lights a lantern for the road ahead.

Quiet Altar

She folds prayer like a paper crane, 
edges soft, creases stubborn, 
and lets it slip between the pages of a notebook 
that smells of coffee and old receipts. 

I watch the candle flicker, a nervous firefly, 
its wax melting into the same shape 
as the teacup she left on the windowsill
a tiny, round confession of heat. 

Faith, she says, is the sound of a shoe 
clicking on a hallway you’ve never walked, 
the echo that answers back “who’s there?” 
when the house is empty and the wind is listening. 

A moth flutters against the glass, 
its wings a map of every night she’s tried 
to write a letter to the sky, 
but the ink keeps dripping into the dark. 

She hums a lullaby to the ceiling, 
the words are missing, but the rhythm stays, 
like a train that never leaves the station, 
yet somehow still arrives. 

When the phone rings with no name, she answers 
with a smile that feels like a sunrise in a drawer, 
and the world, for a moment, pauses
a breath held in a room full of unfinished prayers. 

Faith is not a bridge you cross, 
but the plank you step on while the river laughs, 
and you keep walking, because the water 
doesn’t ask why you’re there. 

She lights another candle, watches the flame bend, 
and whispers, “I’m here,” to the shadows that 
have learned to dance in the same quiet light.

Sunburst in September

September’s first blush:

A symphony of solitude, both sharp and stark, 
Where every note is etched by time, unchased. 

So let the quiet grow, let stillness carve its name, 
For in this hollow, I have found a quiet truth: 
To bear the weight of absence, learn to hold the flame
Alone, I am the keeper of my endless youth.

Ephemeral Echoes 
We are clocks built of breath and borrowed time, 
ticking in rhythm with the sun’s slow descent, 
each shadow we cast a map of what we’ll leave behind
a name etched in fog, a song half-remembered. 

Some days, I trace the cracks in my hands, 
wonder if they spell the same story as the stars, 
if our bones are just stardust with a rental agreement. 
The mirror whispers, You’re here, but not for long, 
and I ask, Then why does the heartbeat feel so infinite? 

Love, too, is a ghost in this how we clasp 
a person’s wrist, believing we can halt the hourglass. 
But their fingers slip through ours, fine as smoke, 
leaving only the warmth of a memory on the skin. 
We build monuments out of glances, out of I miss yous, 
yet the wind erodes them faster than we speak. 

Still, I’d argue the beauty isn’t in the lasting, 
but the trying how we bloom through the ache 
of knowing the petals will fall. How we laugh, 
how we grieve, how we plant gardens in the sand 
of our own deserts. How we become both the artist 
and the ash, the hymn and the silence after the last note. 

So let the grave be a door, not a cage. 
We’ll vanish, yes but for a moment, we glowed. 
And in that glow, we taught the world how to hold 
a star in its palm, how to love what cannot stay. 
The end is written. But the ink? It shimmers. 
And that’s enough to make us immortal, for a while.

In the Quiet Embrace of Solitude
When the world folds its wings and retreats into hush, 
I find You in the hollow where silence is stitched, 
A chamber of echoes that hums with my breath
The only witness to the stars I cannot name. 

Here, shadows wear robes of velvet and sigh, 
Their whispers threading through the cracks of the night, 
Each moment a mirror where my pulse is the clock, 
And solitude becomes both the thief and the balm. 

The moon etches its questions into the floor, 
Unanswered, unasked, yet I carve my prayers 
In the marrow of this empty, aching space
A lighthouse built from the dust of my bones. 

No crowd to scatter the weight of my name, 
Just the slow, sacred burn of a single flame: 
A flicker that knows what it means to be seen 
When even the wind forgets how to speak.

Fractured Hymns 

Stained glass saints in their fractured light 
preach to dust. The pews hum a low, 
unblinking hymn. I count cracks 
in the ceiling, each one a crevice 
for doubt to nest. 

A woman kneels, her prayer a thread 
tangled in the altar’s shadow. 
Behind her, a child asks why 
the statue’s hands are chipped
“Faith is the cracks,” she says, 
and the words hang like a doorknob 
no one turns. 

At the back, a man adjusts his tie, 
a knot too tight for mercy. 
The organ grinds its gears. 
Somewhere, a sparrow taps 
against the window, 
mistaking glass for sky.

The Last Light of the Hollow Tree 
Beneath the oak where leaves decay 
We once carved names, now ghosts in gray 
The wind, a clock, ticks through the years 
Unspooling threads our hands can’t weave 

The hollow holds what rain won’t drink 
Whispers of laughter the bark has sunk 
A nest of shadows, cold and deep 
Where even sorrow forgets to weep 

I trace the knots where hands slipped free 
A rope of dusk, too frayed to climb 
The stars, like ash, drift down in flight 
Too brittle to ignite, too vast to hold tight 

The moon, a coin, drops in the well 
No echo answers when I yell 
The tree still stands, though split in two 
Its roots remember what the earth reclaims from you 

I press my ear to time’s slow breath 
But only silence takes my breath.

The Summit 

He climbed the mountain alone. 
His boots crunched through frost. 
The air thinned, each breath a blade. 
At the peak, the world unfolded
a map of rivers, forests, and the sky’s 
blue wound. For a moment, he forgot 
his name, forgot the ache in his legs. 
The wind spoke in a language 
older than bone. He listened, 
a stone in his chest, heavy 
with the weight of being alive. 
He knew this view, this fire in his lungs, 
would fade. Already, the sky 
was stitching its seams shut, 
and the mountains wore 
their silence like a shroud.

The Language of Joy 
Joy is the laughter that spills like sunlight, 
A sudden warmth that melts the frost of doubt, 
It lives in the way your eyes light up when you’re caught in a moment, 
A smile that blooms without needing to be asked to. 

It’s the rhythm of feet tapping to a forgotten tune, 
The way the wind laughs when it dances through the trees, 
The color of a sky brushed with the hues of twilight, 
And the quiet pride when you see someone else shine. 

Joy doesn’t need grand stages to speak
It whispers in the clink of coffee mugs shared between friends, 
In the crunch of autumn leaves under your feet, 
In the way a hug can say more than a thousand words. 

It’s the stubborn spark that stays even when storms try to fade it, 
A firefly’s flicker in the dark, a heartbeat after rain, 
A hand finding another in the chaos of a crowded street, 
And the courage to say, “This is enough.” 

So let it be the melody in your breath, 
The reason you pause to watch a child’s first step, 
The secret you keep in your pocket when the world feels heavy
Joy is not a lightning strike, but a lantern you hold. 

This is why I reach for the small, the fleeting, the true, 
Why I tell you: the best things in life are the ones that make you feel alive. 
If you want to understand joy, let it be the language you live by
Every day, a new verse in the song of being here.

Unbroken Threads 

They told me to quit when the road turned to mud, 
But I kept on walking, one step at a time. 
Each footfall a battle against the rain, 
My shoes sinking deeper with every grumble of thunder. 
I whispered to myself, “This is not the end,” 
Even when my legs burned like firewalking through ash. 

The weight on my back? Memories. 
Moments I couldn’t outrun
A job that chewed up my hours, 
A heart that leaked trust like a cracked faucet. 
Still, I folded my pride into a paper airplane 
And let it dive toward the horizon. 

Some days, the sky split open with laughter, 
Mocking my stubbornness. 
I tripped over roots, cursed the ground, 
Then dug my palms into the dirt and stood. 
Scars are just stories with nowhere else to live, 
And mine? They glowed like compasses in the dark. 

I’m no hero just a man who learned 
To stitch his spine with the bones of the storm. 
The road? It’s still muddy. 
But I walk it anyway, 
Because resilience isn’t a roar. 
It’s the breath after the scream. 
The seed that cracks the concrete, 
Not because the earth asked it to, 
But because the seed knew: 
Light is worth the ache of breaking.

Embers in the Dawn 

In the belly of the earth, a seed holds its breath, 
A quiet rebellion against the endless night. 
It dreams of sunrises it has yet to see, 
And splits the dark with a stubborn green light. 

The winds may howl, the storms may bend its spine, 
Yet roots dig deeper where the nourishment runs. 
It wears the scars of every bitter blight 
As evidence that life can still begin. 

One day, the shadows lean to peer within, 
And find a flower where a seed once wept. 
Its petals whisper to the trembling and the thin: 
“The dawn is not a myth, but a debt we keep.” 

We carry such embers in our hollowed chests, 
Not guaranteed to blaze, but refusing to drown. 
They flicker through the cracks of our fractured rests, 
And map a sky where constellations frown. 

So when the night insists it will never cease, 
Recall the seed that broke its earthen tomb. 
The world is stitched with countless acts of grace
A silent chorus humming: “You are home.”

October's Whisper 

October’s chill has come to stay, 
Leaves like letters, swept away. 
An empty bench, its wood worn thin, 
Holds echoes of a name within. 

The wind it hums, a mournful tune, 
Through branches stripped of summer’s bloom. 
A single coat, forgotten there, 
Its pockets cold, no one’s home. 

The sky, a gray, unblinking eye, 
Watches the world with listless sigh. 
Footprints dissolve in morning’s mist, 
Memories lost, no trace to miss.

The Flame That Cannot Sleep 

It stirs in shadows, never still, 
A flame that cannot sleep. 
It licks the edges of the night, 
A thirst that never stops. 

You try to cage it, bit by bit, 
But smoke escapes through every crack. 
It dies in frost, then starts again, 
A ghost that haunts the coldest track. 

For every wish it lights, it steals
Some deeper hunger left unmet. 
The more you chase, the more you feel 
The vastness of the need within. 

So let it burn. Let it consume. 
The dawn will come, as dawns all do. 
It’ll whisper, “All you had to do 
Was let the dark and light make room.”

Burden 
I carry your absence in a satchel 
of skin, each step a stone 
slipping through the seams. 
Evening hums a hymn of wasps, 
stings unresolved in my throat. 

The lamp’s glow shrinks, a pupil 
dilating into night. I trace the map 
of your name on the window
fog, then frost. Outside, the road 
unspools like a length of cord, 
its knots all memories we can’t 
tie down. 

Morning arrives as a thief, 
stealing the footprints you left 
in the porch’s shadow. I press 
my ear to the floorboards, 
expecting the echo of your feet, 
but the house has learned your silence, 
has built its walls around the hollow. 

Sorrow, this slow erosion
a river carving its bed 
into the marrow of my ribs.

We Are Not Ghosts 

We dug up the garden, still heavy 
with last year’s snow. Nothing had sprouted 
but the shape of us: two shadows 
until the first green claw of a shoot 
split the husk of what we couldn’t bury. 

We learned to water the ground 
with the salt of forgotten names. 
The roots grew restless, tangled, 
and then not. You were a seed 
I kept swallowing, thinking it would kill me. 

You turned my throat green. 
Bloomed in the ache where I had no hands. 
Now the garden knows our new names
its breath, a map of all we unlearned. 
The soil has never felt more like skin.

The Shape of Absence 
Your chair holds the ghost of your shape, 
a concave hill of nowhere, 
while the clock’s hands 
keep falling 
into the same well. 

I measure time now 
in the rust of untouched teacups, 
in the way the cat avoids the empty food bowl
a small rebellion of hunger. 

Winter learns to mimic your name, 
draping itself in the gray of your last coat. 
The heater hums your absence 
in a language of cold. 

Letters gather dust on the desk, 
their alphabets unraveling 
like a child’s attempt to tie a shoe. 
I write you in the margins, 
but the ink bleeds into never. 

Grief is the only holiday we can’t skip
no pass, no refund
just a ticket punched 
with the date you left, 
and me, 
a traveler stranded 
in a station without a platform.

Green Thread in the Sidewalk 

A sprout in the sidewalk’s grip
where the concrete has split, 
a green thread of defiance. 

City breath – 
salt, diesel, 
and the hum of a thousand 
forgotten engines. 

It bends but does not break, 
its leaves open like small hands 
cupping the air. 

Each morning, a new angle 
of light. The stem thickens. 
A root, perhaps, 
has found the moisture 
in a long-dead pipe. 

You pass by, 
shoe soles scuffing its crown, 
never noticing the risk: 
how it holds itself 
to the upward idea, 
the belief that above, 
the sky is always possible. 

Hope is not the anthem 
of the untouched, 
but a green thread, 
stitching the wound 
where the world has cracked.

Tracing the constellations of dusk
I once chased fireflies, thinking them fallen stars, 
Their flicker a language I longed to decode
The night stretched its arms, a velvet labyrinth, 
Each shadow humming with unsung hymns of the cosmos, 

My footsteps dissolved into the wind’s whisper
A compass needle trembling toward the unknown
The moon, a silent sage, etched paths on the water, 
And I, a vessel of questions, drank deeply of its glow, 

Until dawn cracked the sky with a blush of answers, 
And wonder became the thread stitching my breath to the infinite.

Eternal Whispers Beneath the Stars 
Stars, the keepers of ancient sighs, 
You trace constellations on my skin
A map of longing only moonlight reads, 

A river of time cannot erase 
The moment our shadows first collided, 
Leaving etchings on the soul’s raw marble. 

If I am but a flickering flame, 
You are the breath that bends my flame 
Toward your direction, wild and unnamed, 

For even when our lips part
A chasm hums, a symphony of dust and dawn, 
Two souls, one endless rhyme.

The Symphony of Laughter 
There is a melody in the sunrise, 
Where golden light dances on the dew, 
Laughter spills like a river, 
Through fields of blooming morning glories, 
And carries the warmth of a thousand smiles. 

There is a rhythm in the raindrops, 
As they tap on the windows of the soul, 
Children’s feet tracing constellations 
On the floorboards of a twilight hour, 
Each step a note in life’s refrain. 

Joy is the echo in the heart’s cathedral
A spark from the fiddle of the wind, 
A flame in the lantern of a shared glance, 
The sun’s secret whispered to the grapes, 
Turning their clusters to liquid song. 

And when the stars hum their lullabies, 
The world holds its breath to listen, 
For happiness is not a season, 
But the bloom that roots itself 
In the soil of every fleeting, luminous moment.

Love in the Storm 
Can love be a path we walk with weathered feet, 
Where every step is a lesson learned in silence and heat? 
Do you bear the weight when the shadows grow long, 
Or find strength in the cracks where the light starts to thrum? 

We’ve sailed through tempests where the waves nearly broke, 
Held onto each other like the last breath we spoke. 
Yet here we stand, a mosaic of scars, 
Pieced together by the hands of time and stars. 

No words could mend what the silence had torn, 
But in the gaps between, we carved a new dawn. 
Love isn’t the absence of storms, but the choice to stay
A quiet rebellion in the face of the fray. 

Do you still hold me when the chaos feels right? 
When the fire in my bones burns out of sight? 
Will you cradle the tremble in my trembling hands, 
And call it sacred, not a flaw to understand? 

Love is the ache in the climb, the summit unseen, 
A seed growing roots in the same unseen dream. 
So let the world see us as we are
Not perfect, but whole, with open hearts. 

For love is the whisper that outlives the scream, 
A dance of two souls in the same dream.

Whispers of the Wild Heart 
The mountain breathes its shadow a hymn, 
A symphony of pines hums where the stars dare not tread. 
Love, a nomad, traces the frost on dawn’s cheek, 
While rivers carve confessions into the bones of stone. 

You ask how the soul wears the sky like a cloak, 
When every heartbeat echoes the moon’s ancient ache. 
In the thicket, the wind’s fingers unravel time, 
And the rose, though brief, dares to outshout the storm. 

We are made of twilight’s unspoken verse, 
Our hands etched with maps of forgotten constellations. 
To love is to kneel at the altar of impermanence, 
To cup the flame in your palm before it becomes smoke. 

They say the heart is a compass, not a cage, 
Its wildness unbound by the logic of clocks. 
So let the tempests gather
In the eye of chaos, we’ll build temples of light. 

For the poet’s truth lies in the wound and the wound’s bloom, 
Where the earth’s pulse and our own beat aligns
A fleeting, infinite dance, 
Only the Romantic knows how to lose. 

Muhammad Asad

The Weight of Quiet Days 

It settles like a shadow without a name
a taste of rust in the air, 
feet in wet clay. 
The sky forgets to weep, 
but the willows know. 
Their branches braid sorrow 
into knots no hand can untie. 

You carry it like a stone 
in the pocket of your ribs, 
its edges sharp against your bones, 
a clock that ticks too slow, 
its hands drowned in honey. 
Even the sun wears a veil, 
a half-light that hums 
almost enough. 

Nights stretch like old bandages, 
stained and thin. 
You count the cracks in walls 
where silence blooms
each one a mouth 
whispering stay. 

But the dawn comes 
with a blade of gold, 
and the world, 
though heavy-lidded, 
still opens.

Holding the fading breath in a petal's embrace
The bloom bows to the dust of time, 
Its final sigh a silver thread, 

Weaving the shadow’s kiss into the loom, 
A dance of dusk where light once tread. 

The soul, a moth, taps at the lantern’s glass, 
Whispers of dawn trapped in twilight’s throat
Each crumpled leaf, a requiem unsung, 
Yet roots hum hymns that rivers wrote. 

The wind steals the clock’s forgotten chime, 
And all that’s left is this: 

A petal cradles the void it bore, 
A breath both end and endlessness.

The Space Between Heartbeats 
I found joy in a child’s untied shoelaces, 
how they flapped like wings each time she ran, 
her giggles stitching the sky with string, 
each note a bead of sunlight strung. 

The wind joined her, twirling the petals 
of the wildflowers into a crown, 
and the trees bent close to hear 
the stories only laughter could translate. 

I knelt to tie my own steps to hers, 
but the knots unraveled into song
a melody the earth hummed back, 
rich and warm as a hearth’s last ember. 

Now I know joy is not a thing you keep, 
but a language spoken in the space 
between two heartbeats, breathless, 
where the world forgets to name its weight.

The Patient Teacher 

Beneath the frost where silence clings, 
A sapling dreams in winter’s grip, 
Its roots like veins through frozen strings, 
It cradles secrets yet to tip. 

Spring’s breath unfurls in tender greens, 
A crown of hope against the sky, 
But summer’s heat with trials teems, 
And storms that test both branch and bone. 

Autumn arrives with amber fire, 
Leaves fall like tears in golden streams, 
Yet deep within, the sap still tires, 
Prepared for ice and winter’s gleam. 

So life renews in endless spin, 
A dance of death and birth’s refrain, 
The earth remembers where to begin
A patient teacher, season’s chain.

Faded Ink 

The envelope crumbles in my hand, 
its wax a brittle moon. I unfold 
a world of smudged sepia your loops 
and flourishes, once a forest of letters, 
now a braille I trace with closed eyes. 

Your name, a ghost, lingers in each crease. 
The paper exhales the cedar of your desk, 
the ink a whisper of inkwell and impulse, 
how your pen paused here?

I press my cheek to the page, hear 
your voice in the grain, a syllable 
of laughter tangled with the scent 
of rain on your typewriter keys. 

Time shears the corners, but not 
the pulse beneath: a heartbeat 
in the margin, a date October
when the maple leaves blazed like a thousand 
small remembrances. 

The letter crumbles further. I hold it 
as if it might dissolve into a storm 
of wasp-winter, a season we named 
our own. What remains is the weight 
of absence, the ache of a sentence 
unfinished, still warm.

The Cartography of Us 

We trace the maps on each other’s skin
your thumbs charting unspoken archipelagos, 
my breath a compass where your pulse quickens. 
We name constellations in the freckles scattered 
across your collarbone, invent dialects for the ache 
between your ribs when I whisper home. 

Midnight conversations fray into static, 
words dissolving like sugar in too-hot tea. 
You speak in riddles; I answer in half-erased 
sketches of what might bloom if we dared to dig 
beneath the frost of our good manners. 

Love is the tremor in your hand as you light a match 
to see if the shadows will dance. 
It’s the way your laughter cracks the ice 
on my quietest fears. 
We build a hearth from the kindling of near-misses, 
each spark a memory: 
your lips brushing my jawline at the airport, 
the way your hair smelled after the storm, 
the silence that hummed sweeter than any song 
when we learned to swim in the same tide. 

But sometimes, love is the fog that swallows whole
your back turned to the shore, 
my hands full of nets that won’t hold the moon. 
Still, we measure the distance between us 
in the language of almosts, 
in the weight of a shared glance 
that outlives the moment. 

You ask if it’s enough to be almost found. 
I say: let’s redraw the borders. 
Let’s be a country of maybes, 
a topography of second chances. 
Let’s lose ourselves in the blank spaces, 
where the mapmaker gave up and the stars 
still have names we haven’t learned to say.

The Clock That Never Sleeps 

I count the hours with a steady hand
Sun and moon take turns to stand 
But I remain, a silent guard, 
In the heart of the town, so unswayed. 

Children chase the wind, then fade; 
Lovers quarrel, then depart. 
Each one thinks their tale grand, 
But my hands spin, unafraid. 

I’ve known the frost on winter’s breath, 
The kiss of spring’s green dare, 
The rustle of autumn’s last sigh
All fleeting as a moth’s brief air. 

A hundred faces peer at me, 
Each ticking second they crave. 
They swear they’ll chase some phantom light, 
Yet dread the hour it’s given. 

I’m not eternity, they say. 
Just gears, they mutter, trapped in a loop. 
But what of their bones, their wars, 
Their kingdoms that crumble? 

The sun will forget to rise one day, 
And I’ll still tick, a ghost in the dark
A witness to the great unwinding, 
Where even time cracks its knuckles 
And wonders what it’s written.

January Calendar 

The calendar turns its cold back 
on last year’s notes ink smudged where 
I spilled tea on regret. 
Today, I plant the blank pages 
with seeds: a crocus here, a tulip there, 
each name a hope, each root a promise. 
The frost is still thick, but the soil 
has pockets of warmth
a language of thaw. 
I, who once forgot how to dig, 
learn the rhythm of a spade, 
the patience of a bulb.

Echoes of the Heart's First Dawn 
In the garden where time dissolves, 
a single bird sings its song a thread of light 
that stitches the sky to your eyelids. 
Your breath, a jasmine’s whisper, soft and rare, 
fans the embers of my throat into flame. 

We are the fire that time cannot unmake, 
two shadows clasped in the amber of dusk, 
your fingers tracing the map of my spine 
like rivers carving a wilderness of want. 
The moon, a thief, steals our shadow to keep. 

Here, where the earth hums secrets to the roots, 
your lips are the storm I never outgrew
a tempest of yes, a tide that knows 
no harbor but my hunger. The stars lean close 
to hear our name, still new, still unspooled.

Whispers of the Forgotten Season 
The last leaves cling to their branches, trembling as if they hear the clock of time ticking beneath their fragile skin. 
I walk through the hollowed park, where the wind carries away the names of those who once laughed here
their echoes now buried under the frost of forgotten afternoons. 
The sky is a bruise of dusk, and my footsteps dissolve into the silence, each one a question without a reply. 

The shadows stretch like old regrets, pooling at my ankles, refusing to let me walk unburdened. 
I remember the warmth of a sun that no longer touches this place, 
how it once painted the world in hues of gold, now reduced to a ghost in the glass of my memory. 
Even the trees wear their sorrow openly bark cracked, limbs outstretched as if pleading for a winter that will never thaw them. 

I find a bench where the numbers of our names have been worn smooth by the rain. 
Time, with its rusted gears, refuses to turn. 
I press my ear to the earth, hoping to hear the pulse of something alive, 
but only the sighs of roots, ancient and patient, respond. 
They speak in riddles of decay and rebirth, yet I cannot decipher their code. 

The stars above blink like tired eyes, and I wonder if they, too, forget to shine for some hearts. 
Melancholy is a tenant that never leaves, even as spring promises to return. 
I am a curator of lost symphonies, their notes scattered like ash on the wind. 
The world moves on, but here, in this hushed cathedral of autumn, I am still learning how to mourn the light.

Celestial Pause 
the stars hum low, their ancient hymn 
seeping through the cracks of night, 
while the earth holds its breath
a paused note in the symphony of infinite. 

a child asks why the sky forgets its name 
each time it rains, why light bends 
to touch the ocean’s glassy tongue. 
her question hangs, unspooled 
like thread into the void. 

somewhere, a wave forgets to break. 
somewhere, a tree roots itself in the wind. 
i think of how wonder arrives uninvited
a thief in the hour before dawn, 
stealing the clock’s hands, leaving only 
the weight of now, the ache of almost. 

the moon, a pale coin, balances 
on the horizon’s edge. 
is this the moment the universe 
chooses to begin? or end? 
or just this
a single, borrowed heartbeat 
where the dark feels like a cradle, 
and the dark feels like a blade. 

we name the constellations 
to feel less alone. 
yet the silence between them 
sings louder than any story. 
i close my eyes. 
for a while, the chasm is not a chasm. 
only a hush, a held breath, 
a yes.

The Telescope's Whisper 
The child counts stars 
Like they’re coins in a jar, 
While the cosmos hums a tune 
Only the broken can parse. 

The telescope, a metal throat, 
Swallows light from eons past, 
Spitting out questions we can’t ask 
In a language we’re too young to translate fast. 

Galaxies fold like origami 
In the pockets of silence, 
And every "why" we manage to phrase 
Dissolves like sugar in a cosmic brine. 

We are the comma in the universe’s sentence, 
A pause between "is" and "will be," 
Wondering if the stars are sparks 
Of distant fires or someone else’s "me." 

Does the moon remember tides? 
Do rocks dream in slow motion? 
The night stretches its analog arms
We are small, but the wonder is not a loan.

The Unfolding 

Beneath the frost where roots lie still 
A whisper stirs the frozen loam. 
The earth, a patient on the verge 
Of waking, dreams in green. 

A seed cracks open in the dark 
Its yolk of light unspooled. 
The sapling, bold, reaches for skies 
It never once has known. 

The phoenix, ash, becomes the cloud 
That weeps its sooty hymn. 
From ruin’s heap, a garden climbs 
With fingers made of vines. 

I, too, have died in winter’s grip 
And felt the thaw within. 
Each scar a map of where I burned 
Now cradles new begin. 

The river, after drought, returns 
To carve its path anew. 
So let the old me drown in floods 
And rise as something true.

Vines at Dusk 
Vines eat the fence where I left the spade. 
You always said they were too aggressive. 
I liked their hunger. 

We’re both decomposing by the shed
you of habit, me of neglect. 
Time’s a poor gardener. 
It only knows how to bury. 

The roses, once thornless, now twist 
their petals into fists. 
We pruned too much. 
Or maybe not enough. 

There’s no such thing as control 
only what the roots remember.

Solitude is the Clock in the Empty Room
Solitude is the clock in the empty room, ticking a song without a listener
Each second a note in the melody of time’s unyielding march, 

Solitude is the leaf that falls in autumn, unheard by any ear
Drifting down to a bed of its kin, in a chorus of quiet descent, 

Solitude is the fisherman’s boat at dawn, alone on the misty lake
His oar stirring the water’s face, as the sun paints the horizon in gold, 

In solitude, the mind becomes a boundless desert, where thoughts wander like nomads
Seeking an oasis in the distance, yet finding peace in the endless sands. 

Solitude is the echo in the cave, where the voice meets its shadow
A dialogue without words, between the self and the silence.

Shattered Glass 
I found the key beneath the mat, 
a rusted thing, half-buried in the dirt, 
it turned with a groan, a sound like a sigh, 
into the room where you kept your silence. 

The door swung open to a garden 
of wilted flowers, each petal a whispered lie, 
their stems snapped where your words had grown 
thick as a thorned hedge, sharp and tight. 

I walked through the debris of our trust
shards of glass where the mirror once hung, 
each fragment reflecting a different face, 
none of them mine, none of them yours. 

You stood at the edge of the garden, 
a stranger with my name on your lips, 
watering the roots of your deceit 
with the tears I once cried for you.

Tiny architects of a grief too vast 
To fit inside the body that bore it. 

Perhaps sorrow is not a thing to be cured 
But a shape the world carves into itself 
A hollow where the light pools, 
And the thistle learns to bend 
Until it forgets it ever wished to stand.

Silent Orbits 

She sits in a room where the walls are glass, 
but the silence is concrete
a vault for all the voices 
she’s left outside. 
Tea grows cold in her hands, 
steam curling like questions 
into nowhere. 

The clock eats minutes, one by one. 
She counts the bones of each second, 
traces their ridges with her thumb. 
Outside, birds stitch the sky with song, 
but they do not look down. 
They do not know 
how to address her shadow. 

At night, she becomes a lighthouse 
in a harbor of sleeping ships. 
Her beam cuts through the dark, 
a single, stubborn thread 
of salt and warmth. 
The waves reply in morse
how long can a signal sustain itself? 

She learns the texture of her breath, 
the weight of a single heartbeat. 
Some days, she is a tree 
with roots gnawing at stone. 
Others, a moth 
circling the furnace of a memory. 

The world moves in ellipses
a house with only her footprints, 
and the echo that doesn’t echo.

The Weight of Wings 
A moth tunnels through the plaster of the attic
its wings, still damp from the crawl, 
leave no dust. 

You find it at dawn, 
a tremor in the ceiling, 
listening to the hollow where 
your mother’s violin once hung. 

It does not ask 
why the house forgets its keys, 
why the floorboards buckle 
like old promises. 

You hold your breath 
as it works, 
its body a slow fuse 
lighting the dark with muscle and marrow. 

When it emerges, 
the wings are maps of what the fire missed: 
veins of unburned silk, 
a geography of scars 
that hums with the weight of unasked questions. 

You let it rest on your palm, 
this fragile alchemy
how it balances the pull of flame 
against the gravity of becoming. 

It does not stay. 
It never does. 
But the hole in the plaster 
is now a window, 
and the wind, 
for the first time in years, 
knows your name.

When Joy Sneaks In 

A child laughs on the sidewalk, 
I stop to watch, forgetting my own name. 
Her joy spills over like confetti, 
Uninvited, but I don’t mind the flame. 

I’ve been carrying weights all morning
Bills, deadlines, a friend’s lost key
Yet here she is, all light and motion, 
Her wheels screeching, her hair a spree. 

The world’s a burden most days, they say, 
But here’s a truth no one will spell: 
Joy needs no grandeur, no parade
It lives in a tricycle’s squeal, a bird’s small yell. 

I used to think joy was a firework
Boom! Then silence. But no, it’s the spark 
That flickers when you least expect it, 
A stranger’s grin, a dog’s wet park. 

So let the world spin its old lament, 
I’ll take my joy where I can find
In a child’s laugh, in the sun’s ascent, 
In how small things can leave us blind.

The Weight of Absence 

Her room is a museum of silence, 
each object a relic of what’s lost
a clock with stopped hands, 
a chair still warm from a ghost’s brief visit, 
a letter sealed in a jar of unspoken words. 

Sorrow arrives as a guest who refuses to leave, 
wearing her laughter like a borrowed coat, 
whispering in the hollows of her ribs, 
a tenant in the walls, chewing at the beams. 

She tries to pack it
stuffs the ache into a suitcase, 
but it spills out in black feathers, 
each one a name she can’t remember, 
each one a story she can’t finish. 

Outside, the sky weeps in gray, 
a procession of clouds marching over the hills, 
carrying their own burdens, 
their own unlightened loads. 

She walks the shore where the sea forgets 
and the tide erases footprints, 
but the sand holds her sorrow deeper, 
carving trenches where her tears fall. 

In the end, she learns, 
it’s not a thing to be carried, 
but a thing to be measured
how much of the dark can she hold 
before the light cracks her open? 

And so she becomes the container, 
the vessel, the quiet keeper, 
of all that has no voice, 
carrying the weight of absence 
like a second skin, 
like a shadow that knows her name.

The Palette of Time 

I found your face in the attic of my mind
a Polaroid curled at the edges, 
its sepia tones whispering summer, 
the way your hair caught sunlight like a net 
of golden threads. You were a melody 
I hadn’t learned to name yet, 
a color without a word in any dictionary. 

But beauty isn’t a statue, still and safe. 
It’s the bruise that blooms after a fall, 
the ache of a rose clinging to its petals 
when winter insists on borrowing them. 
You once laughed at the moon, 
said it was just a ghost of a heart, 
and I believed you. I believed everything 
was a metaphor if we stared long enough. 

Then the film grew static. 
You became a half-remembered dream, 
a brushstroke dissolved in rain. 
I traced the phantom of your cheekbones 
in my sleep, asked the stars if they missed you, 
if they still burned for you. 
They only answered in silence, 
or maybe in a language I’d forgotten. 

Now I keep your memory in a jar
not the face, but the weight of you: 
the way your voice cracked when you lied, 
how your hands trembled when you swore 
you’d stay. Beauty, I’ve learned, 
isn’t a thing you hold. 
It’s the hollow you carve out to keep it in, 
the ritual of lighting candles for a ghost, 
the courage to let the flame flicker. 

I still see you in the cracks of mirrors, 
in the way morning gilds the windows. 
You were never just skin and bone, 
were you? You were a hymn, 
a fractured hymn, 
and I’m still singing the fragments 
to the wind. 

Dear Muse, if beauty is eternal, 
I’ve kept you there 
not in the photograph, 
but in the ache of its absence.

Echoes in the Cosmic Sand 
What if time was just a borrowed breath, 
A flicker between two endless darks, 
And we were meant to meet in the cracks, 
Where seconds dissolve like sugar in the storm
Would you remember the sound of my voice, 
Or would my name fade softer than a ghost’s last sigh? 

I’ve been tracing constellations in your shadow, 
Mapping our lost years on the back of my hand, 
Each line a prayer, each scar a hymn, 
Singing how love outlives the clock’s cruel tongue. 
Even if the sun dies and swallows the moon, 
I’ll be the ache in your chest when you whisper forever. 

Do you feel it too? 
That pull of the tide in our veins, 
As if the universe is just a bridge 
Between hearts too stubborn to let go? 
We’re stardust with nowhere else to wander, 
So I’ll cling to your gravity, 
Even if eternity is just us falling, 
Forever missing the ground.

The Day the Clocks Bloomed 

At the crack of dawn, the clocks exhaled petals, 
a calendar uncreased itself into spring. 
I found a turtle in my toaster, nesting 
in the crumb of yesterday’s burnt bread. 

The kettle whistled a tune it once forgot, 
while the doorknob, long rusted, bloomed a vine. 
A coffee cup, chipped and cracked, spat back 
the seeds it swallowed in winter’s name. 

The mirror showed a face I’d never known
cheeks dusted with starlight, eyes cradling 
a storm of forgotten hours. Even my shadow 
peeled off, a snake’s shed skin, to be 
reborn as a ladder leaning against dusk. 

Rebirth, they say, isn’t a spark but a slow 
unfurling. The fridge hums a new hymn, 
the phone screen cracks and heals in a day
all things, given time, learn how to bloom.

The Quiet Architect 
Find me the room 
Where silence is measured 
In the breadth of shadows 
And walls wear their emptiness 
Like a second skin. 

Find me the tree 
That stands at the border 
Of forgotten fields 
Its branches scribbling 
Secrets on the wind. 

Find me the clock 
That counts with a finger 
Each second a tomb 
Its ticking a language 
Only stillness understands. 

Find me the lake 
That holds the sky’s gaze 
But forgets to reply 
Its surface a ledger 
Of unanswered questions. 

Find me the echo 
That lingers after speech 
A ghost of connection 
Hunting for company 
In the folds of air. 

Find me the hour 
Where solitude and company 
Wear the same face 
And the heart, unaccustomed 
To its own company, stumbles. 

Find me the shadow 
That walks behind all days 
A silent companion 
Whispers of absence 
And the weight of presence. 

Find me the solitude 
That is not a prison 
Nor a gilded cage 
But the quiet architect 
Of what we dare to name.

Flicker in the Fuse Box 
A moth circles the bulb above the sink 
where limes rot into soft, sour marbles
their green bleeds into a stain on the counter, 
a spill of days forgotten. 

The walls here hum with wires, 
a tangle of black veins beneath a false panel, 
and sometimes, when the wind forgets to knock, 
you can hear the faint click of a switch 
inside the silence. 

Beauty is the dust that coats the edges 
of broken things: 
the way a crack in the tile mirrors 
the curl of a burnt-out filament, 
how the moth keeps turning, 
its wings catching the light 
not as a prize, but as a mistake
a sun it once knew 
in some other room, 
some other body, 
still warm.

The Unfolding of New Skin 

She sheds her old skin 
in the quiet hour before dawn, 
when the air is still a question 
and the world holds its breath. 

The new skin is fragile, 
a parchment of translucent gold, 
draping over bones 
like light through a shattered pane. 

There is pain in the in-between
a tautness like stretched silk, 
a body forgetting how to hold itself 
without the armor of before. 

But the cells remember: 
how to split, how to climb, 
how to stitch themselves into 
a language of become. 

Now, she moves through the world 
a creature of second mornings, 
her shadow no longer a cage, 
but a cradle for what’s next.

Clothesline Whispers 

The clothesline hangs lower than it should, 
a limp string of surrender between two poles. 
It holds a child’s shirt, a man’s towel
both faded, their edges unraveling 
into the kind of stillness that forgets 
how to flutter even when the wind arrives. 

Detergent ghosts linger in the fabric, 
a scent now diluted by sun and seasons. 
Each thread hums a fainter tune than the last, 
as if the line once sang with a chorus of socks 
and sheets, now reduced to this: two shadows 
clinging to what was once a dance. 

I count the hooks where laughter used to hang, 
their empty curves spelling out a language 
of absences. The shirt collars droop, 
forming question marks in the grammar of the yard. 
Somewhere, a door left ajar. Somewhere, 
a clock lost a minute. Somewhere, 

melancholy stitches itself into the weave
not loud, not grand, but a slow unraveling 
of all the things left to dry in the open.

Whispers of the Lone Hour
Shadows dance in empty rooms, 
A waltz of two, yet I am one
The clock’s breath counts each tear, 
Silence hums a lullaby of rusted gears. 

The moon speaks to the tide, 
But the shore answers only with its sigh. 
If solitude is a door left ajar, 
What locks the key inside my ribs? 

I build kingdoms in the dust of forgotten chairs, 
Where echoes wear gowns of mist. 
Some call it exile; I call it a cathedral
No bells, no prayers, just the hymn of my pulse. 

Roots of the oak do not envy the storm’s rage, 
Nor the moth’s hunger for flame. 
Why then do I measure my depth 
By the absence of footsteps? 

In the theater of night, I am both ghost and audience
A solo act beneath constellations of static. 
To be alone is to hold a lighthouse 
In a harbor unmoored, 
Where every beam finds its own shadow. 

Still, the heart is a compass that does not lie: 
Even in the vastness, 
I am the only map I need.

Hollow Stillness 

Solitude, a patient sculptor, chiseling 
your edges into curves that mirror 
the empty chair. You become 
a dialectic of presence and absence
a moth tasting the dust of its own wings. 

Here, the walls are glass but no one watches; 
even silence has a topology. Time pools 
like spilled mercury, indivisible, 
yet slipping through every joint. 
You are the echo before the scream, 
the shadow that outgrew the flame. 

No need for doors when the self 
is a room that folds inward, 
a well where every stone dropped 
returns as a stranger’s voice. 
The night is not a veil but a host
its stars mere spectators to your orbit. 

You learn to speak in the language of frost, 
how stillness writes its hymns on the skin. 
Alone, you are both altar and desecration, 
a psalm of unlit candles, 
a god who prays to its own ghost.

The Quiet Rebellion of Things 

I found your scarf in the closet today, 
it still smells like lavender and your absence. 
I folded it neatly, as you would have wanted, 
but the silence between the folds was relentless. 

Each stitch a small rebellion against the cold, 
you used to say, while I listened through my teeth. 
Now it lies here, a map of where you walked 
and the spaces where your steps have since withdrew. 

I still make the tea for two, though the cup 
sits forgotten by the clock’s steady ticking. 
Your chair, a hollow I’ve learned to avoid, 
in case the echoes start their quiet weeping. 

The kettle whistles, and I forget to turn it off, 
letting it scream until the water’s gone. 
It’s the only time I’m allowed to be loud, 
a borrowed rage no one else will own. 

Sorrow isn’t the storm you couldn’t stop, 
nor the silence that follows the telephone’s ring. 
It’s the quiet thereafter the slow, patient frost
that turns every memory into something you can’t uncling.

The Hourglass of Shadows 

You are the autumn leaf’s surrender, 
The clockface without hands, 
The candle’s wick bowed low, 
Its light a thief stealing itself to night. 

I am the hourglass of shadows, 
Sand that forgets how to fall, 
A breath held in the ribs of mountains, 
The echo of a laugh the wind erases. 

Your name is the last snowflake of summer, 
Melting in the palm of time’s hunger, 
The unspoken hymn of a dying star, 
A whisper the dark claims before dawn. 

Yet in the hollow where my pulse resides, 
I cradle the dust of what we were
A firefly’s blink in the throat of eternity, 
You, mortality: both the wound and the balm. 

I am the leaf, the flame, the grain of now, 
And you
You are the silence 
that makes us real.

The Unsent Letters 

Drawers swell with folded words, 
each one a ghost of what might’ve been said. 
Ink bleeds through paper, thin and blurred
a silence no storm ever stirred. 

We wrote of summer’s brief warmth, 
of autumn’s too-quick fall; 
of things we thought we’d work out, 
but never gave the chance to crawl. 

Years bloom and wither like untended gardens, 
where letters gather dust and rust. 
The names we wrote in the margins 
are now strangers, blurred by distrust. 

Some truths are meant to stay unspoken, 
some words too sharp to send. 
The drawer, a mausoleum of might-have-beens, 
where all our what-ifs lay, half-bent. 

The weight of all we never said 
settles in the bones like rain. 
Even the postman, once a friend, 
now avoids the street where we both strain.

The Weight of Wings 

A single feather remains 
after the storm’s last sigh. 
You held it like a secret 
between your palms, as if the sky 
had whispered something fragile 
into your hands. 

We were birds once, they said, 
with nests built from thunder 
and eggs cracked by the sun. 
Our wings, those clumsy things, 
could never decide 
if they wanted to rise 
or dissolve into the wind. 

Now the river forgets 
its own name by morning, 
and the trees bend low 
to listen to the wind’s 
unfinished confession. 
Even the stones are learning 
to hum a new tune. 

I’ve loved the way your silence 
bloomed like a wild rose 
in the cracks of the pavement
thorny, insisting, 
never asking for permission. 

But your shadow remains 
in the hollows of my ribs, 
a constant, quiet 
ache that the stars 
refuse to mend. 
Even the moon pauses 
to trace your absence 
in the ink of my veins, 
how we carved our names 
into the bark of the world. 

So let the earth keep 
our unspoken hymns; 
let the sky swallow 
the last of our fire. 
We were never meant 
to be what we became. 
Only echoes, 
still learning to fly.

Horizon's Whisper 
We are drawn to edges
your gaze, a slow eclipse, 
the sky dissolving 
to the color of want. 
Waves, unrelenting, 
carve confessions into the shore, 
each tide a hymn 
of almost, almost. 

The wind holds its breath 
between our unspoken names, 
a taut string 
plucked by dusk’s fingers. 
I am the moth 
you fashioned from smoke and light, 
always circling, 
never consumed. 

What is hunger 
if not the moon’s pull 
on the tide’s endless ache? 
You are the question 
every star refuses to answer
burning, burning, 
but never near enough 
to touch the void.

The Thirst That Maps the Sky 
I have seen the night swallow the sun 
but never as you swallow my name 
like a prayer gone feral. 

Your shadow, a fire 
that burns without smoke, 
etches its code 
into the marrow of my spine. 

The desert in my throat 
grows teeth gnaws 
at the silence between us, 
a language without air. 

Desire is the compass 
that points to no north, 
only the ache 
where the heart forgets 
how to beat. 

And when you move, the air follows, 
a current that pulls me 
toward the edge of the world, 
where the horizon is always ahead, 
and the best was never to come.

When the forest whispers secrets to the wind
Roots etch prayers into the earth's skin, 
While rivers hum hymns of ancient thirst. 

The wind combs through the branches' silver hair, 
Carrying the scent of forgotten years. 

Sunlight fractures into liquid gold, 
Shadows kneel where the petals fold. 

The storm is both the wound and the balm, 
Each drop a star drowned in the calm. 

Moss remembers what the mountains forget, 
Time is a seed that never retires. 

We are the echo of a single breath, 
The earth's pulse beneath our feet.

Ethereal Echoes 

Meet me where the river forgets its name, 
its mouth full of stones and moss, 
each ripple a stuttered hymn. 
We’ll trace the veins of a fallen leaf, 
count the hours until dusk 
unspools its thread of fireflies. 

Your breath is a compass
north is the pine’s trembling resin, 
south, the hollow where owls 
mend their broken silences. 
We are cartographers of the unplanned, 
drawing borders in ant trails, 
erasing them with the same thumb. 

Somewhere between the third star 
and the drone of a power line, 
you cupped a moth in your palm, 
whispered, This is how the world 
still believes in softness. 
I wanted to say: Keep it safe. 
Wear it like a second heartbeat. 

But the night had other verses. 
A fox, luminous as a ghost, 
split the thicket, and we ran
not toward, not away, 
but the blur of feet, the gasp 
of earth beneath our soles. 

At dawn, we built a raft from driftwood 
and the fragments of a lost song. 
The current tugged us onward, 
past the ruins of a mill, its gears 
choked with lichen and regret. 
Even the rust hummed a tune 
we once knew by heart. 

When the fog came, thick as a vow, 
you pressed your ear to the water. 
Listen, you said. The river’s singing 
in a language older than glass. 
I wanted to say: Don’t let it fade. 
This is how we outlast the noise. 

But the sky had other verses. 
Clouds swallowed the sun whole, 
and we were left with the weight 
of unsung ballads, the ache 
of a horizon leaning in, 
always leaning in, 
to hear what the wind 
won’t carry all the way home.

The Meadow's Symphony of Joy 
The golden sun spilled honey over the field
Children’s laughter echoed, light as the breeze, 

Chasing each other, their footprints blooming with every step
Petals of clover adorning their crowns, the air sweet with wild thyme, 

The breeze waltzed with the daisies, twirling them in glee
As the earth hummed a melody older than time, 

A mother’s smile curved like the arc of a rainbow
Her arms open to the sky, cradling the moment, 

We danced in the symphony where joy never sleeps
And the stars blinked in rhythm, adding their light to the dance.

The Weight of Empty Spaces 
The mug cools on the counter, untouched
your favorite, the one with chipped lavender 
paint at the rim. I leave it there, a fossil 
of routine, three days without the sound 
of your voice cracking over coffee grounds. 

The phone lies face-down, its silence a room 
we never moved furniture into. I trace the edge 
of your chair, still warm with the ghost of posture, 
and count each breath like a missed train. 

Outside, the wind peels through the yard 
as if sifting for bones. I wear your coat 
to measure the distance: how sleeves dangle 
past my own, how the lining smells of nothing, 
absence stitched into every thread. 

Night arrives early, dragging its clockless hours. 
I flicker between the lamp’s dimness and shadow, 
a figure in a film reel no one screens anymore. 
Your laugh lives in the walls, but only 
when the pipes are quiet, when the world leans in 
to listen. 

Morning finds me at the edge of the road, 
where we once paused to name the clouds. 
Now the sky forgets to answer. I hold 
the unwritten letter in my pocket, its creases 
already frayed by the weight of your absence
a language composed of all the things 
that no longer fit between us.

The Space Between Heartbeats 
I’ve been counting your footsteps 
as they echo in the hallway
a rhythm I almost recognize, 
but not quite. 

I want to step into the gap 
between your breath and mine, 
to let the silence say what we can’t: 
this thing between us 
that doesn’t have a name. 

If I reach for you now, 
will the distance dissolve 
or just become heavier? 
I’ve practiced both: 
the weight of touch, 
the ache of pulling back. 

Your voice is a thread 
I keep unspooling 
to measure against the dark
how far can I stretch it 
before it snaps? 

I know the answer. 
I’ve seen it in your eyes: 
a door left ajar, 
warmth spilling out 
but no one crossing the threshold. 

Desire is the part of me 
that stays outside the frame, 
tipping my head back 
to watch the light 
pool at your feet, 
never daring to ask 
if it’s enough 
to want you 
like this
like a question 
without a question mark.

Fractured Echoes 
Heartbreak is a shattered glass 
Scattered in the sand 
Each wave a memory I can’t unsee, 
A tide of fragments in the hand. 

The ghost of your laughter, a hollow hymn, 
Silence follows, a shadow I can’t outpace. 
The clock’s thin hands carve wounds in the air, 
A metronome for the ache of your absence. 

Winter taught me how to hold a wound; 
Spring offers no remedy, only a slower frost. 
I’ve counted the cracks in this borrowed room, 
Each one a syllable of your name I can’t drop. 

Your voice was a compass, now it’s a storm 
I sail through the ruins of every maybe. 
The stars blink indifference from their height, 
And I, a beggar, collect their cold currency. 

I’ve learned to stitch time with loose-ended thread, 
To let the scars bloom where the light once lived. 
But the heart is a vault that won’t surrender its keys 
A kingdom of echoes, ruled by what we lost. 

The nights are longer here, though the hours lie 
Like feathers on water, dissolving to dust. 
I’ve drunk from the chalice of every goodbye; 
My throat is a desert, thirsting for the past. 

Yet somewhere, a clock continues to tick 
Not for us, but for the world that moves on. 
And I, a relic of what never will be, 
Carve my grief into a stone no one will own.

THE UNYIELDING BLOOM 
I’ve seen a seed in concrete cracks 
push through the weight of a forgotten world
its leaves a hymn to the unseen light. 

Do you still whisper through the storm, 
hope? 
Or have you drowned in the static of years? 

When night swallows the sun, 
I clutch the residue of your promise
a spark that clings to the palm of the hand, 
warmer than the first touch of dawn. 

Hope is the thread that mends the frayed, 
the scar that fades but never vanishes, 
the child who never gave up asking, 
What if? 

So let the thunder roar and the shadows stretch
somewhere, a root is drinking the dark, 
turning it into a future of bloom. 
Do you still taste the sweetness of maybe? 
Do you still dare to bloom?

Ethereal Vows
Beneath the twilight’s cerulean veil
Their footsteps traced where ancient roots entwined, 

A symphony of leaves whispered secrets through the breeze
The river’s silver tongue told tales of love unreeling, 

The maiden’s laughter, a melody to tame the wild
The stranger’s gaze, a flame to thaw winter’s exile, 

Mountains bowed in silent witness to their breath entwined
A constellation of promises drowned in midnight’s ink, 

Yet storms would crack the sky’s dome like a vengeful crown
They clung to each other two souls, one pulse of defiance, 

When dawn unraveled the shadows’ grip
Their shadows danced on the sun-kissed field, 

A pact sealed not by time, but by the earth’s eternal sigh
Love, the only relic left unshattered in the ruins of fate.

The Clock Without Hands 

We sit where the old clock lost its hands, 
time pooled like water on the floor. 
The fireflies don’t count their twirls
they simply rise, then rise again, 
each flicker a tiny, endless spiral. 

You say, "What if forever is just this?" 
Your breath, a steady tide, brushes my ear. 
The stars above aren’t points, but threads 
weaving the night into a loop, 
and we are both the needle and the knot. 

The oak outside hums in slow circles, 
its rings holding centuries in a single grain. 
We trace the river’s U-turn, our fingers 
dipping into the same current twice
but the water remembers nothing, yet everything. 

When the sky yawns and the last bird forgets its song, 
we’ll fold the dawn like a map without edges, 
kiss the horizon’s unbroken line, 
and begin, again, without beginning.

Topography of Us 

You left the dictionary open 
where we paused page 127, 
the word oblivion underlined 
in that careful, looping hand. 
I trace the margin 
where you wrote remember 
in the shape of a heart, 
its edges soft with use. 

The rain outside is a language 
we’ve learned by ear: 
a rhythm that syncs 
to the clock’s quiet ticking, 
to the way your foot 
finds mine beneath the quilt. 
You call it background noise 
but I’ve memorized the intervals
how the storm always hesitates 
before breaking into syllables. 

There’s a map of us 
in the dog-eared atlas on the floor, 
stamped with thumbprints, 
pins bent into arrows pointing 
nowhere specific. We named 
each crease a season: 
that one, spring thaw
when you wore my sweater 
and I wore your patience. 

Tonight, you hold the teacup 
like a fragile promise, 
steam curling between your fingers. 
I’m mapping how the light settles 
in the hollow of your throat, 
how the silence between us 
is never empty
just a ledger of small geographies, 
all the places we’ve learned 
to spell aloud. 

When you close your eyes, 
I count the topography of your breath
its peaks and valleys, 
the way it carries 
both the weight of us 
and the softness of forgetting.

The Unseen Hourglass 
The hourglass whispers in the language of dust, 
as if each grain is a silent requiem, 
a clockwork caterpillar chewing its own tail 
in the dark. 

A maple tree practices its farewell 
in October, each leaf a falling minute, 
its branches skeletal hymns 
singing to the sky. 

The clock’s hands are knitting needles, 
stitching time into a shroud 
too tight for the chest 
of the living. 

Photographs fade in the dark, 
their subjects already ghosts, 
trapped in a frame where the light 
forgot to linger. 

A candle in a storm forgets its own flame 
while the wind rehearses the word never
a chorus of shadows pooling at the feet 
of the unsure. 

We are all unfinished sonnets
the last line always borrowed, 
a borrowed breath, 
a borrowed end.

The Unseen Path 
I walk through the park at dawn’s first light, 
Feet on the ground, but thoughts in flight, 
Each step a question, each breath a sigh, 
About the world that stretches up to the sky. 

I see the dew upon the grass, 
Each tiny drop a mirror of the past, 
And wonder how the earth can hold 
A thousand stories yet untold. 

A child laughs, chasing a butterfly, 
Their joy a flash in the morning sky. 
What if the wonder is not found in size? 
But in the moment, the heart’s surprise? 

The trees whisper secrets as the wind passes through,

The Last Light 
The room is quiet, except for the clock’s tick

The tea goes cold in the chipped porcelain, 
its steam long gone, like the warmth of your touch. 

I trace the cracks in the windowpane, 
where sunlight once spilled in golden streams. 
Now only dust motes drift through the air, 
and the silence hums in the corners, unseen. 

The last light fades, but the shadows stay, 
pooling in the places you used to fill. 
I leave the lamp off, let the dark take hold
a familiar guest, though it brings no thrill. 

Your voice is a record left on the shelf, 
unplayed, yet echoing in memory’s spin. 
I wind the clock, as if time could be tamed, 
but the hands just creep where they’re meant to go. 

The last light fades, but the shadows stay
they nestle in every photo, every song. 
I count the hours until morning breaks, 
though dawn’s a thief who steals the night along.

a light that doesn’t chase the ache away. 
The clock ticks on, and I stay still

The Unyielding Vine 

There’s a vine in the courtyard 
that climbs through the cracks in the stone. 
They tried to burn it out last winter
now it’s back, green and stubborn,

She sits beneath it, this woman, 
whose husband left with the war 
and never returned. She keeps 
knitting the same scarf, blue as twilight, 
though she’s heard the pattern 
calls for black. Her hands don’t stop, 
even when the yarn runs out. 

The vine hasn’t forgotten 
how to bloom. It learned 
the hard way each year, 
it sheds its dead skin 
and keeps knitting itself back 
into something soft, something 
the wind can’t unmake. 

When the children ask why it grows 
where the wall is thinnest, 
she only says, Because the light 
is thinner there. Because roots 
are just hunger wearing a hat. 

No one tells her to stop 
stitching that scarf. The loops 
of wool are starting to hum. 
You can’t drown a song 
that’s already in your bones.

in the steam.

a reminder that even the sky has a closing hour.
